chapters.title: Chapter 451: Battle For The Crown III
paragraphs: Rodrick wiped the blood from the corner of his mouth, from the coldness in his eyes alone, it was clear that the battle was not going the way he wanted.
"What? You didn’t expect to get beaten like this, Rodrick? Did you think you could suppress me with one hit and end the battle?" Lian noticed it too and mocked him.
"I admit that I underestimated you, but that is not going to change anything, I will be the final winner and ...you still misunderstood one thing about me."
The young Vorhelm raised an eyebrow.
And in response, he gave a short laugh.
"You think all the people I gathered around me are only here so I can have power in the Academy ...you know, all of this is because of my Talent."
Lian’s face became serious, Awakened often hid their Talents, it was not a rule and it was an optional decision, just like him, who had hidden his Talent.
And Rodrick’s Talent was the same, he had never made the information about his Talent public... but it seemed that he had changed his mind.
"My Talent is Sovereign’s Banner... it’s not like it can force someone to become my subordinate. It can’t."
His eyes moved down for a moment, toward the bottom of the mountain, where his people were still fighting.

"Everyone has to choose for themselves to stand under my banner, when they make that choice, they become a part of my territory; they can sense my commands better, the coordination between my people becomes better, and I can also understand the condition of my main forces."
The young Vorhelm said nothing, now some of Rodrick’s behavior had a different meaning.
His obsession with building a faction, gathering powerful students, rewarding loyalty, and indirectly putting pressure on those who stayed outside.
This was not just politics, it was a part of his path to power.
Rodrick fixed his eyes on Lian again.
"You think I am playing for the position of Headmaster." His voice was calm, but there was cold confidence in every word.
"This Academy is only the first place where I build my own territory."
"So I finally understand why you need so many people, you’re not as great alone as you show yourself to be." Lian looked at him for a few seconds and then slowly nodded.
Silence.
"Try it." This time, something flashed in Rodrick’s eyes...killing intent?
"That’s what I’m doing, but I’m curious, why did you tell me about your Talent? And besides, your Talent being S-Rank doesn’t seem that special."
Although no answer came and ...
BOOOOM!
They reached each other again, Rodrick’s fist came from the right and Lian lowered his head.
Suddenly, an elbow came down from above and his armored forearm went up to block it.
Clang!
The attack was pushed aside and the young Vorhelm attacked his stomach with his knee.
Rodrick lowered his palm and caught it.
[ King’s Reprisal. ]
A stream of mana ran through his body and Lian immediately pulled back, he was not going to give Rodrick his own heavy attack for free anymore.
True Sequence activated.
His eyes followed the path of the mana, Crushing Decree was gathering in his fist again but this time he found what he was looking for.
The first impact, then a very short delay, and then the explosion happened, all of this was made possible by the skill in less than one second.
Rodrick moved forward and his fist moved toward Lian’s chest, he raised his left hand and his palm touched the other’s wrist and changed the path of the fist by only a few centimeters.
Clang!
The fist passed beside his body, mana entered the assumed point of impact but the young Vorhelm was no longer there.
[ Ash Step. ]
Fsh!
His body turned into ash right before the explosion.
BOOOOM!
[ Crushing Decree ] exploded behind him and the ash gathered on the other side of Rodrick but this time Lian did not attack directly.
[ Frost Dominion. ]
Crack!
A thick ice wall rose from the ground right behind his enemy, his path of retreat was blocked and Rodrick’s eyes changed.
He appeared in front of him and his palm rose.
Cataclysm Pulse.
"I got you."
BOOOOOOOM!
The explosion hit Rodrick’s chest from a close distance and the ice wall behind him did not let the force of the attack fully escape by moving backward.
His body was trapped between two forces.
Crack!
The entire ice wall behind him broke and he was thrown away together with thousands of pieces of ice, landing nearly twenty meters away.
He had completely fallen to the ground.
The young Vorhelm let out a short breath, his mana was not infinite.
Two Royal Seal Guardians, the battles from the previous stages, and now this bastard, if this continued, it would not take long for his mana to be completely drained.
But fortunately, he still had more than he needed.
[Time Remaining: 05:28.]
Rodrick moved, slowly sitting on one knee and blood had run from the corner of his mouth down to his chin.
For a few seconds, he only looked at him, there was no smile left on either of their faces.
[Elena’s Protective Seal activated.]
[Participant eliminated.]
Rodrick’s eyes moved down for a fraction of a second, Lian also gave a quick look and in the distance, particles of light were rising toward the sky from one of the lower platforms.
Seraphina was still standing, their duel was over and Elena had lost, this result seemed shocking.
But it really was not, Seraphina had a four-star Dual Class along with a Legacy from an ancient civilization that was still helping her improve.
While Elena had a three-star Class and her Talent Rank was B.
The basic difference between them was not something that Level alone could make up for.
Rodrick turned his eyes back to the young Vorhelm.
"Looks like your friends aren’t bad either."
"Why do you think I’m friends with them? Unlike you, I make better choices."
"Choice? All of my subordinates are smart and loyal, and these same subordinates helped me become King, unlike you, who still couldn’t even get your position back in the Vorhelm family."
"Really? All of them? Are you sure about Darren?" Lian laughed.
A muscle beside Rodrick’s eye moved for a moment.
"His barking wasn’t bad." And he made his smile a little deeper.
"You really don’t know when to shut your mouth, Vorhelm."
"I usually know, I just don’t see a reason to." And the young Vorhelm shrugged.
Rodrick stood up from the ground, he looked calm and controlled, but something in his eyes had changed.
He now understood that if the fight continued like this, there was a real chance of losing, he did not like to accept it.
But he was not stupid enough to close his eyes to the truth.
His eyes moved to the timer for a moment.
Then to his forces below the mountain.
"You know what the biggest difference between you and me is? The number of people standing behind me." And then he asked.
This made Lian raise an eyebrow, he did not understand where this idiot wanted to go by saying these things.
Rodrick held the Crown in front of his chest for a moment and closed his eyes, the mana inside his body changed.
It was not like activating a normal skill but something deeper.
Thin golden lines started from his chest and spread across his neck and arms.
At the same time, several members of Rodrick’s faction below the mountain suddenly trembled.
One of them fell to one knee and another was forced to put his hand on the ground, the speed of a third person clearly decreased.
The young Vorhelm narrowed his eyes.
Rodrick opened his eyes, the pressure of his presence had suddenly changed.
Stronger.
Faster.
Heavier.
"You asked me why I told you about my Talent, right? Because I wanted you to understand the difference between me and yourself ... I am a King! And you are just a lone rebellious peasant."
"A lone peasant can never surpass the glory of a true King." It was clear that he believed every word he said.
He really thought he was a King ...no, he thought he was destined to become a King

"And this is where you can understand the difference between a King and a subject like yourself ...the first innate trait of the tree, Tyrant’s Tribute." Rodrick closed his right fist and a wave of pressure spread around him.
"You took their power?" Lian examined him for a few moments, one look was enough for him to understand what was happening.
This bastard had just taken the power of his subordinates.
"I borrowed it."
"That doesn’t make much difference."
"For someone who has no one behind them, maybe, but I am a King, it is the duty of my soldiers to lend their power to me." Rodrick rolled his shoulders.
Lian stayed silent for a moment ...then he laughed...he really laughed.
"No one is behind me?" He slightly lowered his head.
Kain.
Rindo.
Seraphina.
Liana.
Selina.
Marcus.
Ethan.
Cassian.
They were all still there.
"I just don’t need to take their power from them to prove it...besides, can you shut up and stop saying King, King all the time?"
Rodrick’s smile completely disappeared and a moment later, Hunter’s Instincts screamed.
Lian did not even have time to think and the enemy arrived.
BOOOOM!
His fist hit the young Vorhelm’s forearm, the force was much greater than before.
His body left the ground and before he could land, the King was in front of him again, his speed had also increased.
A knee came up.
Lian could not activate Mountain Anchor while in the air.
So...
[ Ash Step. ]
Fsh!
His body turned into ash.
Rodrick was not surprised this time and immediately turned to the right, his fist went straight toward the place where the young Vorhelm had appeared the last time.
But there was nothing there and his eyes changed.
"I thought you said it only takes one time to learn." Lian’s voice came from above.
He raised his head and a few meters above him, a thin platform of ice had formed in the air, the ash gathered on it and it was clear that he had appeared there.
The young Vorhelm fell from above at that exact moment towards him...

chapters.title: Chapter 452: Battle For The Crown ( Final )
paragraphs: The young Vorhelm fell from above at that exact moment.
Giant’s Momentum.
The real weight of the World-Devourer Bastion gathered behind his fall and his fist went toward Rodrick’s head, he raised both forearms to protect himself from the attack.
[ King’s Reprisal ]
BOOOOOOM!
The ground under his feet sank, but he did not fall. Streams of mana moved from his forearms to his shoulders and chest again.
He took the force of the attack, stored it, and returned it together with his borrowed power.
His fist hit Lian directly in the stomach.
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
This time, the young Vorhelm was smashed into the ground like a cannonball, the stone exploded and a crater several meters wide formed in the platform.
Dust rose dozens of meters into the air.
If it were not for the World-Devourer Bastion on his body, that attack could have crushed part of his chest.
Even with the armor, terrible pain spread through his entire stomach and Lian stayed among the broken stones for several seconds.
Then his black armored hand came out through the dust, grabbed the edge of the crater, and pulled himself up.
Clang.
One of the armor’s chest plates had a deep crack.
[Structural Memory activated.]
Silver lines started to move, he spat the blood that had gathered in his mouth onto the ground, then looked at Rodrick.
He was also breathing heavily, Tyrant’s Tribute had given him great power, but it was not free, his mana was being used up at a terrible speed.
"Why are you still standing?" Then a proud smile appeared on his lips.
"Wouldn’t it be better if you surrendered right now, Vorhelm?"
"All you have to do is admit that I am stronger than you... better than you... more handsome than you... and most importantly, I am the King."
His smile became deeper.
"If you kneel right now and accept this King’s mercy, maybe when you leave this place, you will still have a few bones left unbroken."
"So think carefully, Vorhelm."
"Will you choose your pride... or your King’s mercy?"
"Pride?" Lian’s smile became a little deeper.
"I think the fact that I was able to make you reveal your trump card despite the sixteen-Level difference between us... that alone counts as a victory."
His eyes became sharper and he stared directly at Rodrick.
"And besides... I’m still not done with you... and now you’re asking me to surrender? Don’t you think it’s a little too early to call yourself the winner?"
Something changed in Rodrick’s eyes.
Level 23.
Only this number kept repeating in his mind again and again.
Level 23.
This man had defeated two Royal Seal Guardians before reaching this place.
After that, he had fought him, and now even after Rodrick activated the first innate trait of his class and borrowed the power of several subordinates, he was still standing.
Worse, he was still smiling, this was something that had gotten stuck in the corner of his mind, he had tried to ignore it but it was really bothering him.
Even with a sixteen-Level difference, he still could not defeat this Vorhelm and the professors were watching this.
If he could not give this battle a glorious ending, it would be no different from a defeat for him.
Down the mountain, Rodrick’s faction was also starting to fall apart.
Not because they had suddenly become weaker, but because the same power that their King had borrowed from them was now being taken from their bodies at the worst possible time.
Several notifications appeared one after another.
[One participant eliminated.]
[One participant eliminated.]
[One participant eliminated.]
Then a fourth one.
Rindo’s group’s pressure no longer stopped, the enemy group’s last line of defense had been broken and now there was no one left who could reach the peak and stand between the two of them.
Rodrick was truly alone, though not completely, the power of his subordinates was still flowing through his body, but they were no longer beside him.

Lian thought about this contradiction, the person whose entire path to power was about building a territory and gathering people had, at the most important moment of the test, been forced to take their power and stand alone.
It was not a bad irony.
[Time Remaining: 00:38.]
Thirty-eight seconds.
Both of them looked at the timer at the same time.
Rodrick no longer needed to defeat the young Vorhelm, he only needed to survive.
Thirty-eight seconds.
If the Crown stayed in his hand, it would be over and he would get first place, but this was another kind of humiliation for him.
He could not defeat someone who was sixteen Levels below him, even after using an innate trait ... so how was he any different from a loser?
He slowly breathed in and then all his remaining mana started to move and flowed toward his right fist.
Tyrant’s Advance activated.
One step.
Second step.
Third step.
All the force from his previous steps gathered inside his body.
The borrowed power of his subordinates, the stored force of King’s Reprisal, his remaining mana, and the Tyrant Body all gathered at one point.
A fist.
[Tyrant’s Final Decree.]
Even before Rodrick moved, the stone around his feet started to crack.
Lian understood too, this was no longer an attack he could simply move away from, if he retreated, Rodrick would only buy more time.
So he moved forward.
[ Mountain Anchor ]
The feet of the World-Devourer Bastion locked into the ground.
[ Thunder Calamity ]
KRRRRRRAAAACK!
Blue and purple lightning covered his entire right arm.
[ Giant’s Momentum. ]
The true weight of the armor went behind his movement and right before the collision ...
[ Cataclysm Pulse ]
But this time he did not release it, he kept the destructive wave inside his fist, compressed, tightly packed, and waiting for one single point and their eyes met.
Rodrick roared and Lian smiled, then both of them moved.
Fist against fist.
Clang.
For a fraction of a second, there was no sound and then it was as if the world exploded.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The shockwave came out from the peak and hundreds of meters around the mountain shook, the rocks at the edge of the platform broke off and fell into the sea of clouds.
All the remaining ice turned into white powder in an instant and even the students standing lower down had to raise their arms in front of their faces.
At the center of the collision, Thunder Calamity mixed with Rodrick’s golden mana.
And at that exact moment, Cataclysm Pulse was released.
BOOOOM!
A second explosion happened and dust covered the entire peak, for several seconds no one could see anything and then the wind pushed the dust away.
Two shadows appeared, both of them were still standing.

The young Vorhelm was one step behind the place of the collision, parts of the forearm and shoulder plate of the World-Devourer Bastion were broken and deep cracks could be seen on the chest of the armor, though they were already returning to their original form.
His breathing was heavy and blood was running from the corner of his mouth.
In front of him, Rodrick’s right hand was shaking, his knuckles were torn open and blood was dripping from between his fingers onto the stone.
Part of his sleeve was completely destroyed and his breathing was even heavier than Lian’s, but no Protective Seal had activated.
Not for Lian.
Not for Rodrick.
Neither of them had managed to eliminate the other, the direct and final clash had ended in a draw.
[Time Remaining: 00:12.]
Rodrick looked at the timer and a tired smile appeared on his face.
"It’s over." He said while breathing heavily.
Lian also looked at the time and then put his eyes back on Rodrick.
"The fight? Yeah."
Rodrick’s eyebrows came together and the Vorhelm stepped forward.
"If we only count our fists... we’re tied."
For a moment, Rodrick almost felt that this was Lian admitting defeat.
Because a draw was not enough, he had the Crown, he was the final winner and he was going to get first place.
Only twelve seconds remained but Lian’s next sentence broke that feeling.
"But you’re Level 39."
Rodrick’s smile disappeared.
"You completed your First Evolution, unlocked the first innate trait of your class, used your own power, and when that was not enough, you also borrowed the power of your subordinates."
The young Ashen said nothing.
And Vorhelm looked directly into his eyes.
"And in the end... you could only draw with a Level 23."
Something broke on Rodrick’s face, very small but clear, all the cold calmness he had kept since the beginning of the test cracked.
Anger.
Humiliation.
And something worse than both.
Disbelief.
Because he could not deny Lian’s words.
If Rodrick had defeated him, it would not matter what power he had used.
The winner was the winner, but he had failed, he had put everything on the table and had only managed a draw.
Then something suddenly came to his mind, why was Lian still this calm?
His eyes narrowed.
That’s right ... this bastard had not been forced to use any trump card, he had not been forced to show his full power.
And yet he had put everything he had on the table and they had only gotten a draw ...?
This was not a draw ... this was a defeat, in the eyes of the professors and all the Guild representatives ... even in the eyes of all the students, this was a complete defeat for him.
This was a defeat for a King.
The Tyrant King could not defeat a lone Peasant even with the help of his subordinates.

After that, he had fought him, and now even after Rodrick activated the first innate trait of his class and borrowed the power of several subordinates, he was still standing.
Worse, he was still smiling, this was something that had gotten stuck in the corner of his mind, he had tried to ignore it but it was really bothering him.
Even with a sixteen-Level difference, he still could not defeat this Vorhelm and the professors were watching this.
If he could not give this battle a glorious ending, it would be no different from a defeat for him.
Down the mountain, Rodrick’s faction was also starting to fall apart.
Not because they had suddenly become weaker, but because the same power that their King had borrowed from them was now being taken from their bodies at the worst possible time.
Several notifications appeared one after another.
[One participant eliminated.]
[One participant eliminated.]
[One participant eliminated.]
Then a fourth one.
Rindo’s group’s pressure no longer stopped, the enemy group’s last line of defense had been broken and now there was no one left who could reach the peak and stand between the two of them.
Rodrick was truly alone, though not completely, the power of his subordinates was still flowing through his body, but they were no longer beside him.

Lian thought about this contradiction, the person whose entire path to power was about building a territory and gathering people had, at the most important moment of the test, been forced to take their power and stand alone.
It was not a bad irony.
[Time Remaining: 00:38.]
Thirty-eight seconds.
Both of them looked at the timer at the same time.
Rodrick no longer needed to defeat the young Vorhelm, he only needed to survive.
Thirty-eight seconds.
If the Crown stayed in his hand, it would be over and he would get first place, but this was another kind of humiliation for him.
He could not defeat someone who was sixteen Levels below him, even after using an innate trait ... so how was he any different from a loser?
He slowly breathed in and then all his remaining mana started to move and flowed toward his right fist.
Tyrant’s Advance activated.
One step.
Second step.
Third step.
All the force from his previous steps gathered inside his body.
The borrowed power of his subordinates, the stored force of King’s Reprisal, his remaining mana, and the Tyrant Body all gathered at one point.
A fist.
[Tyrant’s Final Decree.]
Even before Rodrick moved, the stone around his feet started to crack.
Lian understood too, this was no longer an attack he could simply move away from, if he retreated, Rodrick would only buy more time.
So he moved forward.
[ Mountain Anchor ]
The feet of the World-Devourer Bastion locked into the ground.
[ Thunder Calamity ]
KRRRRRRAAAACK!
Blue and purple lightning covered his entire right arm.
[ Giant’s Momentum. ]
The true weight of the armor went behind his movement and right before the collision ...
[ Cataclysm Pulse ]
But this time he did not release it, he kept the destructive wave inside his fist, compressed, tightly packed, and waiting for one single point and their eyes met.
Rodrick roared and Lian smiled, then both of them moved.
Fist against fist.
Clang.
For a fraction of a second, there was no sound and then it was as if the world exploded.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The shockwave came out from the peak and hundreds of meters around the mountain shook, the rocks at the edge of the platform broke off and fell into the sea of clouds.
All the remaining ice turned into white powder in an instant and even the students standing lower down had to raise their arms in front of their faces.
At the center of the collision, Thunder Calamity mixed with Rodrick’s golden mana.
And at that exact moment, Cataclysm Pulse was released.
BOOOOM!
A second explosion happened and dust covered the entire peak, for several seconds no one could see anything and then the wind pushed the dust away.
Two shadows appeared, both of them were still standing.

The young Vorhelm was one step behind the place of the collision, parts of the forearm and shoulder plate of the World-Devourer Bastion were broken and deep cracks could be seen on the chest of the armor, though they were already returning to their original form.
His breathing was heavy and blood was running from the corner of his mouth.
In front of him, Rodrick’s right hand was shaking, his knuckles were torn open and blood was dripping from between his fingers onto the stone.
Part of his sleeve was completely destroyed and his breathing was even heavier than Lian’s, but no Protective Seal had activated.
Not for Lian.
Not for Rodrick.
Neither of them had managed to eliminate the other, the direct and final clash had ended in a draw.
[Time Remaining: 00:12.]
Rodrick looked at the timer and a tired smile appeared on his face.
"It’s over." He said while breathing heavily.
Lian also looked at the time and then put his eyes back on Rodrick.
"The fight?
Yeah."
Rodrick’s eyebrows came together and the Vorhelm stepped forward.
"If we only count our fists... we’re tied."
For a moment, Rodrick almost felt that this was Lian admitting defeat.
Because a draw was not enough, he had the Crown, he was the final winner and he was going to get first place.
Only twelve seconds remained but Lian’s next sentence broke that feeling.
"But you’re Level 39."
Rodrick’s smile disappeared.
"You completed your First Evolution, unlocked the first innate trait of your class, used your own power, and when that was not enough, you also borrowed the power of your subordinates."
The young Ashen said nothing.
And Vorhelm looked directly into his eyes.
"And in the end... you could only draw with a Level 23."
Something broke on Rodrick’s face, very small but clear, all the cold calmness he had kept since the beginning of the test cracked.
Anger.
Humiliation.
And something worse than both.
Disbelief.
Because he could not deny Lian’s words.
If Rodrick had defeated him, it would not matter what power he had used.
The winner was the winner, but he had failed, he had put everything on the table and had only managed a draw.
Then something suddenly came to his mind, why was Lian still this calm?
His eyes narrowed.
That’s right ... this bastard had not been forced to use any trump card, he had not been forced to show his full power.
And yet he had put everything he had on the table and they had only gotten a draw ...?
This was not a draw ... this was a defeat, in the eyes of the professors and all the Guild representatives ... even in the eyes of all the students, this was a complete defeat for him.
This was a defeat for a King.
The Tyrant King could not defeat a lone Peasant even with the help of his subordinates.

chapters.title: Chapter 453: The Broken Crown ( Final )
paragraphs: His left hand closed tighter around the Crown and he pressed his teeth together ... the feeling of humiliation was burning deep into his mind and bones.
Lian smiled.
And suddenly his body turned into ash.
[ Ash Step ]
"No!" Rodrick immediately turned around, he suddenly felt something very bad and dangerous, his entire mind was tense from the feeling of humiliation and he could not think properly.
Even he did not know what he was doing.
This time, his fist went toward the right, the same direction where the Vorhelm had appeared during his previous use, using the last of his remaining mana.
But no one was there, his eyes opened wider, Lian had never planned to appear behind him from the beginning.
And the ash gathered right beside Rodrick’s left hand.
Frost Dominion.
Crack!
A layer of ice formed around Rodrick’s fingers in an instant, not enough to freeze his hand and not even to hurt him but only for one thing.
To make his fingers unable to close more tightly around the Crown for a fraction of a second.
"Damn it!" He exploded his mana.
The ice broke, but that fraction of a second was enough.
Vorhelm appeared, his right palm placed on Rodrick’s wrist.
[ Cataclysm Pulse ]
This time it was small, compressed, and precise.
Clang!
There was no big explosion, this attack was very controlled and only for one specific purpose, and as a result, the target’s wrist moved.
His fingers opened and ...the Crown came out of his hand.
Both of their eyes fell on the Crown.
Rodrick reached out his hand, Lian did the same.
The first one’s distance was shorter, he was about to catch it, but a thin ice platform formed right under the Crown.
Clang!
The Crown hit it, its falling angle changed, it passed beside his fingers and turned directly toward Vorhelm.
Lian’s black armored hand closed around the Crown.
Silence covered everything for a moment and then
[Crown ownership changed.]
Rodrick remained still.
[The previous King failed to complete the Crown holding condition.]
His eyes slowly opened wider.
[Duration of Rodrick’s Crown holding: 29:59.]
Twenty-nine minutes.
Fifty-nine seconds.
Only one second.
All the defense ...all the planning...everyone who had fought for him...dozens of students he had eliminated, his own power and Tyrant’s Tribute ...all of them had failed for one second.
The next notification appeared.
[The King has been defeated.]
[King Defeat Reward: 500 Crown Points.]
[500 points have been given to Lian Vorhelm.]
[Points: 1694.]
And finally
[New Crown Holder: Lian Vorhelm.]
[Test has ended.]
Lian looked at the Crown in his hand for several seconds, then raised his head.
Rodrick was still standing there, but something on his face was different from a few minutes ago, disbelief had first taken over everything.
His eyes moved between the Crown and the notification showing twenty-nine minutes and fifty-nine seconds.
It was as if his mind refused to accept the result.
Then anger came, his jaw was clenched so tightly that the muscles beside his face became visible.
His bloody fist shook but even anger could not hide the third feeling.
Humiliation.
Not because Vorhelm had defeated him with one punch.
If something like that had happened, he could have blamed it on an unknown ability or a strange difference in power.
What happened was worse, Rodrick had shown everything he had.
Himself.
His evolved Class.
His innate trait.
His subordinates.
And after all of that, Lian had still been able to stand in front of him.
"I told you I didn’t come for the Crown." The new King raised the Crown and said calmly.
"But now that it’s here... I’ll keep it." His original goal really was not the Crown, but under no circumstances would he let this bastard feel that he had won.
His goal was simple, to break all of his prestige and the stupid structure he had built, and the best way to do that was to crush his pride.
He was not someone who caused trouble for others without a reason, but Rodrick had spent all of high school humiliating him, just because he had failed Awakening.
After that, he had even dared to isolate his best friend Kain for months and cause trouble for him.
He would not let such a bastard become a problem for him in the future, when he could destroy his roots right here.
Unfortunately, defeating the enemy was not easy for him, the Level difference was still causing problems, he had to use everything he had.
And when there were other ways to crush Rodrick, he did not need to defeat him in a traditional battle.
Besides, winning a battle does not always mean that the other side is the winner, the real point of victory is to break the enemy’s pride so badly that they never dare to stand up again.
But Lian was still not finished, there was still one final shot left.
"Don’t worry, you weren’t a bad King, but now this Peasant will proudly take your Crown for himself."
At that exact moment, kilometers away from the simulated territory, the Academy’s monitoring hall had fallen into silence.
Dozens of large images were floating in the air.
But almost no one was looking at any other image anymore and everyone’s eyes were fixed on one image.
Lian and the Crown that was now in his hand.
The Academy’s senior professors were there, representatives of several large Guilds, people who had originally come to examine Rodrick, Kain, Seraphina, and the other talents of the new generation.
Some of them had already seen the first reports about Lian Vorhelm a long time ago.
But reading a report was different from seeing it.
One of the Guild representatives said nothing for several seconds.
"His Level... is really 23?" Then, as if he needed to make sure he had not read the number wrong, he asked quietly.
No one answered immediately.
Professor Silas was still looking at the image behind his glasses, his usual amused expression was much weaker now.
Beside him, Professor Aldric had his arms crossed over his chest.
He already knew that Lian was more dangerous than his Level showed, he had already seen that this boy was not ordinary.
But even he had not expected the difference to be this ridiculous.
Level 23.
Against Level 39.
It was not only the Level difference.
Rodrick had completed his First Evolution long ago, his four-star Class had evolved into Tyrant Ruler.
He had also unlocked the first innate trait of his Class and in the end, he had even brought the power of several subordinates into his own body.
And he still could not defeat Vorhelm.

"What is that boy’s Class? Could it be five-star? I guess it isn’t just an ordinary five-star either, he must also have a very powerful Talent." Another representative slowly leaned forward from his seat.
Another silence formed.
Lian’s official file had no answer that could explain what they had just seen, he had registered his Class as Warrior before Evolution and his Talent was not public either.
Silas said nothing for several seconds, then he slowly pushed his glasses higher while his eyes were still on the image of him.
But Rodrick was not the only one looking at Lian in disbelief.
At that moment, almost all the professors and Guild representatives present in the monitoring hall had also fallen into a heavy silence.
And one of the most serious reactions belonged to the Headmaster of the Academy, Seraphina’s father...

chapters.title: Chapter 454: A King’s Humiliation
paragraphs: [The Final Stage has ended.]
[All battles have stopped.]
[Crown Holder at the moment of the end: Lian Vorhelm.]
[The Broken Crown Test has ended.]
The red light that had been reaching the sky from the Crown until a few moments ago disappeared in an instant.
Almost at the same time, all the active mana on the peak also died down.
Rodrick, who was still clenching his bloody fist, tried to take another step forward for a moment, but his body no longer obeyed him.
The simulated battle realm itself had stopped the battle.
It was over.
Lian was standing in front of him and the Crown was still between his armored fingers.
There were only a few meters between them.
But what had looked like a close competition a few minutes ago now had a clear result.
Rodrick looked at the Crown and then slowly raised his eyes toward Vorhelm’s face.
His usual control had mostly returned, but even now he could not completely hide the anger deep in his eyes.
"This isn’t over." He said in a low voice, there was no direct threat in his tone and it sounded more like a promise.
"Do you want to humiliate yourself even more? This time it ended in a draw, next time the result will be your defeat." Lian looked at him for a few moments.
The young Ashen’s face became stiff for a moment, he wanted to deny it but all the evidence showed that if another battle happened in the future, he would be the loser.
But would he accept such a result? No! No matter what happened, he would return today’s humiliation a thousand times over.
He would never accept losing to this bastard, such a thing would never become reality.
Lian Vorhelm always had to be under his feet, only this way could he continue to be a King.
And before he could say anything, white light formed around both of them.
The world disappeared.
When Lian could see again, the inverted mountain was gone.
The stone ground of the Academy’s central arena was under his feet and thousands of pillars of light appeared across the area one after another.
The students were returning from the simulated realm, some immediately fell to one knee.
Some took several deep breaths and some others just stood still for several seconds, as if their minds still had not accepted that they no longer needed to expect an attack at any moment.
A large part of the physical damage caused by the test had disappeared after leaving the realm, but mental exhaustion and mana consumption were real.
He raised his head and at that moment noticed that many eyes were fixed on him.

For several seconds, no one said anything, as if the shock of what they had experienced was not easy to accept, and they had every right to feel that way, they had seen something that should not have been possible in any way or by any logic.
Then the first whisper came.
"That’s him..."
Another voice came from a few meters away.
"He got two Seals by himself."
"Speed Seal and Spirit Seal."
"He also drew with Rodrick."
"A draw? He even took the Crown from him at the end."
"His Level is really 23?"
Then someone said a sentence that made several others immediately turn their heads away so their laughter would not be seen.
"Twenty-nine minutes and fifty-nine seconds...
Lian raised the corner of his lips.
That number probably was not going to be forgotten anytime soon.
"Twenty-nine minutes and fifty-nine seconds."
A familiar voice came directly from in front of him this time.
Lian lowered his eyes.
Kain walked through several students and stood in front of him and only looked at him for several seconds...then slowly shook his head.

"You really waited until the last second to take the Crown? Was it luck? Had you already thought about it? Didn’t you think about what would happen if your calculations went wrong???" He asked with an expression between laughter and disbelief.
"I had thought about it, it was my plan from the beginning, I knew that defeating him in a direct battle was not easy, and I would have to reveal many things." Lian answered calmly.
"So you waited until the last second to take the Crown? Didn’t you think it might not work???"
"It was more painful this way." The young Vorhelm shrugged.
Kain stared directly at his face for several seconds, his mouth opened several times but each time he did not know what he should say and closed it again.
He wanted to teach Rodrick a lesson, but what this boy had done was not a physical lesson, he had destroyed his entire reputation.
He had destroyed all the power and charisma that bastard had built.
What he had not been able to do in nine months, Vorhelm had done in just a few days after his return.
At that moment, a short laugh came from behind Kain.
Liana and Selina approached them together with Marcus, Ethan, Cassian, and Seraphina.
Rindo was a few steps behind them and unlike Kain, he did not have a smile on his face.
His eyes first moved to Lian and then to the students who were still standing around them and talking about the result of the test.
"Today you didn’t just get first place, you also broke something else; something Rodrick spent months building."
"His image of being unbeatable?"

"Exactly, until today many people thought the only question was who could stand behind Rodrick, but now for the first time they saw that someone could also stand in front of him and I have to thank you for that...I guess there won’t be any more problems for the Student Council’s position."
"Someone who is sixteen Levels lower than him." Kain gave a crooked smile.
"That part probably hurts the most, but I guess now you are becoming what Rodrick wanted to be." Rindo gave him a quick look.
It seemed that just saying Rodrick’s name was enough, the crowd a few meters away slowly moved aside.
And the person they were talking about appeared.
Elena was walking on his right and several members of his faction were also behind them.
Darren was also among them, this time the way people opened a path for Rodrick was different from before.
There was still respect, there were still many people who admired his power and position but the looks directed at him were no longer all the same.
Curiosity.
Comparison.
Even something like pity in a few cases.

The matter was not just a battle between two young men, both sides were well-known, one was a young man whose name had been known for almost two years because of his four-star Class and S-Rank Talent.
He was from a great family and had managed to become part of one of the five great Guilds of the country, Guilds that had a name, reputation, and power across the entire continent.
A person who called himself a King and had ruled over the entire Academy and Base #3 like a King for nine full months.
And the other? Lian Vorhelm, until not long ago he was known as a loser and even as someone who had been exiled from his own family.
Especially since there had already been conflicts between the two in the past, and even the girl who was now beside Rodrick had once been Vorhelm’s fiancée.
"He almost won."
"But their Level difference was sixteen, if you can’t defeat someone like that with one hit, then how are you any different from being a loser?" one of the students said quietly.
"Rodrick even activated that trait that took the power of his people, right?"
"He borrowed it."
"Whatever, in the end he still couldn’t defeat Vorhelm."
Rodrick’s right hand clenched for a moment, only for a moment and then opened again, his steps did not change at all.
But Lian noticed that small movement from several meters away, their eyes met for a moment and this time neither of them said anything.
Elena also turned her eyes toward him, it lasted only a few seconds but there was something in her eyes that was not easy to read.
It was a complicated feeling.
One year ago, Lian was known to many as nothing more than the loser who had failed Awakening.
Now that same person, at Level 23, had taken two Seals, stood in a direct battle against Rodrick at Level 39, and pulled the Crown from his hand at the last second.
Lian saw Elena’s gaze but only for a moment and then took his attention away from her.
The girl pressed her lips together very slightly.
Less than ten minutes later, all the participants were moved to the Academy’s main arena.
The wide seats around the arena were also full and students from other years, professors, and guests who had come to watch the test were all present.
In the special section of the seats, dozens of representatives from different Guilds could also be seen.
Some of them had been quietly talking to each other since the moment the students returned.
But when Professor Silas appeared on the central platform, the voices quickly became silent.
The man pushed his glasses slightly higher and looked at the crowd.
"First of all, congratulations, even if you did not get the rank you wanted, those who lasted until the end of the Broken Crown at least proved that they are ready to make decisions under pressure."
Several huge screens appeared above the arena.
"Before announcing the results, let me make one thing clear, points were not the only thing that determined your final rank."
The words appeared one after another.
[Final Evaluation Criteria:]
[Points.]
[Adaptive Difficulty.]
[Combat Performance.]
[Decision-Making Quality.]
[Leadership.]
[Exploration.]
[Unconventional Solutions.]
Silas gave the screen a quick look.

"Someone who collected one thousand points is not necessarily better than someone who got eight hundred points. If the second person faced higher difficulty, fewer resources, and made better decisions to reach those same eight hundred points, the final evaluation takes this difference into account."
Now many eyes unconsciously moved toward Lian, they were probably curious about the number of his points.
There was no doubt that he would get first place, but they had no idea how many points he had.
Silas gave a very faint smile.
"Anyway, let’s move on to the rankings."
The main screen changed.
[Top Ten Rankings of the Broken Crown Test.]

Lian Vorhelm always had to be under his feet, only this way could he continue to be a King.
And before he could say anything, white light formed around both of them.
The world disappeared.
When Lian could see again, the inverted mountain was gone.
The stone ground of the Academy’s central arena was under his feet and thousands of pillars of light appeared across the area one after another.
The students were returning from the simulated realm, some immediately fell to one knee.
Some took several deep breaths and some others just stood still for several seconds, as if their minds still had not accepted that they no longer needed to expect an attack at any moment.
A large part of the physical damage caused by the test had disappeared after leaving the realm, but mental exhaustion and mana consumption were real.
He raised his head and at that moment noticed that many eyes were fixed on him.

For several seconds, no one said anything, as if the shock of what they had experienced was not easy to accept, and they had every right to feel that way, they had seen something that should not have been possible in any way or by any logic.
Then the first whisper came.
"That’s him..."
Another voice came from a few meters away.
"He got two Seals by himself."
"Speed Seal and Spirit Seal."
"He also drew with Rodrick."
"A draw?
He even took the Crown from him at the end."
"His Level is really 23?"
Then someone said a sentence that made several others immediately turn their heads away so their laughter would not be seen.
"Twenty-nine minutes and fifty-nine seconds...
Lian raised the corner of his lips.
That number probably was not going to be forgotten anytime soon.
"Twenty-nine minutes and fifty-nine seconds."
A familiar voice came directly from in front of him this time.
Lian lowered his eyes.
Kain walked through several students and stood in front of him and only looked at him for several seconds...then slowly shook his head.
"You really waited until the last second to take the Crown?
Was it luck?
Had you already thought about it?
Didn’t you think about what would happen if your calculations went wrong???" He asked with an expression between laughter and disbelief.
"I had thought about it, it was my plan from the beginning, I knew that defeating him in a direct battle was not easy, and I would have to reveal many things." Lian answered calmly.
"So you waited until the last second to take the Crown?
Didn’t you think it might not work???"
"It was more painful this way." The young Vorhelm shrugged.
Kain stared directly at his face for several seconds, his mouth opened several times but each time he did not know what he should say and closed it again.
He wanted to teach Rodrick a lesson, but what this boy had done was not a physical lesson, he had destroyed his entire reputation.
He had destroyed all the power and charisma that bastard had built.
What he had not been able to do in nine months, Vorhelm had done in just a few days after his return.
At that moment, a short laugh came from behind Kain.
Liana and Selina approached them together with Marcus, Ethan, Cassian, and Seraphina.
Rindo was a few steps behind them and unlike Kain, he did not have a smile on his face.
His eyes first moved to Lian and then to the students who were still standing around them and talking about the result of the test.
"Today you didn’t just get first place, you also broke something else; something Rodrick spent months building."
"His image of being unbeatable?"

"Exactly, until today many people thought the only question was who could stand behind Rodrick, but now for the first time they saw that someone could also stand in front of him and I have to thank you for that...I guess there won’t be any more problems for the Student Council’s position."
"Someone who is sixteen Levels lower than him." Kain gave a crooked smile.
"That part probably hurts the most, but I guess now you are becoming what Rodrick wanted to be." Rindo gave him a quick look.
It seemed that just saying Rodrick’s name was enough, the crowd a few meters away slowly moved aside.
And the person they were talking about appeared.
Elena was walking on his right and several members of his faction were also behind them.
Darren was also among them, this time the way people opened a path for Rodrick was different from before.
There was still respect, there were still many people who admired his power and position but the looks directed at him were no longer all the same.
Curiosity.
Comparison.
Even something like pity in a few cases.

The matter was not just a battle between two young men, both sides were well-known, one was a young man whose name had been known for almost two years because of his four-star Class and S-Rank Talent.
He was from a great family and had managed to become part of one of the five great Guilds of the country, Guilds that had a name, reputation, and power across the entire continent.
A person who called himself a King and had ruled over the entire Academy and Base #3 like a King for nine full months.
And the other?
Lian Vorhelm, until not long ago he was known as a loser and even as someone who had been exiled from his own family.
Especially since there had already been conflicts between the two in the past, and even the girl who was now beside Rodrick had once been Vorhelm’s fiancée.
"He almost won."
"But their Level difference was sixteen, if you can’t defeat someone like that with one hit, then how are you any different from being a loser?" one of the students said quietly.
"Rodrick even activated that trait that took the power of his people, right?"
"He borrowed it."
"Whatever, in the end he still couldn’t defeat Vorhelm."
Rodrick’s right hand clenched for a moment, only for a moment and then opened again, his steps did not change at all.
But Lian noticed that small movement from several meters away, their eyes met for a moment and this time neither of them said anything.
Elena also turned her eyes toward him, it lasted only a few seconds but there was something in her eyes that was not easy to read.
It was a complicated feeling.
One year ago, Lian was known to many as nothing more than the loser who had failed Awakening.
Now that same person, at Level 23, had taken two Seals, stood in a direct battle against Rodrick at Level 39, and pulled the Crown from his hand at the last second.
Lian saw Elena’s gaze but only for a moment and then took his attention away from her.
The girl pressed her lips together very slightly.
Less than ten minutes later, all the participants were moved to the Academy’s main arena.
The wide seats around the arena were also full and students from other years, professors, and guests who had come to watch the test were all present.
In the special section of the seats, dozens of representatives from different Guilds could also be seen.
Some of them had been quietly talking to each other since the moment the students returned.
But when Professor Silas appeared on the central platform, the voices quickly became silent.
The man pushed his glasses slightly higher and looked at the crowd.
"First of all, congratulations, even if you did not get the rank you wanted, those who lasted until the end of the Broken Crown at least proved that they are ready to make decisions under pressure."
Several huge screens appeared above the arena.
"Before announcing the results, let me make one thing clear, points were not the only thing that determined your final rank."
The words appeared one after another.
[Final Evaluation Criteria:]
[Points.]
[Adaptive Difficulty.]
[Combat Performance.]
[Decision-Making Quality.]
[Leadership.]
[Exploration.]
[Unconventional Solutions.]
Silas gave the screen a quick look.
"Someone who collected one thousand points is not necessarily better than someone who got eight hundred points.
If the second person faced higher difficulty, fewer resources, and made better decisions to reach those same eight hundred points, the final evaluation takes this difference into account."
Now many eyes unconsciously moved toward Lian, they were probably curious about the number of his points.
There was no doubt that he would get first place, but they had no idea how many points he had.
Silas gave a very faint smile.
"Anyway, let’s move on to the rankings."
The main screen changed.
[Top Ten Rankings of the Broken Crown Test.]

chapters.title: Chapter 455: The Recruitment War
paragraphs: The ranks from one hundred to ten were never announced at all, these ranks were only personal and could only be seen by the student themselves.
The ranks from ten to four were also clear, in order, Ethan, Marcus, Selina, Liana, Cassian, and Seraphina took fifth place.
When the girl’s rank was revealed, a short wave of whispers spread through the crowd, the Vice President of the Student Council and the Academy’s famous flower had managed to take fifth place.
Everyone had thought that because they had fallen behind for such a long time and their Levels were lower than the others, they might not be able to reach such high ranks.
But all those who had entered the Special Area had still managed to take top ranks.
Fourth place was naturally Kain.

For someone who had spent almost all of the past nine months completing his missions alone, reaching the top four of a test where a large part of the score was related to leadership and cooperation was not a small result.
But the fact that he was a Ranker who had lost to Rodrick was what stopped him from reaching third place.
The screen changed again.
[Third Place: Rindo Valcrest]
A loud cheer came from the Student Council’s section, and even many of the other students clapped.
Rindo only lowered his head slightly.
Leading his group, taking the Resistance Seal, and his performance in the final stage had secured his position.
Two names remained.
But almost no one really had any question about who would take second place.
[Second Place: Rodrick Ashen.]
The arena became silent for a moment, and then scattered cheers rose, Rodrick’s performance had not been weak.

Even considering his final defeat, he had held the Crown for almost thirty minutes against the attacks of a large number of participants and had shown one of the best examples of leadership in the test.
These cheers also came from his supporters and his group, the other students did not feel the need to cheer for him anymore.
But he himself only looked at the screen.
The next name had already been decided, and the huge screen turned golden.
[First Place: Lian Vorhelm.]
The noise in the arena suddenly became much louder.
But the announcements were not over yet.
[Points: 1694.]
[Overall Evaluation: Exceptional.]
[The highest Adaptive Difficulty recorded in this period.]
[Two Seals were directly claimed.]
[The King of the Final Stage was defeated.]
Each announcement caused a new wave of reactions.
Lian had his hands in the pockets of his clothes and was only looking at the screen, his armor was no longer visible on his body because he had already turned it off.
First place.
The same thing he had wanted from the beginning, but when he turned his eyes toward Rodrick for a moment, his satisfaction became a little greater.
Some victories tasted better.
Silas waited until the noise of the crowd became lower.
"The top three of the test will not only receive the Academy’s normal rewards." He raised his hand and another screen appeared.
"One of the rewards that was announced before the test is a permit to enter the Land of First Dawn."
Several people in the crowd immediately became silent, the name of this realm was familiar to many.
Even the students who had no chance of reaching the top three knew how valuable entering it was.
"But the entry is not immediate, the Land of First Dawn will open for the next period three months from now."
The screen lit up.
[Permit to Enter the Land of First Dawn.]
[Entry Time: 90 Days From Now.]
[Permit Holders:]
[Lian Vorhelm.]
[Rodrick Ashen.]
[Rindo.]
Lian looked at the number ninety for a few moments.
Three months.
It was not a short amount of time, many things could happen before then, but at least now one of his future destinations was completely clear.
Another announcement appeared only in front of him.
[Special Reward for First Place.]
[One Free Choice from the Special Section of the Academy Store.]
[Selection Range: Skills with the potential to grow up to Holy Rank.]
This time, his eyes stayed on the announcement for a few more moments, skills with the potential to reach Holy Rank.
Abilities that even had the possibility of reaching such a rank were not things a student could easily buy from the market with money.
They were so rare that they could either only be found in very private auctions, or only the top Guilds and families had access to them.
Before he could think about it more, a new movement on the central platform caught everyone’s attention.
Silas moved aside and another man stepped forward.
Arius, the head of the Academy and Seraphina’s father...He did not need to raise his voice, and his mere presence was enough to make the arena become silent.
He was wearing the official Academy uniform without any extra decoration, his expression was calm, but it was the kind of calm that showed authority more than friendliness.
"The top three, come to the platform." He said, and a few moments later, Lian, Rodrick, and Rindo were standing in front of him.
The three people who had each become the center of this test in a different way.
Rindo, the current President of the Student Council.
Rodrick, the one who was openly moving to replace him and considered himself the king of the Academy.
And Lian, someone who seemed to have no interest in either of these positions, but had broken the balance between both of them in a single day.
Arius first looked at Rindo and held out his hand.

"Your performance as the President of the Student Council was acceptable, even when things went out of control, you did not forget your priority and kept your group together. That is more important than getting a few more points."
"Thank you, Headmaster."
Arius then stood in front of Rodrick and looked at him for a few seconds.
"Twenty-nine minutes and fifty-nine seconds holding the Crown, while your position was visible to all the participants, is not a weak performance."
The muscle in Rodrick’s jaw moved almost without being noticed.
That damn number again!
But Arius had no intention of making fun of him.
"One final second does not make all the twenty-nine minutes before it worthless, but it changes the result. Understand the difference between these two and learn from it."
"I understand, and thank you." He nodded at the end.
Arius nodded and then stood in front of the last person.
Lian.
His pause was a little longer, and the young Vorhelm noticed it.
Even if someone did not know the Headmaster, the greater coldness in his eyes when looking at him was easy to notice.
He did not like Lian, he did not like how close he was to his daughter, and the fact that he had once been a failed, talentless person only made things worse.
After he was also exiled from the Vorhelm family, the Headmaster had tried several times to keep them apart.
But at least he was professional enough not to let this matter change the result of the test.
"First place, two Seals, the highest Adaptive Difficulty of this period, and taking the Crown in the final second."
He stayed silent for a few moments.
"That was an impressive performance." His tone did not match the sentence, it was praise but there was no warmth in it.
"You don’t seem very happy." Lian studied his face for a moment.
Below the platform, Seraphina slightly raised her head, and the corner of her lips moved almost without being noticed.
Kain also quietly said something like, "Here we go."
But Arius did not even blink.
"My duty is not to be happy about the result, my duty is to accept the correct result, even when I personally prefer another one."
At least he was honest.
Vorhelm held his hand, the Headmaster’s grip was firm.
"Congratulations, Lian Vorhelm."
"Thank you, Headmaster."
The two released their hands, for a moment, the three top-ranked students stood beside each other, and the huge screen behind them lit up again.
At the bottom of the arena, the lights of several recording devices turned on.
It was clear from seeing them that this image was probably not going to remain only inside the Academy’s walls.
But for now, it did not matter and the only thing he wanted was a little silence.
Unfortunately, he was not going to get it.
The official ceremony had not even completely ended when the first person stepped forward.
A man in a long white coat with a golden crown symbol on his chest.
"Mr. Vorhelm." He stopped in front of Lian with a professional smile.
"I am a representative of the Heavenly Crown Association. I think it would be better if we talked about your future."
Lian had not even had time to answer when another voice came from the left.
"Before you make a decision, I suggest you also hear the conditions of the Eternal Dawn Association." A woman with light gray hair approached.
"Our main activity is exploring unknown realms. Based on what we saw from you today, I think it would be a very suitable path for you."
The third person entered almost immediately, a huge man who had the symbol of a stone tower on his clothes.
"Titan Bastion does not have the usual financial limits for talents like you." He said directly.
"If we are talking about resources, equipment, or training, we can offer more than most Associations.
Lian opened his mouth.
The fourth person spoke before him.
The representative of Black Moon had appeared beside the crowd almost out of nowhere.
His clothes were simpler than the others.
"We did not come here with a standard offer, if you are interested, a special offer will be prepared just for you. Something that the others do not need to know about."
"Crimson Dragon will guarantee you a direct position in one of the main groups in the Heavenly Realm once you reach a suitable Level." Another man with a red dragon symbol interrupted him.
The five top Associations of the country.
Heavenly Crown.
Eternal Dawn.
Titan Bastion.
Black Moon.
Crimson Dragon.
And the problem was that they were not the only ones who had come.
Several representatives from smaller Associations were also waiting for a chance.
In less than a minute, Lian found himself in the middle of a circle of people, each of them trying to speak before the others.
"Our contract—"
"Monthly resources—"
"Access to exclusive areas—"
"Personal instructor—"
"Mission shares—"
He only looked at them for a few seconds and then his eyes passed over the shoulder of one of the representatives.
A few meters away, Kain was in almost the same situation, four people were standing around him and two more were coming closer.
Kain’s eyes met Lian’s, neither of them said anything for a moment, and then the first one very quietly moved his lips.
"Help."
Lian looked around himself.
Eight people..
"I’m stuck too." He looked at his friend again and raised one shoulder.
Kain closed his eyes.
Rindo was not in a better situation either.
Several representatives who were looking for members ready to immediately enter professional operations had gone directly to him.
Seraphina was also surrounded by two Associations.
Liana and Selina had not even had a chance to leave the arena yet.
Only Rodrick did not have such a problem.
He was already connected to an Association, and the other representatives also knew enough about this that they did not waste their time.
"Mr. Vorhelm, if you could just give us five minutes—"
"I think you have bothered him enough." A voice came at that moment, it was not loud, but it was enough to silence the circle around him.
The people moved aside.
Professor Aldric stepped forward from the crowd.
His hands were behind his back, and his expression showed that he was not very interested in arguing.
One of the Heavenly Crown representatives kept his formal smile.
"Professor Aldric, we were just—"
"You are just having eight people talk into his ears at the same time, if your goal is to annoy him, I think you succeeded."
Several people became silent.
"Come." The Professor moved his eyes toward him.
"With pleasure." Lian did not think for even a moment.
He passed through the gap that had opened, one of the representatives wanted to say something again, but Aldric’s look was enough to make him stop.
A few minutes later, the two had moved away from the busiest part of the arena.
"Thank you." Vorhelm let out a quiet breath.
"For what?" Aldric looked at him.
"If I stayed there for another five minutes, I would probably have to throw one of them out of a window."
"Then your first achievement after obtaining first place, would be getting expelled from the Academy." The Professor stayed silent for a moment.
When they reached the intersection of the Academy’s main paths, he then pointed toward the main building of the Academy Store instead of the path to the dormitory.
"Your first-place reward, do you want to receive it now?"
The tiredness on Lian’s face became less for a moment, he was not stupid enough to not understand what he meant.
"A skill with the potential to reach Holy Rank?"
"Yeah, do you want to receive it now?"

"If I stayed there for another five minutes, I would probably have to throw one of them out of a window."
"Then your first achievement after obtaining first place, would be getting expelled from the Academy." The Professor stayed silent for a moment.
When they reached the intersection of the Academy’s main paths, he then pointed toward the main building of the Academy Store instead of the path to the dormitory.
"Your first-place reward, do you want to receive it now?"
The tiredness on Lian’s face became less for a moment, he was not stupid enough to not understand what he meant.
"A skill with the potential to reach Holy Rank?"
"Yeah, do you want to receive it now?"

chapters.title: Chapter 456: Holy Rank Skill I
paragraphs: "Of course, how could I delay receiving something this important until later?" Lian added with a greedy smile.
Of course, he needed some time to just relax, but a skill with the potential to reach Holy Rank...was tempting enough.
This was not something he could easily obtain, of course, as a Vorhelm, his family had several of these skills, but even for the young members of the Vorhelm family, obtaining them was not easy.
He quickened his steps and reached Aldric’s side.
"I knew it." The Professor gave him a short look.
The two moved away from the main arena.
The noise of the ceremony had still not completely ended, and groups of students were spreading out along different paths.
Every few meters, someone would turn their eyes toward Lian and then quietly say something to the friend beside them.
He noticed it several times but did not care.
For Aldric, the scene was a little different, as he walked beside that boy, he sometimes looked at the young man from the corner of his eye.
Level 23.
A number that, from his point of view, was almost funny.
Not much time had passed since the beginning of the year, but he clearly remembered what condition this boy had been in when he first started watching him more seriously.
His Level had barely even been 10.
A young boy with a strange Awakening history that no one still knew where to place.
Even many of the professors were not sure that a bright future was waiting for him.
Now that same boy was Level 23.
He had completed his First Evolution.
He had defeated two Unholy Guardians while one of his main body stats was completely sealed each time.
He had taken two Seals by himself.
And in the end, he had stood against Level 39 Rodrick.
Not a tired and defenseless Rodrick.
But a Rodrick who had completed his First Evolution, unlocked the first innate trait of his Class Tree, and in the end had even borrowed the power of some of his subordinates.
Even so, he had not been able to defeat Lian.
Aldric had been teaching Awakened for many years, Level was still one of the simplest and most reliable ways to estimate a person’s strength.
Someone at Level 30 was usually stronger than someone at Level 20, actually almost always
Someone who had completed their Evolution usually should not even be placed in the same group as someone who had not reached that stage yet.
But the more he looked at this Vorhelm, the more he realized that this standard was losing its real meaning for him.
Not that Level no longer mattered, Lian also became stronger as his Level increased.
But it was no longer possible to judge his real strength just by looking at the number beside his name.
If someone had told Aldric one year ago that a Level 23 boy could stand against a Level 39 Evolver, his first question would have been how weak that Level 39 person was.
But Rodrick was not weak.
The problem was that Lian no longer fit into any normal standard.
And this reminded him of another legend, the man whose simple steps could cause an earthquake that shook the continent.
The Guardian of the Continent and the Celestial Knight, the Patriarch of the Vorhelm family.
The son and father really did look similar.
"What is it?" Lian’s voice pulled the Professor out of his thoughts.
"Nothing." He realized that he had been looking at this boy for a few seconds too long.
"That look usually doesn’t mean nothing."
"I was thinking about how someone who was Level ten at the beginning of the year has now reached the point where I can’t guess how strong he really is just from his Level."
"Was that a compliment? Can I consider that the most serious and bad-tempered Professor in the Academy just complimented me?" Vorhelm stayed silent for a moment and then gave a small smile.
"Whatever." Aldric ignored him and then added.
"Just don’t get too used to it. You are still Level twenty-three. Being able to fight above your Level does not mean the Level difference no longer exists."
"I know." This time Lian’s answer had no joke in it, he knew better than anyone how terrifying the gap between higher Levels could become.
Level was only one part of strength, but even that part was not something he could ignore forever.
Especially after the Third Evolution, the difference between each Level became crazy.
They walked a few more steps in silence until he suddenly asked another question.
"Professor, what do you think about the Land of First Down?"
The Professor’s steps became slightly slower, he did not answer for a few seconds, and Lian noticed that pause.
"That silence was not very promising."
"I don’t have a good feeling about it."
Vorhelm raised his eyebrows, this was almost the last answer he had expected, he had thought this land was some kind of paradise that everyone loved.
So why would the Professor give such an answer?
"Considering that the permit to enter it is the reward for the top three of one of the Academy’s most important tests, I expected a more convincing answer."
"I said I don’t have a good feeling about it, I didn’t say it was a bad place."
"What’s the difference?"
Aldric thought for a moment.
"Almost all the reports we have about it are good. There are resources found there that are extremely rare outside the realm, ancient items, skill books, and even strange treasures."
His expression became a little more serious.
"Every time we explore it, at least several people return with something that can change the course of their lives."
Lian waited for the rest for a few seconds.
But the Professor became silent and said nothing else.
"And where is the bad part in that?"
"That’s it...I don’t trust places that give more than they take."
Vorhelm said nothing for a moment, even to him, this sentence made sense, no great resource came without a cost.
If there really was a place that let Awakened enter it and almost always sent them back with huge rewards, the natural question was not why people entered it.
The question was what that place itself gained.
"Has anything suspicious ever happened?"
"Nothing that can be used as evidence."
"So it’s just a feeling."
"Exactly, stay alive for many years, then you’ll understand that sometimes the bad feeling of an experienced person is worth more than ten pages of reports."
"Do you think something is hidden there?"
"I don’t know. If I knew, it wouldn’t be called a bad feeling anymore." Aldric raised one shoulder.
They reached the end of the path, and the large Academy Store building appeared from behind a row of trees.
Before entering, the Professor stopped for a moment and gave him some advice.

"I’m not saying don’t go. If I were you, I would enter three months from now too. It’s an opportunity that would be stupid to pass up, but when you go there, don’t only look at what is in front of your eyes. Some dangers don’t come at you with teeth and claws, a realm does not need to attack you to be dangerous."
"I’ll remember that." Lian then thanked him for the advice.
The main Academy Store was larger than its name suggested.
The first floor was almost like a controlled market, students could use their points to buy materials, potions, simpler equipment, Mana Cores, and skill books.
But Aldric did not even look at any of them.
He passed the main counter and entered a hallway that normal students were not allowed to enter.
At the end of the hallway, there was a dark metal door, it had no handle.
And he held his Senior Professor Badge in front of the panel beside it, several lines lit up on the surface of the door.
Click.
The door opened.
Lian expected a huge hall full of treasures behind it, but the space behind the door was quite small.
A rectangular room with several shelves and a number of glass containers, each one covered with several layers of Seals, and a large amount of empty space.
"I expected it to be bigger."
"There aren’t many things that are truly valuable, if we had a large storage room full of rare skills, that would be too bad and could make people lazy." He walked toward the far wall.
Three containers were separated from the others, and each one contained a different book.
Aldric stood in front of them.
"The entire Academy only has three skills whose confirmed Evolution Paths can reach Holy Rank."
