chapters.title: Chapter 457: Holy Rank Skill II
paragraphs: "The entire Academy only has three skills whose confirmed Evolution Paths can reach Holy Rank." Aldric then pointed at the first container.
The book inside was black, and seven thin silver lines could be seen on its cover.
"Seven Void Steps, a movement skill."
The information on the container lit up.
[Seven Void Steps.]
[Rank: Common (+).]

[Description: At the current stage, it allows you to make several sudden changes in direction over a short distance, without having to completely stop your previous momentum. The higher it goes, the number of steps, distance, and freedom to change direction will increase.]
Lian looked at the book for a few seconds, it was not a bad skill, in fact, it was excellent for most close-range fighters.
But he already had several movement skills, a skill after reaching Holy Rank could definitely become much more useful.
But he felt that he should not waste his reward like this.
"I don’t recommend it to you, from what I’ve seen, you have strong movement skills."
He went to the second container, a white book with golden lines.
[The Indestructible Body.]
[Current Rank: Common (+).]

"It starts by creating a permanent Mana cycle inside the body. It increases resistance, recovery, ability to endure pressure, and the ability to continue fighting. At higher stages, its body regeneration becomes really ridiculous." The Professor explained.
"This one isn’t bad." Lian whispered to himself.

"No, it’s very good, this skill after reaching Holy Rank can give you a body that is practically indestructible for several minutes, even attacks from someone like me would not be able to destroy it, but it is not the best for you." Aldric gave Lian’s body a short look.
"Why?"

"Your body changed enough after the First Evolution that you already naturally have many of the advantages this skill gives at its lower stages. Bones, muscles, joints, ability to take hits...all of them have increased to an abnormal level." His eyes narrowed slightly.
"I don’t know exactly what your Evolution did to you, and you also have that armor, I guess it’s Ancient Rank, right? That armor alone is enough."
Lian said nothing, a body that was indestructible for several minutes? This skill could be very good for someone like Marcus.
Even for himself, it could be useful and could help him when fighting creatures much stronger than himself.
But he waited until he saw the last Holy Rank skill before making his final choice.
They reached the third container, a dark-colored book with the image of a palm on its cover, the image was simple.
But several thin golden lines spread from the center of the palm toward the fingers.
Lian had not asked anything yet when the panel of the container lit up.
[Suppressing Palm.]
[Rank: Common (+).]
"At the initial stage, you compress Mana inside your palm. You can release it together with a real strike, or send it from a distance in the form of a Mana palm." The Professor explained.
"But what makes this skill valuable is not the size of the palm. It is the density. The higher your mastery becomes, the more power you can compress into a smaller space."
"Does Physical Strength also affect it?" Lian looked at the information.

"Yes, this skill can be both a small strike and a very large strike, at Holy Rank its name becomes Heavenly Suppressing Palm, once, you can make a strike that can deal devastating damage and lock all of the opponent’s stats for several seconds to several dozen seconds, depending on the opponent’s strength."
This was exactly suitable for his fighting style.
A skill that could deal both limited damage and wide-range damage, and especially after reaching Holy Rank, it could basically act as a trump card for him.
Especially locking all of his enemy’s stats for several seconds, those few seconds would be enough for him to take down many enemies.
Lian had almost made his decision, he looked at the three books for a few more seconds and then pointed at the third container without hesitation.
"I’ll take this one."
"I thought you would choose this one, besides, I have this skill myself." Aldric did not even raise an eyebrow.
"Really?" He stayed silent for a moment and looked at the book again, then asked.
"Yes, and mine has reached Holy Rank."
"You managed to evolve it all the way?" He asked this question because upgrading a skill to Holy Rank could require thousands of Fragments.
Of course, it was not always like that, there was also a way to obtain a skill directly at Holy Rank, without needing to upgrade it anymore.
But that method required a Level 100 Awakened who had passed through all five Evolutions, this was the same method Seris had used to obtain her Holy Rank skill.
But he doubted that the Professor had used such a method.

"It took years, as you know, having Holy potential does not mean the skill will wake up one morning and become Holy, it needs thousands of Fragments, many people never reach the final stage even though they have such a skill."
The container opened and Aldric took the book out and gave it to Lian.
"That is why choose carefully."
"I think I just chose." Lian took the book, his fingers touched the image of the palm.
Light came out of the cover of the book, the pages started turning without any wind.
And a moment later, the lines separated from the book and entered his hand.
New information appeared in his mind.
The Mana circulation path, how to compress it, the angle of the palm, the moment of transferring the force.
[New Skill Acquired.]
[Suppressing Palm.]
[Rank: Common (+).]
"Can you show me the peak of this skill?" The young Vorhelm looked at the announcement for a few seconds and then turned back to Aldric.
"Of course, but we can’t do it here, come with me." Then they left the place.
Naturally, they went to one of the training areas, a place built exactly for Awakened to practice new skills and reinforced by various Arrays.
In the middle of it, several testing pillars made of a gray and very dense material were placed.
Each one was made to withstand attacks from high-Level Awakened and they did not break that easily.
Aldric stood in front of one of the pillars, and Lian stood several meters behind him with his arms crossed over his chest.
He expected to see something big, considering the name of the skill, maybe a palm tens of meters large that covered half of the yard.
The Professor only raised his right hand, Mana gathered in front of his palm.
At first it was misty and then became denser, the shape of five fingers appeared inside it, a semi-transparent palm almost two meters tall.
"That’s it?" Vorhelm looked at it for a few seconds.
"Size is important for beginners." Aldric said without looking at him and then moved his palm slightly forward.
The palm also moved and went forward.
Click.
It hit the pillar.
Lian waited, but nothing happened, even the pillar had not moved back a single centimeter, and he raised an eyebrow.
"Are you sure it’s Holy Rank?"
"Come closer." The Professor lowered his hand.
He went forward, the outer surface of the pillar was completely fine, even the place where it had been hit could not be seen.
Aldric placed his index finger on the stone.
Crack.
The outer shell of the pillar shook for a moment and then...collapsed.
The intact stone shell folded inward like an empty piece of cloth, and thousands of gray particles fell from inside it onto the ground.
The entire pillar had turned into powder.
Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly, this time there was no joke in his eyes at all, and the Professor moved his foot through the stone powder.
"When you first learn the skill, you will probably make a twenty-meter palm, put half of your Mana into it, and be very happy that you blew up a wall."
"And when you master it? It no longer needs to be big." He picked up some of the stone powder between two fingers.

"Power that is spread everywhere wastes a large amount of itself. Power that is released at one specific point, at one specific time, and with enough density...can destroy the inside of the target without making any noise."
Lian smiled calmly, this skill could be both loud and quiet, and it completely depended on its user.
But the fact that the Professor used the quiet version made him feel that either he did not like noise, or his base Class was an Assassin.
He was satisfied with his choice, he had chosen it mostly because of its Holy version, which could be a trump card.
But upgrading it was not easy, and this reminded him again that he needed to do something about Fragments, and hunting wolf-like monsters seemed to be the only way.
Nearly an hour later, the two separated

Power that is released at one specific point, at one specific time, and with enough density...can destroy the inside of the target without making any noise."
Lian smiled calmly, this skill could be both loud and quiet, and it completely depended on its user.
But the fact that the Professor used the quiet version made him feel that either he did not like noise, or his base Class was an Assassin.
He was satisfied with his choice, he had chosen it mostly because of its Holy version, which could be a trump card.
But upgrading it was not easy, and this reminded him again that he needed to do something about Fragments, and hunting wolf-like monsters seemed to be the only way.
Nearly an hour later, the two separated

chapters.title: Chapter 458: The Future of the Group
paragraphs: Lian was on his way back to the dormitory when he saw a few familiar faces near the smaller arena.
Rindo, Kain, Seraphina, Liana, Selina, Cassian, and Marcus were still there.
There was no sign of Ethan, he had gone to finalize his recruitment into the Guild he had chosen, he was also a third-year student and did not want to miss such an opportunity.
For the first time in a long while, almost all of them had a few days ahead without any forced missions or tests.
"How does it feel to be popular? All five of the top Guilds in the country were surrounding you." Rindo was the first one to notice him.
"Terrible, if Professor Aldric had not helped me, I would have gone crazy." Lian sighed.
"I still don’t understand why no one saved me." Kain was sitting on a bench beside the path.
"Because watching you suffer was entertaining." Seraphina answered without any guilt.
"Too bad you’re the Vice President of the Student Council, otherwise I would answer you."
"Oh? Looks like you became braver during these nine months, so you don’t dare say anything anymore just because I’m the Vice President?" she snorted, grabbed his ear, and started pulling it.
"Don’t—ow, ow, ow—I’m sorry, stop..."
The discussion quickly turned to their plans for the coming days, and almost all of them agreed on one thing.
A few days of rest and then returning to the Ruined Realm, none of them wanted to stay on Earth for too long, especially after seeing how quickly the other students had grown.
Rodrick was now Level 39, and the others had also improved a lot during their absence.
Although their group was not behind in raw power because of what had happened in the Special Area, no one wanted the Level gap to become bigger.
Rindo was the only one whose plans were more complicated.
He and the other third-year members of the Student Council had basically finished their time at the Academy.
From this point on, they had to decide what to do, joining one of the Associations, accepting an offer from an organization, or continuing their path as an independent Awakened.
He had no shortage of offers, and several large Associations had directly approached him because of his leadership ability, not just his combat power.
But he still had not made a decision.
Liana and Selina did not have the same problem, both of them were just entering their second year and had plenty of time ahead of them.
They had received several offers, but there was no need for them to sign anything yet.
For now, Liana was more interested in her new Griffin than any contract.
"I still don’t even know its abilities properly." She looked at the huge creature beside her.
"I want to know how far it can fly, how long it can fight, and exactly what kinds of food it likes before we return to the Ruined Realm."
"With how fast it eats, the last one is the most important." Kain looked at the Griffin.
"Are you jealous?" Liana frowned.
"Of what? Your food bill?"
Selina laughed.
She also wanted to rest for a few days, organize her skills again, and then return with the others.
But Kain had almost made up his mind.
"Are you seriously going to reject all the offers?" Lian looked at him.
"Probably."
"Even Heavenly Crown?"
"Even them."

"You know what you’re giving up, right? Better mission information, healers, cheaper equipment, private areas, resources, support teams... a lot of things that an independent Awakened has to search for by himself are directly provided by an Association."
"I know." Kain locked his hands behind his head, and a small smile appeared on his face.
"But for nine months, I went wherever I wanted, accepted whatever missions I wanted, and whenever I got tired of seeing people, I just disappeared." His eyes moved away for a moment.
"At first, I was forced to be alone. Then at some point, I realized I liked it."
His voice became a little quieter.

"The freedom I had during these nine months became kind of addictive. I don’t know if I’m ready to explain to someone again where I’m going, what mission I’m accepting, or why I haven’t answered for three weeks."
"But independence has a cost." Rindo added another point this time.
"Yeah. Fewer resources, less support, more danger, and when you get stuck in a mission, there is no group behind you, but at least if I fall into a hole, I chose which hole I fell into."
"That’s an amazing logic." Marcus muttered.
"Thanks."
"That wasn’t a compliment, I said it because it’s stupid, but I understand."
Kain ignored him, and the topic slowly returned to Rodrick.
"For now, we don’t need to worry about him too much." Lian listened to them for a while, then said.
"Rodrick?"
"Yeah. What he had been building for months took a hit today."
"His image of being unbeatable." Rindo immediately understood what he meant.
Vorhelm nodded.
"His network is still there, his resources are still there, and his people aren’t all going to leave him tomorrow morning. But no one thinks anymore that he can’t be stood against."
The Student Council President nodded.
"Exactly." His eyes moved toward the students walking in the distance.

"Until today, for a large part of the Academy, Rodrick’s name alone was enough. If his group made an offer, many people would accept it before even thinking about it, because they didn’t want to become his opponent." His eyes returned to Lian.
"But once fear is broken, building it again is much harder. Rodrick’s network is still powerful, but it can no longer act in the same wide and unrestricted way."
He paused for a few moments.
"In fact, the new problem is that many of those same people may now come after you...I originally wanted Cassian to become the next Student Council President."
Cassian, who was standing beside them, turned his eyes toward him.
"But after today, maybe you’re the only one who can really gather enough votes to stand against Rodrick." Rindo continued without paying attention.
"Me? Student Council President?" Lian stayed silent for a few seconds.
"Do you dislike the position?"

"It’s not about liking it, I need freedom to act. If one day I need to enter a Realm for a month or more, I don’t want ten meetings, signatures, and responsibilities to tie my hands." The young Vorhelm shared his view.
"You don’t need to imagine your coronation ceremony yet. The Student Council President isn’t a prisoner of the Academy." The Student Council President laughed.
Then his expression became serious again.
"But if you don’t want this position, after what happened today, I doubt Cassian still has much of a chance against Rodrick."
"Thank you very much for having this much faith in me." Cassian stared at him for a few seconds.
"I’m just being realistic." Rindo answered without the slightest guilt.
"I know, I really can’t be compared to either of them in popularity right now." He sighed, but he had no desire for this position.
From the beginning, he wanted to become the next Student Council President so he could continue on the same path as his role model.
"Unless Rodrick is miraculously expelled from the Academy before the election." The Student Council President added again.
"Is that even possible?" Liana immediately turned her head.
"Yes and no."
"What kind of answer is that?"
"The Academy is very strict about expelling students, the environment where Awakened are trained naturally allows more fights, injuries, and even breaking some rules than a normal school."
His voice became a little more serious.
"But we have red lines. Some things can no longer be solved with point deductions or punishments."
"For example?" Liana looked at him with curiosity.
"An intentional attempt to kill another student outside the legal conditions of combat."
The smiles disappeared from several faces.
"If it is proven that someone intentionally tried to kill a student, not only can they be expelled immediately, but they may also be directly involved in a criminal case."
"Anyway, I’ll think about the Student Council. The election isn’t tomorrow, it will be held six months from now, so there is plenty of time." Lian added.
"That’s what I wanted to hear, but make your decision sooner, because if you reject it, we have to find a way for Cassian to win." Rindo nodded.
The topic ended there, at least for now, and slowly everyone went their own way.

chapters.title: Chapter 459: Child Of Light
paragraphs: Rindo had to take care of the remaining Student Council work and the graduation process, and Cassian went with him.
Liana took her Griffin with her almost immediately, and Selina also returned with her to their dormitory to rest.
Seraphina also took another path after a short goodbye.
They agreed to coordinate again a few days later for their return to the Ruined Realm.
In the end, only Lian and Kain remained on the way to the dormitory.
"I also want to return to the Ruined Realm as soon as possible, I’ve stayed on Earth much longer than I wanted." The latter added while keeping his hands behind his head.
"Is Level 34 not enough for you?"
"For the First Evolution? No, for the Second Evolution? Very much." Then he looked at the sky.
"I want to reach the Second Evolution as soon as possible. During these past few months, I realized that the longer you wait, the more people will pass you by."
Lian nodded, he could understand this feeling.
"Now that I think about it, you never told me what your evolved Class is." They walked a few more steps before something suddenly came to his mind.
Kain slowly turned his head toward him and looked at him for a few seconds.
"Did you ever tell me what your own Class is?"
"That makes sense." The young Vorhelm did not stop walking, but after a few moments, he laughed.
His friend also laughed, and then his expression became a little more serious.
"Honestly, I don’t know why you’re hiding it and I’m not going to pry. But I’m not stupid, Lian." He looked directly at his friend.
"It has to be related to why your power doesn’t look anything like Level 23, right?"
Lian did not answer, and even his expression did not change.
Kain waited for a few seconds, then shrugged, that silence was enough for him.
"If it’s such an important secret that you won’t even tell me, then keep it hidden. You don’t need to tell me something that could cause trouble for you just to prove that you trust me."
Vorhelm turned his eyes toward him for a moment, and he smiled.
"My Class isn’t as crazy as yours, so I don’t mind telling you."
"My original Class was Mage, three-star, you know that after I obtained the Divine of Light’s Tear, it became four-star."
"Yeah."
"After the Evolution, the name of my Class changed to Follower of Light." He raised his hand, and a very faint golden light appeared around his fingers for a moment.
"But the strangest part isn’t the Class, it’s my Talent." Before the Evolution, Kain only had one main Talent.
A B-Rank Talent called Lesser Pursuit, which allowed him to learn an element by pursuing it, it only had one slot and it had to be one of the four main elements.
Water, Fire, Earth, and Wind, and he could not learn anything outside these four.
But with the First Evolution, its structure had changed almost completely from the foundation.
Greater Pursuit, A-Rank.
This Talent even allowed him to learn elements by pursuing them, and learn them in the form of innate skills, and he was no longer limited to the four main elements.
It also had four slots, and he could learn up to four elements at the same time.
Basically, he could Pursuit almost anything.
"And not only that, in the end I got a second Talent." Kain finally said.
Kain opened his palm, and the golden light appeared again, but this time it was purer, as if it was the most real and pure form of light.
[Child of Light]
[Rank: A]

"It increases my compatibility with Light, learning and using Light skills has become easier for me, their Mana cost is lower, and I also have more resistance against corruption and dark energy." Kain said.
He paused for a few moments.
"I can even turn Mana into Light."
Lian stayed silent for a short time, and then the pieces easily came together.
"Divine of Light, you only absorbed one drop of its tear and it caused all these changes."
"I thought about it too." Kain gave a short laugh.

"Then your three-star Class became four-star, its entire Evolution path turned toward Light, your previous Talent completely changed, and a new A-Rank Talent appeared too, it is unlikely to be a coincidence."
"Do you think it only changed the First Evolution? Or is it going to change my entire Evolution path?"
"I don’t know, but something that only one drop of it was able to change the structure of your Class probably didn’t end its effect with the First Evolution." Lian added.
"That means my Second Evolution path may have changed too, if that is really the case, I’d like to know what I will become in the end." Kain looked at the Light that remained on his fingers.
"If possible, you should research it more, if this effect really came from the Divine of Light, it would be better to understand exactly what changed inside your body before the Second Evolution."
Kain nodded, he had the same idea and wanted to do the same thing, he stayed silent for a few seconds and then suddenly laughed.
"What do you think the natives of the Ruined Realm did when they found out that I absorbed one drop of their sacred being’s tear?"
"Their fanatics? They probably want to kill you." The young Vorhelm did not even need to think.
"Very hopeful." He laughed loudly.
"But those fanatics probably have the most information about the Divine of Light, if you can get information from them without getting killed, you might understand where your Class is really going."
Kain sighed.
"That ’without getting killed’ part is the problem, they don’t like us at all. The people of the two worlds have fought each other several times before, and their forces aren’t weak either.
Lian knew about this.
But his next sentence made his expression change slightly.
"I also heard something else recently. Some of the Crystals needed to cleanse the Ruined Realm may be inside the human areas there."
"This is the first time I’m hearing this, where did you get that from?" Lian turned his head toward him.
"It is just an internet rumor and has no basis." Kain’s smile had completely disappeared.

"But if it is true, at least some Crystals are located in an area controlled by the natives. That means if we need all of them to close the Realm, one day we’ll have to deal with them... or take them from them."
The young Vorhelm said nothing for a few seconds, this was no longer just about an unknown civilization, the Crystals were directly connected to the fate of the Ruined Realm and their world.
"If it is true, things will become much more complicated."
"Yeah, we need the Crystals to cleanse the Realm, but maybe we’ll have to enter an area where its owners won’t even be happy to see us just to get them."
"At least it isn’t our problem for now." Lian let out a quiet breath.
"That was very responsible of you."
"It’s realistic, this issue is above our Level of involvement. Until the Federation or the governments decide what to do, two students aren’t going to negotiate with another civilization."
Kain looked at him for a few seconds and nodded, the issue of cleansing and closing the Ruined Realm was not their responsibility for now.
Besides, they still had 24 years.
They had gotten close to the dormitory building when the phone inside Lian’s pocket vibrated.
Once.
Twice.
He took it out, and a name was shown on the screen.
Commander Gareth.
His steps became a little slower, and then he answered the phone.
"Commander, it’s been a while."
There was no sound for a few moments...then Gareth’s voice came from the other side.
"Is your test over?" His tone was not normal and was more serious than his usual calls, and he went straight to the main point.
"Yes, a little while ago."
"Good, then if you’re free, I need your help." This time the silence on the other side lasted a little longer, and then he added.
"About that same white-eyed man we captured."
"I sent people to bring you here. appreciate it if you came and helped us understand why this man... is waiting for you."

He took it out, and a name was shown on the screen.
Commander Gareth.
His steps became a little slower, and then he answered the phone.
"Commander, it’s been a while."
There was no sound for a few moments...then Gareth’s voice came from the other side.
"Is your test over?" His tone was not normal and was more serious than his usual calls, and he went straight to the main point.
"Yes, a little while ago."
"Good, then if you’re free, I need your help." This time the silence on the other side lasted a little longer, and then he added.
"About that same white-eyed man we captured."
"I sent people to bring you here. appreciate it if you came and helped us understand why this man... is waiting for you."

chapters.title: Chapter 460: Beneath the Mountain
paragraphs: The black military vehicle had been driving away from the Academy for almost forty minutes.
Lian was sitting in the back seat and looking outside through the dark window.
For the past twenty minutes, even his phone had lost all signs of connection, and the route the driver had chosen had been far away from any public road for a long time.
He did not ask the driver where they were going.
Gareth had personally sent people to pick him up, and that alone was enough to show that their destination was not a place whose coordinates they would give to just anyone.
The narrow road turned between two rocky slopes, and a few minutes later, the view in front of them almost filled his entire field of vision.
It was a mountain, there were no buildings around it, no watchtowers, no fences, not even a single guard, but only a huge wall of gray stone that rose hundreds of meters into the sky.
The vehicle moved directly toward it without slowing down.
He raised an eyebrow, the distance became smaller.
One hundred meters.
Seventy meters.
Fifty meters.
And right at that moment, he felt something, the flow of Mana inside his body became heavy for a moment.
Lian sat a little straighter and looked through the mountain rocks, nothing could be seen with his eyes, but his senses were telling him something else.
Hundreds of Arrays were layered across the entire mountain, some of them were on the surface, some were deep inside, and some were so thin and wide that even finding their borders was not easy.

Resistance Arrays that strengthened the entire structure of the mountain, defensive Arrays, concealment Arrays, and Arrays that redirected Mana and did not allow anyone outside to feel the amount of energy inside the mountain.
And among all of them, the Mana Suppression Arrays caught his attention more than the others.
He had not even entered yet, but he could already feel his Mana moving a little slower than normal, and the closer the vehicle got, the stronger the pressure became.
He gave the driver a short look, the man did not react at all.
It was clear that this was not his first time.
If someone did not know the exact coordinates of this place, even if they flew directly over the mountain, they would probably see nothing more than a normal mountain range.
Even a powerful Awakened would easily pass by it if they were not intentionally looking for a sign.
But what was hidden inside was not normal, this was without a doubt one of the safest places in the entire country.
The vehicle was only twenty meters away from the wall when very thin lines of light suddenly appeared on the stone.
Hundreds of lines connected to each other in a fraction of a second, and a large part of the wall moved inward without making any mechanical sound.

The mountain itself had moved aside, and a dark tunnel appeared in front of them, the vehicle entered, and three seconds later, the lines of light behind them disappeared and the stone returned to its original position.
Natural light completely disappeared, and white lights on the ceiling of the tunnel turned on one after another.
Lian looked behind him, there was no sign of the entrance anymore.
"Very well hidden." He said quietly.
"It is not supposed to be found, Mr. Vorhelm." The driver answered for the first time since they left.
Lian gave a faint smile.
"With this many Arrays, I think even if someone finds it, getting inside would be the harder part."
The driver did not answer this time...perhaps because he did not disagree.
The tunnel continued for almost five hundred meters, and then the first checkpoint appeared.
Black metal walls completely blocked the path, and they only moved aside after several white beams passed over the vehicle.
[Vehicle Identity Confirmed.]
[Passengers Confirmed.]
[Checking.]
[Unregistered Living Being: Not Found.]
[External Hidden Space: Not Found.]
Lian kept his eyes on one of the notifications, the system was even checking for hidden storage spaces or hidden living beings.
This made him unconsciously think about his own Colony Space, more precisely, about One, the creature that was somehow inside him.
Could the mountain’s defense system detect her?
But there was no reaction, apparently, what was connected to his own existence was not detected as a normal external space.
The first gate opened.
Then the second.
The third.
At the fourth checkpoint, the Mana Suppression suddenly doubled, and he frowned for a moment.
In this area, the flow of Mana had not stopped and it was not completely suppressed either, but it clearly felt heavy.
If someone tried to suddenly activate a powerful skill, several Arrays would probably react at the same moment.
The farther they went, the clearer it became that the security of this place did not depend on one wall or one guard.
Layer after layer, and if someone passed through one, ten more were waiting for them...
After the final gate, the tunnel suddenly ended.
And the space in front of them opened up.

The young Vorhelm said nothing for a few seconds, the inside of the mountain had been almost completely hollowed out, and a huge space, with a height that easily reached several hundred meters, had been built inside the stone.
Dozens of metal floors had been built along the inner walls, and narrow and wide bridges connected them to each other.
Vertical elevators moved up and down along the central pillars.
There were separate paths for vehicles.
On the higher floors, glass observation rooms watched over the entire facility like silent eyes.
Hundreds of security and military forces were moving through different areas, and several-meter-wide doors opened into unknown hallways.
Blue lines of energy passed through the ceiling, floor, and walls, and the entire structure worked calmly and in an organized way like a living thing.
Even so, there was no chaos, everyone knew where they needed to be and what they needed to do.
He looked around through the window, this place was not just a prison, its scale was much larger than that.
Some areas were clearly built for holding prisoners, and in some floors, research equipment could be seen behind glass.
And several paths also led to areas where, even from this distance, he could feel the heavy protective Arrays around them.
They were probably keeping objects, creatures, or people there that the Federation was not even willing to allow in a normal facility.
"So this is the place..."
The vehicle moved through the inner paths for a few more minutes and finally stopped in front of a metal platform, the driver got out and opened the back door.
"We’re here, Mr. Vorhelm."
Lian got out of the vehicle, the Mana pressure was stronger here, but it was still not painful, although he was sure that the moment he used Mana, something interesting would happen.
Even the security of the Vorhelm family was not at this level, although his family was so proud and arrogant that they believed no one would dare to enter their territory.
And they were not completely wrong, at least until today, no one had dared to.
Several people were waiting in front of the vehicle.
They were wearing official security uniforms, and each of them looked at least more dangerous than their appearance suggested.
But his eyes quickly stopped on a woman at the front of the group, he knew her.
Rina.
Gareth’s deputy, the same serious attitude, the same cold eyes, and almost the same expression that made it seem like smiling was an unnecessary part of life.
The woman took one step forward.
"Mr. Vorhelm, welcome. The Commander is waiting for you." She greeted him with a short nod.
"Ms. Rina. It has been a while." Lian also lowered his head slightly.
"Yes, anyway, the Commander is waiting for you on the third underground floor."
He looked around once more while walking with them.
"This is a lot of security for someone who is only supposed to talk to a prisoner."
"His prisoner is not normal." Rina did not even turn her head.
The young Vorhelm said nothing this time, she was right, they were talking about a creature whose existence in this world should not even be possible.
The elevator was large enough for almost twenty people to stand inside comfortably.
The woman placed her identification on the screen.
The doors closed.
[Access Level Confirmed.]
[Destination: Underground Floor Three.]
The elevator started moving down, and the numbers changed.
Zero.
Minus one.
Lian felt the Mana Suppression pressure increase.
Minus two.
More.
The flow of Mana in his body was still under control, but now it felt like it was moving through a thick liquid.
If the higher floors were designed to control normal people, this place was built for those who had no meaning for the word "normal."
Minus three.
Click.
The doors opened.
Gareth was standing directly behind the doors, and when he saw him, he gave a short smile.
"I’m glad you could come."
"Commander, I hope you didn’t have to wait long."
"Not too long." Gareth gave Rina and the others a short look. "Thank you. I’ll take him from here. You can go back."
"Yes, Commander." His deputy nodded without asking any questions.
The group entered the elevator again, the doors closed, and the two of them were left alone.
The Commander started walking toward one of the long hallways, and Lian walked beside him.
The walls of this floor were almost completely black, and at regular distances, heavy doors could be seen on both sides of the hallway.
There were no names on any of them, only numbers, the two walked in silence for a few moments until the man finally looked at the young man.
"To be honest, I’d really like to sit down with you one day and hear about your adventures myself."
Lian raised an eyebrow.

"Every time your name reaches my ears, there’s always some strange report attached to it, when I first saw you in that fallen border city, I already knew a bright future was waiting for you...but you’ve surprised me, and you’ve gone far beyond what I expected."

chapters.title: Chapter 461: Overlord Orion
paragraphs: "I think telling you all of them would take a long time." Lian gave a faint smile, he could feel the surprise and amazement in the Commander’s voice.

And he could understand it, besides the rumors about the Special Area, there was also his achievement in defending Base #3, along with what had happened in the Vorhelm family during his sister’s birthday ceremony.
These were things that reached the Commander’s ears, and when the center of all these events was an eighteen-year-old, it was hard to ignore him.
He could only hope that this man would not try even harder than before to recruit him into the army.
"That is why I said one day, for now, we have something more important."
Lian also became more serious, it was clear that they had finally reached the real reason for his presence here.
Gareth took a few more steps.
"The white-eyed man has been in our hands for a while, long enough that we have tried almost every normal interrogation method on him."
"Professional interrogators, behavior experts, Awakened with lie-detection skills, psychological pressure, isolation... even a few other methods that I would rather not go into."
"And none of them worked?" The young Vorhelm looked at him.
"Almost none."
"You couldn’t force him to talk?"
The Commander’s steps slowed for a moment and he stayed silent for a few seconds... then he let out a quiet breath.
"He is a madman, Lian." His tone sounded more tired than angry.
"You can force a normal person with something. Fear, pain, money, freedom, family, benefits, threats... in the end, you can find something that matters to them."
He looked at him for a moment.
"But how do you force a madman when the things that matter to him don’t make any sense at all?"
Lian became silent, he had met that man once and knew that he was truly a madman.
Gareth continued.
"We tried many methods. Every time, he either stays silent or starts saying the same nonsense. Sometimes he talks for hours about things that have nothing to do with the question."
The face of the white-eyed man appeared in Lian’s mind.

The border city, that strange smile, those completely white eyes, and the sentences that were sometimes so crazy and unrelated that it was impossible to know whether he was really insane or only pretending.
And of course, that strange monster, a creature that looked nothing like normal monsters, he had created a monster and called it a masterpiece.
He said that masterpiece was going to save humanity, a creature that was clearly made to kill people.
How could it save people?
"You are right. It was the same when I first saw him, so how did you capture him in the end?" He finally said.
"We didn’t capture him." Gareth did not answer immediately.
"No?" Lian turned his eyes toward him.
"No, one of the Overlords captured him."
The young Vorhelm’s steps slowed for a moment.
An Overlord.
This title was not easily given to every powerful Awakened, Overlords were at least Level 80 and had completed all four Evolutions.
At that stage, the gap between them and normal Awakened was no longer a matter of a few Levels, each one of them was considered a strategic force on their own.
People whose presence alone could change the fate of a continent, extremely powerful beings who had almost reached the top of the world’s power.
Even seeing them was not something common, they could not be easily seen whenever you wanted.
"Oh? Even an Overlord got involved in this?" Lian asked with curiosity.
"This matter is much more important to the Federation than you think." Gareth looked at him.
"Which Overlord?"
"Overlord Orion."
"The same Mountain Breaker?"
"Himself."
For the second time in a few minutes, the Commander had managed to surprise him.
Orion was not just a normal Overlord, almost every Awakened knew his name.
Fifteen years ago, during one of the country’s worst Rift incidents, an entire region went out of control in less than an hour.
This region included eleven countries and the Rift that opened there contained tens of thousands of monsters.
Hundreds of waves of monsters passed through the Rift one after another and the defensive lines fell one after another.
Eleven countries were close to falling, if it had really happened, it would have become one of the darkest disasters in human history.
But Overlord Orion had almost alone held the main path where the monsters were entering for several hours and had managed to suppress almost all the waves by himself.
And the reason for his title, Mountain Breaker, came from a skill called Mountain Breaker, and with the help of that skill, he had eventually managed to suppress tens of thousands of monsters alone.
They said that with that skill, he could split hundreds of mountains with one punch, and with the wave created from it, he had slaughtered the monsters.
People like him did not move to capture a normal criminal, in fact, someone like him did not move to capture any criminal.
"The Federation sent the Mountain Breaker to capture one person?"
"Now you understand why I said it was important." Gareth gave a very faint smile.
"Not completely."
"Do you remember that creature he made in the border city?"
"It is hard to forget." Lian gave him a short look.
"We examined its remains, it was a masterpiece."

"A masterpiece? That madman also called that thing a masterpiece, from my point of view, because it was almost immortal and I could not even kill it in the end, maybe it can be called a masterpiece, but what makes you call it a masterpiece, Commander?"
"Its organs had not formed naturally. The tissues of several different creatures had been combined inside one body, but its body did not reject them."

"The energy paths inside its body were man-made, exactly like weaving a handmade carpet, and it had a Core that showed no sign of natural formation, and even though it had only one Core, its quality was equal to the Core of an Unholy."
After a short pause, he added.
"But even that was not the strangest part, the System officially identified that creature as a monster, a monster."
Lian said nothing, this was not a small difference, that man had not simply put several body parts together and forced them to stay alive.
He had created something that even the System had accepted as a real creature, he also remembered that the System had recognized it, but at that time he had been too busy to care about such a thing.
And this immediately created several more questions in his mind.
If the System registered those creations as monsters... how would Gluttony deal with them?
Butcher?
If he killed that creature, could he extract a skill from its artificial body?
Even the Devourer Egg needed monster corpses to grow.
And what about his Talent, how would Colony Sovereign deal with it? Could it add that creature to his own Colony?
If those creatures really belonged to the same category... the matter was much more interesting than he had first thought.
"Did you think of something?" Gareth noticed the small change in his eyes.
Lian shrugged.
"Just that if the System considers them monsters, then his work goes far beyond combining several creatures together."
"Exactly, that is why after receiving the final report, the Federation decided to capture him alive no matter what."
Lian looked at him.
Gareth also looked at him for a few moments, and during that exchange of looks, he found the answer himself.
"You want his knowledge, right? You want to understand how he made something like that."
"Exactly."
This time the young Vorhelm’s expression became clearer, a look that contained surprise and a big "Really?" in it.
The Commander gave a faint smile.
"I understand why you are looking at me like that."
"I just didn’t think the Federation was interested in learning how to make monsters."
"Why wouldn’t we be?"
Lian said nothing.
"Almost half of the things we use today as normal Awakened technology once came from the Ruined Realms." Gareth continued.
As they walked, he counted a few things with his fingers.
"The Blacksmith profession, the Array Master profession, the Rune Master profession, some fighting methods, Golem making, and these are only the famous and popular professions."
His expression became more serious.

"For two hundred and fifty years, humanity has been taking everything it learns from the Ruined Realms, absorbing it, and turning it into our own things. If a new method can increase our power, we have no reason to ignore it just because it came from another civilization."
"That makes sense." The young Vorhelm nodded slightly, he was not against progress either, after all, learning something like this could make them stronger and help them end this apocalypse sooner.
"The first time we met a civilization in the Ninth Ruined Realm, it was a small civilization that called themselves the Volkari." The Commander continued.
"As you know, the civilizations of the Ruined Realms do not always follow our power system."
The young Vorhelm nodded, this was nothing new.
Every Ruined Realm had its own laws, power paths, and civilizations.
Something that was considered normal on Earth could be completely meaningless in another realm.
Even the System, Levels, Skills, Classes, and Talents were specific to them.
"For the Volkari, the power of their own bodies was never the main standard, but what they created was."
"They created monsters. Biological creatures. They combined tissues, changed Cores, designed paths for Mana to move through, and placed the traits of different creatures inside one body."
His voice became slightly lower.

"A Volkari might not be as dangerous as a normal warrior in direct combat, but if he is a good creator, he might have three or four monsters beside him, and each one of them could slaughter an entire group."
"So they measure their power by what they create, that reminds me of Summoners to some degree, except they do not make their own monsters." Lian said.
"Exactly, the white-eyed man is one of them." Gareth paused for a moment.
Now more pieces came together.
His behavior, his knowledge about monsters, that creature he called a masterpiece, and the reason the Federation had been willing to involve an Overlord to capture him.

"This matter is much more important to the Federation than you think." Gareth looked at him.
"Which Overlord?"
"Overlord Orion."
"The same Mountain Breaker?"
"Himself."
For the second time in a few minutes, the Commander had managed to surprise him.
Orion was not just a normal Overlord, almost every Awakened knew his name.
Fifteen years ago, during one of the country’s worst Rift incidents, an entire region went out of control in less than an hour.
This region included eleven countries and the Rift that opened there contained tens of thousands of monsters.
Hundreds of waves of monsters passed through the Rift one after another and the defensive lines fell one after another.
Eleven countries were close to falling, if it had really happened, it would have become one of the darkest disasters in human history.
But Overlord Orion had almost alone held the main path where the monsters were entering for several hours and had managed to suppress almost all the waves by himself.
And the reason for his title, Mountain Breaker, came from a skill called Mountain Breaker, and with the help of that skill, he had eventually managed to suppress tens of thousands of monsters alone.
They said that with that skill, he could split hundreds of mountains with one punch, and with the wave created from it, he had slaughtered the monsters.
People like him did not move to capture a normal criminal, in fact, someone like him did not move to capture any criminal.
"The Federation sent the Mountain Breaker to capture one person?"
"Now you understand why I said it was important." Gareth gave a very faint smile.
"Not completely."
"Do you remember that creature he made in the border city?"
"It is hard to forget." Lian gave him a short look.
"We examined its remains, it was a masterpiece."
"A masterpiece?

That madman also called that thing a masterpiece, from my point of view, because it was almost immortal and I could not even kill it in the end, maybe it can be called a masterpiece, but what makes you call it a masterpiece, Commander?"
"Its organs had not formed naturally.
The tissues of several different creatures had been combined inside one body, but its body did not reject them."

"The energy paths inside its body were man-made, exactly like weaving a handmade carpet, and it had a Core that showed no sign of natural formation, and even though it had only one Core, its quality was equal to the Core of an Unholy."
After a short pause, he added.
"But even that was not the strangest part, the System officially identified that creature as a monster, a monster."
Lian said nothing, this was not a small difference, that man had not simply put several body parts together and forced them to stay alive.
He had created something that even the System had accepted as a real creature, he also remembered that the System had recognized it, but at that time he had been too busy to care about such a thing.
And this immediately created several more questions in his mind.
If the System registered those creations as monsters... how would Gluttony deal with them?
Butcher?
If he killed that creature, could he extract a skill from its artificial body?
Even the Devourer Egg needed monster corpses to grow.
And what about his Talent, how would Colony Sovereign deal with it?
Could it add that creature to his own Colony?
If those creatures really belonged to the same category... the matter was much more interesting than he had first thought.
"Did you think of something?" Gareth noticed the small change in his eyes.
Lian shrugged.
"Just that if the System considers them monsters, then his work goes far beyond combining several creatures together."
"Exactly, that is why after receiving the final report, the Federation decided to capture him alive no matter what."
Lian looked at him.
Gareth also looked at him for a few moments, and during that exchange of looks, he found the answer himself.
"You want his knowledge, right?
You want to understand how he made something like that."
"Exactly."
This time the young Vorhelm’s expression became clearer, a look that contained surprise and a big "Really?" in it.
The Commander gave a faint smile.
"I understand why you are looking at me like that."
"I just didn’t think the Federation was interested in learning how to make monsters."
"Why wouldn’t we be?"
Lian said nothing.
"Almost half of the things we use today as normal Awakened technology once came from the Ruined Realms." Gareth continued.
As they walked, he counted a few things with his fingers.
"The Blacksmith profession, the Array Master profession, the Rune Master profession, some fighting methods, Golem making, and these are only the famous and popular professions."
His expression became more serious.
"For two hundred and fifty years, humanity has been taking everything it learns from the Ruined Realms, absorbing it, and turning it into our own things.
If a new method can increase our power, we have no reason to ignore it just because it came from another civilization."
"That makes sense." The young Vorhelm nodded slightly, he was not against progress either, after all, learning something like this could make them stronger and help them end this apocalypse sooner.
"The first time we met a civilization in the Ninth Ruined Realm, it was a small civilization that called themselves the Volkari." The Commander continued.
"As you know, the civilizations of the Ruined Realms do not always follow our power system."
The young Vorhelm nodded, this was nothing new.
Every Ruined Realm had its own laws, power paths, and civilizations.
Something that was considered normal on Earth could be completely meaningless in another realm.
Even the System, Levels, Skills, Classes, and Talents were specific to them.
"For the Volkari, the power of their own bodies was never the main standard, but what they created was."
"They created monsters.
Biological creatures.
They combined tissues, changed Cores, designed paths for Mana to move through, and placed the traits of different creatures inside one body."
His voice became slightly lower.

"A Volkari might not be as dangerous as a normal warrior in direct combat, but if he is a good creator, he might have three or four monsters beside him, and each one of them could slaughter an entire group."
"So they measure their power by what they create, that reminds me of Summoners to some degree, except they do not make their own monsters." Lian said.
"Exactly, the white-eyed man is one of them." Gareth paused for a moment.
Now more pieces came together.
His behavior, his knowledge about monsters, that creature he called a masterpiece, and the reason the Federation had been willing to involve an Overlord to capture him.

chapters.title: Chapter 462: The Greatest Monster Maker I
paragraphs: "But the more we studied this man’s creations, the more we realized that we were not dealing with an ordinary Volkari."
"How good is he?" Lian asked.
Gareth stayed silent for a few seconds.
"Probably the best monster creator we have ever seen from their civilization."
He understood the importance of the prisoner behind those walls, if what the commander said was true, that man was not just a crazy person from a strange civilization.
He might have part of a knowledge that, if the Federation gained access to it, could affect the power of all humanity.
They walked a few more steps in silence.
"So what exactly do you want from me?"
"Get him to talk." Gareth answered without going around the subject.
"That’s it?" Lian raised an eyebrow.
"That simple thing that everyone in this base has failed to do, plus there are three main things we want."
He raised his first finger.

"First, see if you can find out what he wants in exchange for cooperation. He doesn’t have to give us all his knowledge right away. Even if we only find out what can convince him, we will have taken one step forward."
His second finger.
"Second, find out if there are other people like him in our world."
His expression became more serious.

"This part is even more important for security than his monster-making knowledge. We are not comfortable with the idea that people from the Ruined Realms might be living inside our cities without us knowing."
Then his third finger.
"And finally, find out how he entered our world."
"I thought he entered through the cracks." The young Vorhelm slightly frowned.
"That was our first guess too."
"But?"
"We have no evidence." Gareth slowly shook his head.
Lian said nothing for a few moments, cracks or rifts were one of the best-known results of failures in the Ruined Realm.
The exact conditions for opening them were not always the same.
If the clearing of a dungeon in the Ruined Realm failed, the monsters inside could enter Earth through a crack.
The death of a certain number of Awakened could cause a crack to open.
Some events had their own special conditions, sometimes no one even knew which condition had been activated until the crack opened.
But the result was almost always the same, a path between the two worlds opened and monsters entered Earth.
Lian had thought from the beginning that the white-eyed man had somehow entered along with one of these waves.
At that time, because they had guessed that not only monsters but also people from the Ruined Realms might enter through the cracks, even he had become worried.
Because if that was true, all their knowledge about the Ruined Realms would be called into question.
But it seemed the Federation was still not sure that such a thing was possible, or it simply was not willing to accept it.
"Our guess might be correct. There is even a high chance, but a possibility is not enough." Gareth said.
Lian understood what he meant.
If the white-eyed man had found another way to travel between the worlds and if others also knew that way, the Federation’s security problem would be much bigger than a few cracks.
The problem was that there was a large civilization in the Tenth Ruined Realm and they did not want to take the risk that the people of this realm might also find a way to enter their world.
That was why, to make sure something like that would not happen, they had to identify the way itself as soon as possible.
"I understand, but I won’t promise that I can get anything out of him." He slowly nodded his head.
"I’m not expecting a miracle."
"But I’ll try."
"Thank you, Mr. Vorhelm." Gareth smiled.
"Mr.?" Lian turned his eyes toward him.
"You’re trying so hard to help us, I should show you a little respect."
For a few seconds, the weight of the conversation became lighter, but another question was still in his mind.
"Anyway... how are the cracks these days?"
The commander’s smile disappeared immediately and a short frown appeared between his eyebrows.
"Bad, very bad." These two words were enough to make the young Vorhelm serious.
"The number of cracks opening is higher than we expected. Not a little higher... significantly higher."
They passed another security door.

"Several small cities have fallen. We took some of them back, some are still in the hands of monsters. The army, Guilds and independent groups are constantly moving around, but the main problem is the number of fronts."
"How is it compared to the previous Ruined Realms?" Lian asked.
Gareth frowned.
"The number of monsters that have entered Earth from the Tenth Ruined Realm during this same period is much higher than what we saw in the first year of several previous realms."

He became silent for a moment, this comparison was not a small thing, the Tenth Ruined Realm was still new, if the pressure was already this high at the beginning, what would happen in the following years?
"Don’t you have a plan to prevent the cities from falling?"
"We do. That’s why no major city has fallen so far."
The commander locked his fingers behind his back.

"The defense networks of the main cities are on the highest level of alert. We have quick response groups, the Guilds have given their required number of forces, the army has moved more units and the warning systems are constantly being improved."
Then he let out a short sigh.
"The problem is the small cities. You can’t keep a permanent army, several high-level Awakened and a defense system as strong as the capital in every small city. Resources are limited."
His tone became heavier.
"The governments are sending forces, the Federation is doing the same, the Guilds are also helping whenever they can, but there are not just one or two problems."
With every step, his voice became more serious.

"The cracks are one problem. The Ruined Realm itself is another. Dungeons, evacuating people, moving resources, defending cities, taking back fallen areas... all of them need forces at the same time."
He stayed silent for a few moments and this time his silence was different from before, as if he did not want to say the next sentence.
"What is it?" Lian noticed.
Gareth did not answer for several steps ...then he slowly said.
"What bothers me the most is that I feel this is still only the beginning."
The young Vorhelm looked at him and this time he did not stop either.
"If this continues, we might face the hardest test humanity has seen in these two hundred and fifty years."
He paused for a moment and then said something that even made Lian’s steps slow for a moment.
"Maybe even something on the level of the Forbidden Era.
He said nothing.
The Forbidden Era.
It was not a name that someone would easily say in a normal conversation.
Even several decades later, history books still recorded a large part of the information from that era in a different way from normal events.
An era when a Demon had entered their world.
And the presence of that single creature had been enough to cause the fall of a continent.
A continent!
Even now, more than 150 years later, parts of that disaster had still not been completely repaired.
Lian only looked at the hallway in front of him for a few seconds, if a student made such a comparison, it might be called an exaggeration.
But Gareth was a commander who saw the real reports about cracks, casualties, fallen areas and the situation on the fronts.
If he was talking about the Forbidden Era, it meant that what normal people knew about the current situation was probably only a small part of the real picture.
"Commander, what do you mean by—" He opened his mouth.
Gareth suddenly stopped, Lian also became silent... there was no longer a long hallway in front of them, instead, a huge black door covered the entire wall.
It was almost four meters tall and there was no normal handle or opening on its surface.
Several array circles were carved into the metal, some for restraint, some for resistance and several other arrays were so complex that their purpose was not clear.
Two armed guards were standing on both sides of the door and both immediately moved aside when they saw the commander.
But what caught Lian’s attention the most was the pressure, the mana suppression arrays in this area were several times stronger.
The mana inside his body was still moving, but it had become extremely heavy.
Even activating a powerful skill here would probably be several times harder than normal, in fact, it was completely impossible, he could not even activate a skill here.
Gareth looked at him.
"We’ll talk about the rest later."
Then he placed his palm on the identification panel beside the door and a thin white line moved across the panel.
[Identity confirmed.]
Click.
The first lock was released, the light on one of the array circles went out.
Click.
The second lock.
Then the third.
Each time, the sound of the heavy lock opening echoed through the hallway, louder than the one before, and finally all the lines on the door turned white for a few seconds.
He lowered his hand.
"It’s here."
Vorhelm kept his eyes on the black door.
Behind these few meters of metal and arrays was the same man who, among everyone in this base, had asked to speak to only one person.
Him.
"The white-eyed man’s cell."
