chapters.title: Chapter 463: The Greatest Monster Maker II
paragraphs: "The White-Eyed Man’s cell." Gareth said in a low voice.
Click.
The last lock was released.

The huge black door first moved a few centimeters backward, the sound of heavy mechanisms moving inside the wall filled the area, and a moment later, the entire several-ton door slowly moved to the left.
Lian expected the cell to be directly behind it, but what appeared in front of him was another small room.

The walls of the observation room were almost completely black, and only a few white mana lines ran across the ceiling and floor, in front of them, several layers of glass covered the entire wall; dozens of small arrays were shining between its layers.
The White-Eyed Man’s cell was behind it, and the room was almost empty.
There was a metal table, two chairs, four gray walls, and there was no bed, no extra object, and not even something that could be broken and used as a weapon.
The White-Eyed Man was sitting on the chair on the other side of the table.
His wrists were locked with black mana suppression rings, two more rings were around his ankles, and a thicker ring was around his neck.
Short chains connected each of them to the chair and the floor.

Even so, his appearance did not look like a prisoner at all, he was leaning against the back of the chair, his shoulders were relaxed and his head was slightly lowered; as if he was not sitting in one of the safest prisons in the country, but sitting in his own home waiting for a guest who was late.
Gareth had only taken one step into the observation room when the man moved, his head rose, before the inner door of the cell had even opened.
His completely white eyes locked directly onto Vorhelm through the several layers of glass.
Only him.
He stayed silent for a few seconds and then a calm smile appeared on his face.
"You finally came." He said in an almost happy tone.
"I heard you missed me." Lian looked at him for a few seconds without changing his expression.
The man’s lips opened and a short, strange laugh came from his throat.
"Missed you? No, no..." The White-Eyed Man seriously shook his head, as if he was truly correcting an important mistake.
"That’s not a good word. I was curious. Very curious."
He slowly tilted his head to one side and his eyes moved across Lian’s body.
"I wanted to see how much my little piece has grown."
The inner door opened with Gareth’s approval, and the pressure from the mana suppression arrays inside the cell immediately became several times stronger.
As Lian crossed the entrance, he felt the mana inside his body become like a thick and useless liquid.
The commander also entered with him, and the White-Eyed Man did not take his eyes off Vorhelm.
"I said I wanted to talk to the boy." He said this time in a bored tone.
"And I’m staying here." Gareth stood beside the table.
The White-Eyed Man turned his white eyes toward him, looked at him for two seconds, and then simply shrugged.
"Okay." And he became silent.
Gareth waited.
Five seconds.
Ten seconds.
Fifteen seconds.
The White-Eyed Man only smiled at him, not a single word, not even an extra movement, he was completely silent.
The commander narrowed his eyes and understood what he was trying to do.
"Don’t think you can make demands from us in your current situation.
The White-Eyed Man slightly pursed his lips.
"I didn’t make a demand, I said I wanted to talk to him. You stayed, so I don’t talk." He slightly tilted his head.
"See? It’s very simple, even children can understand it."
A thin vein appeared beside Gareth’s temple, Lian felt that if this continued for a few more minutes, the interrogation would probably end before it even started.
He turned his eyes toward the commander.
"Let me try. Everything is being recorded, right?"
Gareth looked at him for a few seconds, it was clear that he did not like this decision, but in the end he nodded.
"Image, sound, mana changes, and every movement inside the room are recorded. The arrays are also active, and if anything happens, the forces outside will enter in less than one second."
Then he fixed his eyes on the White-Eyed Man.
"And I’ll also be right behind this glass."
"How reassuring." The madman said with a smile.
The commander ignored him and looked at Lian again before leaving.
"If he makes even the smallest move, you don’t need to play the hero."
The young Vorhelm nodded, and he left the cell, closing the door behind him.
Click.
The locks became active again, and now only two people remained inside the room.
Lian pulled back the chair across from the man and sat down, neither of them said anything for a few seconds, the quiet sound of the room’s air system was the only thing breaking the silence.
The White-Eyed Man was looking at him, but not like someone looking at another person’s face.
First, he examined his fingers, then his forearms, shoulders, chest, neck, and finally his eyes.
That look was less human than it was like the look of a surgeon seeing his favorite test subject again after several months.
And the young Vorhelm allowed it to continue for a few seconds before speaking calmly.
"If you’re only going to look at me, you could have asked for a picture."
"Pictures don’t breathe." The man answered without even thinking.
"Why did you want to see me?"
"I told you, I missed my remaining piece."
Lian said nothing, he only looked at him.
Three seconds.
Five seconds.
Eight seconds.
The man’s smile slowly disappeared. Then he moved his head back with childish annoyance.
"Ugh...you’re so boring, you don’t even play a little." He complained under his breath.
In the next moment, that annoyance disappeared from his face, as if it had never existed, and his bound fingers began tapping on the table.
Click.
Click.
Click.
"I only came back to take my masterpiece back, they took it. They cut it into pieces, cut it, measured it, looked at it, opened it up..."
His face became slightly angry for a moment.
"You’re very nosy."
Lian thought about the border city, that strange monster the White-Eyed Man proudly called his masterpiece.
And the conversation they had that same day, the man had asked him for something, his body, he had asked him to become part of the monster.
Had this madman brought him here again because of something like that?
"But you’re still missing one piece, let me guess." He finally said calmly.
The tapping of his fingers stopped and the man’s white eyes shone slightly.
And the young Vorhelm looked directly at him.
"You want me."
The White-Eyed Man suddenly leaned forward and the chains around his hands made a clicking sound.
"Smart!"
And he immediately started laughing.
"You’re really smart! That’s why I like you." He suddenly frowned.
"No, no...like is not a good word."
He thought deeply for a few moments.
"Am I happy to see you? No." He tilted his head again and then a big smile appeared on his face.
"I want you...Yeah. That’s better." His white eyes examined Lian’s body again.
Lian raised an eyebrow, he felt like he was talking to a pervert, and the man continued without caring.
"My offer is still there. You can become stronger, very, very much stronger. Even the strongest. I can make things from you that you don’t even know are possible yet."
He suddenly became silent and his smile disappeared, then his eyes became truly focused.

"Wait...you became stronger...no, much stronger, this growth is not like the others, and why...why! Why! Why do you smell like them?" His eyes opened wider and his body moved forward as far as the chains allowed.
"How? What happened? What did you do? What did you eat? Who did you kill? Did something change inside your body? Who opened you? Why do you smell like those bastards?"
"Did you come into contact with them? ...No! That’s impossible, we can’t see them."
The questions came out one after another, and his voice became more excited with every question.
"Enough nonsense." Lian frowned, he did not even understand what this madman was talking about.
Who exactly did he mean by that smell?
"I’m not going to become part of any of your strange creatures, let alone your masterpiece." He then added.
The man remained completely still for a few seconds, then a short sound came from his throat.
"Hehehe..."
His laughter became louder, his head dropped and his shoulders started shaking.
"Oh...sorry." He said between his laughs and raised his head again...this time the laughter suddenly stopped.
"You think you still have a choice?"
The young Vorhelm remained silent, and the man also became completely calm for a moment.
"No, you don’t have a choice."
"To create my greatest masterpiece...to create a Calamity Seed...I need you."

sentences.text: "The White-Eyed Man’s cell." Gareth said in a low voice.
Click.
The last lock was released.

The huge black door first moved a few centimeters backward, the sound of heavy mechanisms moving inside the wall filled the area, and a moment later, the entire several-ton door slowly moved to the left.
Lian expected the cell to be directly behind it, but what appeared in front of him was another small room.

The walls of the observation room were almost completely black, and only a few white mana lines ran across the ceiling and floor, in front of them, several layers of glass covered the entire wall; dozens of small arrays were shining between its layers.
The White-Eyed Man’s cell was behind it, and the room was almost empty.
There was a metal table, two chairs, four gray walls, and there was no bed, no extra object, and not even something that could be broken and used as a weapon.
The White-Eyed Man was sitting on the chair on the other side of the table.
His wrists were locked with black mana suppression rings, two more rings were around his ankles, and a thicker ring was around his neck.
Short chains connected each of them to the chair and the floor.

Even so, his appearance did not look like a prisoner at all, he was leaning against the back of the chair, his shoulders were relaxed and his head was slightly lowered; as if he was not sitting in one of the safest prisons in the country, but sitting in his own home waiting for a guest who was late.
Gareth had only taken one step into the observation room when the man moved, his head rose, before the inner door of the cell had even opened.
His completely white eyes locked directly onto Vorhelm through the several layers of glass.
Only him.
He stayed silent for a few seconds and then a calm smile appeared on his face.
"You finally came." He said in an almost happy tone.
"I heard you missed me." Lian looked at him for a few seconds without changing his expression.
The man’s lips opened and a short, strange laugh came from his throat.
"Missed you?
No, no..." The White-Eyed Man seriously shook his head, as if he was truly correcting an important mistake.
"That’s not a good word.
I was curious.
Very curious."
He slowly tilted his head to one side and his eyes moved across Lian’s body.
"I wanted to see how much my little piece has grown."
The inner door opened with Gareth’s approval, and the pressure from the mana suppression arrays inside the cell immediately became several times stronger.
As Lian crossed the entrance, he felt the mana inside his body become like a thick and useless liquid.
The commander also entered with him, and the White-Eyed Man did not take his eyes off Vorhelm.
"I said I wanted to talk to the boy." He said this time in a bored tone.
"And I’m staying here." Gareth stood beside the table.
The White-Eyed Man turned his white eyes toward him, looked at him for two seconds, and then simply shrugged.
"Okay." And he became silent.
Gareth waited.
Five seconds.
Ten seconds.
Fifteen seconds.
The White-Eyed Man only smiled at him, not a single word, not even an extra movement, he was completely silent.
The commander narrowed his eyes and understood what he was trying to do.
"Don’t think you can make demands from us in your current situation.
The White-Eyed Man slightly pursed his lips.
"I didn’t make a demand, I said I wanted to talk to him.
You stayed, so I don’t talk." He slightly tilted his head.
"See?
It’s very simple, even children can understand it."
A thin vein appeared beside Gareth’s temple, Lian felt that if this continued for a few more minutes, the interrogation would probably end before it even started.
He turned his eyes toward the commander.
"Let me try.
Everything is being recorded, right?"
Gareth looked at him for a few seconds, it was clear that he did not like this decision, but in the end he nodded.
"Image, sound, mana changes, and every movement inside the room are recorded.
The arrays are also active, and if anything happens, the forces outside will enter in less than one second."
Then he fixed his eyes on the White-Eyed Man.
"And I’ll also be right behind this glass."
"How reassuring." The madman said with a smile.
The commander ignored him and looked at Lian again before leaving.
"If he makes even the smallest move, you don’t need to play the hero."
The young Vorhelm nodded, and he left the cell, closing the door behind him.
Click.
The locks became active again, and now only two people remained inside the room.
Lian pulled back the chair across from the man and sat down, neither of them said anything for a few seconds, the quiet sound of the room’s air system was the only thing breaking the silence.
The White-Eyed Man was looking at him, but not like someone looking at another person’s face.
First, he examined his fingers, then his forearms, shoulders, chest, neck, and finally his eyes.
That look was less human than it was like the look of a surgeon seeing his favorite test subject again after several months.
And the young Vorhelm allowed it to continue for a few seconds before speaking calmly.
"If you’re only going to look at me, you could have asked for a picture."
"Pictures don’t breathe." The man answered without even thinking.
"Why did you want to see me?"
"I told you, I missed my remaining piece."
Lian said nothing, he only looked at him.
Three seconds.
Five seconds.
Eight seconds.
The man’s smile slowly disappeared.
Then he moved his head back with childish annoyance.
"Ugh...you’re so boring, you don’t even play a little." He complained under his breath.
In the next moment, that annoyance disappeared from his face, as if it had never existed, and his bound fingers began tapping on the table.
Click.
Click.
Click.
"I only came back to take my masterpiece back, they took it.
They cut it into pieces, cut it, measured it, looked at it, opened it up..."
His face became slightly angry for a moment.
"You’re very nosy."
Lian thought about the border city, that strange monster the White-Eyed Man proudly called his masterpiece.
And the conversation they had that same day, the man had asked him for something, his body, he had asked him to become part of the monster.
Had this madman brought him here again because of something like that?
"But you’re still missing one piece, let me guess." He finally said calmly.
The tapping of his fingers stopped and the man’s white eyes shone slightly.
And the young Vorhelm looked directly at him.
"You want me."
The White-Eyed Man suddenly leaned forward and the chains around his hands made a clicking sound.
"Smart!"
And he immediately started laughing.
"You’re really smart!
That’s why I like you." He suddenly frowned.
"No, no...like is not a good word."
He thought deeply for a few moments.
"Am I happy to see you?
No." He tilted his head again and then a big smile appeared on his face.
"I want you...Yeah.
That’s better." His white eyes examined Lian’s body again.
Lian raised an eyebrow, he felt like he was talking to a pervert, and the man continued without caring.
"My offer is still there.
You can become stronger, very, very much stronger.
Even the strongest.
I can make things from you that you don’t even know are possible yet."
He suddenly became silent and his smile disappeared, then his eyes became truly focused.
"Wait...you became stronger...no, much stronger, this growth is not like the others, and why...why!
Why!
Why do you smell like them?" His eyes opened wider and his body moved forward as far as the chains allowed.
"How?
What happened?
What did you do?
What did you eat?
Who did you kill?
Did something change inside your body?
Who opened you?
Why do you smell like those bastards?"
"Did you come into contact with them? ...No!
That’s impossible, we can’t see them."
The questions came out one after another, and his voice became more excited with every question.
"Enough nonsense." Lian frowned, he did not even understand what this madman was talking about.
Who exactly did he mean by that smell?
"I’m not going to become part of any of your strange creatures, let alone your masterpiece." He then added.
The man remained completely still for a few seconds, then a short sound came from his throat.
"Hehehe..."
His laughter became louder, his head dropped and his shoulders started shaking.
"Oh...sorry." He said between his laughs and raised his head again...this time the laughter suddenly stopped.
"You think you still have a choice?"
The young Vorhelm remained silent, and the man also became completely calm for a moment.
"No, you don’t have a choice."
"To create my greatest masterpiece...to create a Calamity Seed...I need you."

chapters.title: Chapter 464: The Greatest Monster Maker III
paragraphs: "For making my greatest masterpiece... for creating a Calamity Seed... I need you."
All of Lian’s attention immediately focused on the last three words, and the man did not notice the very small change in his expression and continued excitedly.
"I tried! I really tried!"
His chains made a sound as he moved his hands.
"I went, I searched, I looked, I cut, I experimented... There are so many talented people in this world, you know? So many."
Then his face suddenly became sad.
"But it’s your fault."
"Me?" Lian raised an eyebrow.
"Yes, you!" The man pointed at him almost like he was complaining.
"You ruined my standards!"
The young Vorhelm stared at him for a few moments, and the white-eyed man continued.
"After seeing you, everyone else became ugly. Incomplete. Boring. Good bones, bad mana. Good mana, weak body. Good body, worthless soul."
He shook his head sadly.
"None of them were complete." Then his smile slowly returned.
"That’s why I came back to you."
The young Vorhelm became silent, until this moment he had thought the white-eyed man had been running from the Federation all this time.
Hiding, changing locations and trying to stay alive, but apparently he was wrong, this man had still been working on his own project all this time.
He was looking for people, experimenting, creating and apparently killing. Just because none of them reached what he had seen in Lian, he had come back again.
But even this was not the most important part of what he had said.
Calamity Seed.
Lian had seen this term before, in the Special Area and more exactly in the Giant Forest when he met that Ant Queen.
The System had judged that creature as something beyond a normal monster.
[Calamity Seed.]
At that time, he had not paid much attention to it, not because those words were unimportant but because he had no idea what "Calamity" meant in that context.
But now things were different.
He had seen the Black Silence, fought a Calamity and swallowed it in the heart of the Ruined Realm.
He had seen the memories of that Calamity and now he knew what Calamities actually were and what they referred to.
Those two words now had a different meaning.
"A Calamity Seed?" Lian asked quietly.
The white-eyed man froze immediately and his eyes opened slightly wider.
"Oh, I shouldn’t have said that word." He pressed his lips together.
He showed no reaction and only waited, the man slowly shook his head several times.
"No, no, no. I won’t explain it. There’s no point." He started muttering to himself.
"You people of this world know nothing. Nothing. Zero. Every time I explain it, you look at me with those stupid eyes as if I’m crazy."
"Me? Crazy?" He suddenly looked at him and gave a short laugh.
"That’s ridiculous." Then he started mumbling again.
"I told some of you before. No one believed me. You say our people were crazy, you say it’s a legend, superstition, the fear of the people of a dead world...
His voice suddenly became louder.
"But you are the crazy ones!"
His voice echoed through the cell and one second later, he became completely calm again.
"Happy idiots."
Lian looked at him for a few seconds, he did not have enough information, but he had something he could try, something that might show him the man’s reaction.
He leaned a little closer and spoke in a way that only that man could hear.
"What is it that we don’t know? About the Five Calamities?"
The white-eyed man... froze, this time the difference was clear, it was not acting, it was not a show and it was not one of his strange changes in mood.
It was real shock, and his completely white eyes opened wider, his lips stayed slightly open for a moment and his whole face seemed to ask one question.
How do you know?
But he did not say it, he only stared.
One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Then the corner of his lips rose... more... more, until the smile on his face became almost unnatural.
"I knew it... I knew it!" The man suddenly stood up from his chair.
Clang!
The chain around his neck pulled tight and did not let him stand completely, but he did not care.
"I knew you were different from the others! I knew it! I knew it! My eyes don’t make mistakes, they never make mistakes!"
His crazy laughter filled the room.
"Oh..." He lowered his head and then looked at Lian again.
"Now I want you even more!"
The young Vorhelm only looked at him, at this moment, he had no doubt anymore, this man was truly crazy.
The only thing he did not understand was how someone could reach such a state.
Even so, his stupid and exaggerated reaction had at least proven two things, the white-eyed man knew about the Five Calamities and the Calamity Seed was related to them.
He opened his mouth to ask his next question, but the man suddenly became silent, his laughter stopped and his head lowered.
"Now that you know... there is no need to waste time anymore." He then whispered quietly.
Lian’s eyes narrowed, the man slowly raised his head and a new smile appeared on his face.
"I’ve made my decision again, you will be the final piece."
Ding...
Suddenly, a strange sound echoed from nowhere.
The young Vorhelm immediately stood up from his chair, the sound was very quiet, but the strangest part was that he had not heard it with his ears.
The sound had directly entered his soul.
Ding...
No mana fluctuation appeared, none of the suppression arrays reacted, even the warning light did not turn on.
Then something appeared behind the white-eyed man.
A small bell.
It was half-transparent, but it had not come out of his pocket and it had not come from anything like a storage space, instead it seemed to have been pulled directly out of his soul.
The surface of the bell was covered with hundreds of tiny symbols, writings that he did not recognize even one of.
Ding!
This time, the room shook.
No... he understood it immediately, the room was not shaking, space itself was shaking, the table in front of him was divided into dozens of half-transparent cubes for a moment.
Part of the wall moved three centimeters to one side, while another part stayed still.
The floor.
The lights.
The chair.
The man’s body.
Even Lian’s own hand all became cube-shaped blocks of reality for a moment, his eyes opened wider.
"What the hell is this—"
And at that exact moment, the world disappeared.
White.
The first thing he saw was only white, snow stretched all the way to the horizon.
Huge frozen plains spread under a heavy gray sky, and strong wind carried small pieces of snow across the entire area like white fog.
Ice-covered mountains could be seen in the distance.
He slowly blinked.
He felt no cold.
The temperature of the area could kill a normal human in a short time, but for the Heir of Winter, it was almost meaningless.
He looked around, there were no buildings, roads or any sign of civilization, there was only ice.
Lian thought for a moment about his possible geographical location.
"Antarctica?" he whispered quietly.
A laugh came from behind him, the white-eyed man was standing several meters away.
There was no ring around his neck and no chains on his hands, and he opened his arms happily.
"Welcome to my new home!" Behind him, at the bottom of a huge wall of ice, the dark entrance of a cave could be seen.
Without giving any other explanation, the man turned around and walked toward it.
The young Vorhelm watched him for a few seconds and then followed him.
If this man had wanted to attack him immediately, a few seconds ago would have been a much better time to do it.
And more importantly, he still had not gotten his answers.
"So all this time, whenever you wanted, you could leave the prison?" he asked while walking a few meters behind him.
"Yes!"
The answer came without any pause, and then the man started laughing.
"That’s so funny. They built those things beneath mountains, placed arrays, placed soldiers, built doors, first lock, second lock, third lock..." He counted with his fingers while walking.
"They thought I was a prisoner." Then he turned slightly toward him like a child telling a funny secret.
"I only stayed there because I wanted to."

chapters.title: Chapter 465: Calamity Seed I
paragraphs: Lian kept his eyes on the man’s back, one of the safest places in the country, with hundreds of arrays, commanders, and suppression systems, had all become meaningless ...at least against that bell.
"Can that bell also move between worlds?" He thought about what he had seen a few moments ago.
The white-eyed man suddenly stopped and turned around, then gave him a big smile.
"Ah! You want to know how I entered your world, huh?" He hit his own chest with his other hand.
"The answer is that bell."
He narrowed his eyes slightly, so one of Gareth’s three questions had been answered very quickly.
The white-eyed man had not entered their world through the cracks, he had a tool that seemed to be able to move between worlds.
But this answer created another question.
What was that bell?
Even the System had not shown any information at that moment.
But the fact that the System had shown nothing was not the main problem, the main problem was what kind of artifact had the ability to travel between worlds.
And how did it even work?
Whatever it was, he felt that getting that bell might not be a bad thing, that artifact had really caught his attention.
Lian did not ask anything for now and the man started walking again.
At first, the entrance of the cave looked completely natural, ice walls, dark rocks, and icicles hanging from the ceiling.
But only a few dozen meters ahead, everything changed, thin lines could be seen inside the ice.
Several semi-transparent tubes passed through the walls and a green liquid slowly flowed inside them.
Blue mushrooms had grown in the corners of the path, giving off a weak light.
A little farther ahead, there was a weak smell of blood, mixed with unknown materials and large glass containers were placed beside the walls, with unclear organs floating inside colored liquids.
Lian looked at one of them, it looked like an eye, but it had three pupils, so he immediately looked away.
The farther they went, the less the cave looked like a cave and the more it looked like the inside of a huge creature.
Finally, the path opened and a huge space appeared in front of them.
He stopped, there was a laboratory in front of them, but it looked nothing like the laboratories on Earth.
Some parts of the equipment were made of metal and other parts looked almost alive, tubes like veins moved along the walls.
Unknown organs were floating inside containers.
Cutting tools were placed beside tables whose surfaces were covered with old blood marks.
But Lian’s eyes stayed on them for only a few seconds because something in the center of the cave caught all of his attention.
A huge egg, almost ten meters tall, with a transparent shell.
A dark liquid slowly moved inside it and hundreds of thick veins connected from the walls of the container to whatever was inside.
It was a creature, its body was still incomplete, its hands were crossed over its chest and very thick bones could be seen under the half-formed flesh.
Parts of its body were covered with black natural armor, its head still did not have its final shape.
But he immediately saw the similarity, it was the same creature from the border city, or at least something made through the same process, but this one was different.
More organized and even in its incomplete state, it looked much more dangerous, even though they looked similar, they were also different.
It was clear that this was not the same creature, but he was certain that parts of that creature had been used to make this one.
"So this is the real version?" Lian stayed silent for a few seconds and then asked.
Was this what this man had really been working on? Was this his goal all this time?
"Yes and no." The white-eyed man stood beside the container.
The young Vorhelm looked away from the creature and looked at him, and the man placed his palm against the transparent shell.
"I told you I came back to take my masterpiece back, right?"
He smiled.
"What you saw in the city was not the final masterpiece itself. It was a part, a container, and a stage." He tapped the shell a few times with his fingernail.
Tap.
Tap.
"I only wanted some parts of it." His eyes moved lovingly over the creature inside the container.
"The good parts."
"I am sure that when the Federation took that creature, it was complete, how did you get these parts?"
"Curious people see many things, but because they think they see everything... they fail to see exactly the important things."
Lian said nothing, a few hours ago he might have thought this claim was an exaggeration.
But this same man had escaped from one of the safest prisons in the country a few minutes ago without activating even a single alarm.
Stealing a few parts from a body that was being studied no longer seemed that strange.
So this man had been playing with the Federation all this time, he had even managed to play with an Overlord, this was no longer just madness.
It was a crazy kind of genius, something that truly deserved admiration, no matter how crazy he was, he had still done something that Lian had never thought he would have the courage to do.
The white-eyed man took his hand away from the shell and took two steps back.
"You asked what a Calamity Seed is, right?"
This time Lian gave him his full attention, this was something he wanted to understand, he could make some guesses.
The man stayed silent for a few seconds and a small change appeared on his face, the calm smile slowly disappeared and something like seriousness could be seen in his expression.
"If you know about the Five Calamities...then you should know what a Calamity means."
He started walking around the container.
"Things that eat worlds, crush civilizations, erase generations, and when nothing is left, they move on to the next world."
He stopped for a moment.
"My world saw one of them too, but there is something you don’t know." The corner of his mouth rose slightly.
"There were not five of them from the beginning."
The silence of the cave became heavier.
"There were six positions."
The young Vorhelm’s eyes narrowed for a moment, he did not show much on the outside, but he was shocked in his mind.
Six Calamities? He had only seen five Calamities in the memories of the Black Silence, and everywhere else he had heard about them, he had always heard the number five.
But six? He had never seen anything that confirmed this number, but the man in front of him was saying that there had been six Calamities at the beginning.
What was the truth now?
"One of them was destroyed a very, very, very long time ago." The white-eyed man continued and his eyes moved away for a moment.
"But it was killed."
"How?" Lian asked immediately, even he himself had not been able to kill a Calamity alone and had swallowed it with the help of the Heart of Ruin.
So how had someone managed to kill another Calamity?
"I don’t know!" The man almost shouted and then moved his hands angrily.

"Nobody knows! The story is so old that even my people only had pieces of it. Some said something from outside the world killed it, some said the other Calamities ate it, some said the world itself turned against it."
Suddenly all the anger disappeared from his face and he shrugged.
"It doesn’t matter."
The young Vorhelm gave him a short look, it was very clear from his tone that it actually mattered a lot, but the man did not want to stop at something he did not know the answer to.
"After it died, the position stayed empty, and then...interesting things started happening." The man went back beside the container.
His smile returned.
"Sometimes, in different worlds, creatures were born that were not like the others. They grew, they changed, they broke their own limits, and changed again."
He raised his index finger.
"They are Seeds...Calamity Seeds."

sentences.text: Lian kept his eyes on the man’s back, one of the safest places in the country, with hundreds of arrays, commanders, and suppression systems, had all become meaningless ...at least against that bell.
"Can that bell also move between worlds?" He thought about what he had seen a few moments ago.
The white-eyed man suddenly stopped and turned around, then gave him a big smile.
"Ah!
You want to know how I entered your world, huh?" He hit his own chest with his other hand.
"The answer is that bell."
He narrowed his eyes slightly, so one of Gareth’s three questions had been answered very quickly.
The white-eyed man had not entered their world through the cracks, he had a tool that seemed to be able to move between worlds.
But this answer created another question.
What was that bell?
Even the System had not shown any information at that moment.
But the fact that the System had shown nothing was not the main problem, the main problem was what kind of artifact had the ability to travel between worlds.
And how did it even work?
Whatever it was, he felt that getting that bell might not be a bad thing, that artifact had really caught his attention.
Lian did not ask anything for now and the man started walking again.
At first, the entrance of the cave looked completely natural, ice walls, dark rocks, and icicles hanging from the ceiling.
But only a few dozen meters ahead, everything changed, thin lines could be seen inside the ice.
Several semi-transparent tubes passed through the walls and a green liquid slowly flowed inside them.
Blue mushrooms had grown in the corners of the path, giving off a weak light.
A little farther ahead, there was a weak smell of blood, mixed with unknown materials and large glass containers were placed beside the walls, with unclear organs floating inside colored liquids.
Lian looked at one of them, it looked like an eye, but it had three pupils, so he immediately looked away.
The farther they went, the less the cave looked like a cave and the more it looked like the inside of a huge creature.
Finally, the path opened and a huge space appeared in front of them.
He stopped, there was a laboratory in front of them, but it looked nothing like the laboratories on Earth.
Some parts of the equipment were made of metal and other parts looked almost alive, tubes like veins moved along the walls.
Unknown organs were floating inside containers.
Cutting tools were placed beside tables whose surfaces were covered with old blood marks.
But Lian’s eyes stayed on them for only a few seconds because something in the center of the cave caught all of his attention.
A huge egg, almost ten meters tall, with a transparent shell.
A dark liquid slowly moved inside it and hundreds of thick veins connected from the walls of the container to whatever was inside.
It was a creature, its body was still incomplete, its hands were crossed over its chest and very thick bones could be seen under the half-formed flesh.
Parts of its body were covered with black natural armor, its head still did not have its final shape.
But he immediately saw the similarity, it was the same creature from the border city, or at least something made through the same process, but this one was different.
More organized and even in its incomplete state, it looked much more dangerous, even though they looked similar, they were also different.
It was clear that this was not the same creature, but he was certain that parts of that creature had been used to make this one.
"So this is the real version?" Lian stayed silent for a few seconds and then asked.
Was this what this man had really been working on?
Was this his goal all this time?
"Yes and no." The white-eyed man stood beside the container.
The young Vorhelm looked away from the creature and looked at him, and the man placed his palm against the transparent shell.
"I told you I came back to take my masterpiece back, right?"
He smiled.
"What you saw in the city was not the final masterpiece itself.
It was a part, a container, and a stage." He tapped the shell a few times with his fingernail.
Tap.
Tap.
"I only wanted some parts of it." His eyes moved lovingly over the creature inside the container.
"The good parts."
"I am sure that when the Federation took that creature, it was complete, how did you get these parts?"
"Curious people see many things, but because they think they see everything... they fail to see exactly the important things."
Lian said nothing, a few hours ago he might have thought this claim was an exaggeration.
But this same man had escaped from one of the safest prisons in the country a few minutes ago without activating even a single alarm.
Stealing a few parts from a body that was being studied no longer seemed that strange.
So this man had been playing with the Federation all this time, he had even managed to play with an Overlord, this was no longer just madness.
It was a crazy kind of genius, something that truly deserved admiration, no matter how crazy he was, he had still done something that Lian had never thought he would have the courage to do.
The white-eyed man took his hand away from the shell and took two steps back.
"You asked what a Calamity Seed is, right?"
This time Lian gave him his full attention, this was something he wanted to understand, he could make some guesses.
The man stayed silent for a few seconds and a small change appeared on his face, the calm smile slowly disappeared and something like seriousness could be seen in his expression.
"If you know about the Five Calamities...then you should know what a Calamity means."
He started walking around the container.
"Things that eat worlds, crush civilizations, erase generations, and when nothing is left, they move on to the next world."
He stopped for a moment.
"My world saw one of them too, but there is something you don’t know." The corner of his mouth rose slightly.
"There were not five of them from the beginning."
The silence of the cave became heavier.
"There were six positions."
The young Vorhelm’s eyes narrowed for a moment, he did not show much on the outside, but he was shocked in his mind.
Six Calamities?
He had only seen five Calamities in the memories of the Black Silence, and everywhere else he had heard about them, he had always heard the number five.
But six?
He had never seen anything that confirmed this number, but the man in front of him was saying that there had been six Calamities at the beginning.
What was the truth now?
"One of them was destroyed a very, very, very long time ago." The white-eyed man continued and his eyes moved away for a moment.
"But it was killed."

"Nobody knows!
The story is so old that even my people only had pieces of it.
Some said something from outside the world killed it, some said the other Calamities ate it, some said the world itself turned against it."
Suddenly all the anger disappeared from his face and he shrugged.
"It doesn’t matter."

"After it died, the position stayed empty, and then...interesting things started happening." The man went back beside the container.
His smile returned.
"Sometimes, in different worlds, creatures were born that were not like the others.
They grew, they changed, they broke their own limits, and changed again."
He raised his index finger.
"They are Seeds...Calamity Seeds."

chapters.title: Chapter 466: Calamity Seed II
paragraphs: Another image appeared in the young Vorhelm’s mind, the Ant Queen, the same creature that the System had evaluated as a Calamity Seed and had even given him a Quest to kill.
So if he had not killed that Ant Queen, another Calamity would have entered their world.
And that random announcement was not simply a title for a special monster, that creature was a possible candidate for something much greater.
"How many Seeds are there? A hundred? A thousand? More?" The white-eyed man continued.
He gave a quiet laugh.
"Who cares? Many worlds have died, and a lot of time has passed." Then his smile disappeared.
"But none of them succeeded." He placed his finger on the egg’s shell.
"None of them could take the sixth position, so I decided not to wait for nature and make one myself."
Lian looked directly into his eyes and the white-eyed man opened both hands.
"I will make the sixth Calamity."
For a moment, the only sound was the liquid moving inside the container, then that crazy excitement appeared on the man’s face again.
"Think about it!" He took one step forward.
"Something that can stand beside them, not under their feet, not behind them, beside them!"
His voice became louder.
"Something that, when a Calamity comes down from the sky of its world, does not run! Does not kneel! Does not leave its people behind and wait for death!"
He hit the container with his hand.
Bang!
"Only a Calamity can fight a Calamity! So I will give humanity a Calamity!"
The young Vorhelm looked at him for a few seconds and the man took a heavy breath, but then, for the first time, something broke in his expression.
The excitement went away and the smile disappeared.
"Do you think I was happy to see my world destroyed?"
His tone had changed, it was not childish and he was no longer laughing, he only looked tired and hurt.
"I was there."
His eyes moved past Lian, as if the ice walls of the cave no longer existed and he was seeing something very far away.
"I saw our cities... I saw my people... I saw children who did not even understand why the sky had turned black."
For a few seconds, there was no sign of the crazy man from a few minutes ago.
"Everything we built... everything we learned... no matter how much we fought... it was not enough."
Then he looked at him again.
"Now, out of all the Volkari...only I remain...Ezrak."
Lian recorded the name in his mind, finally the white-eyed man had a name, Ezrak looked at the creature inside the container again.
"So yes... I will make a Calamity."
And the calmness in his voice slowly started to become crazy again.
"With it, I will kill the thing that destroyed my people." A calm smile appeared.
"Then that one... then the next one, and save the rest of humanity."
Vorhelm said nothing for a few moments, now he finally understood the sentence he had heard a long time ago.
In the border city, this man had said that his goal was to save humanity, at that time he had thought it was just another piece of nonsense from a crazy man.
But no, Ezrak had not lied, at least from his own point of view, he truly believed that what he was doing was saving humanity.
The problem was the price of that salvation.
He kept his eyes on the container, images of the dead bodies from the border city appeared in his mind.
People who had died, creatures that had been made from the bodies of several creatures.
Laboratories, killings, and if what Gareth had said was true, this man had probably turned hundreds of thousands of people into test materials over the years.

Especially with the Calamity he had created in East Asia, which had killed a large number of people, and if all the killings across other continents like Europe, North America, South America, and Africa were added together, the number of deaths might even reach the millions.
But to Ezrak, they were not victims, they were materials, they were that worthless, he only saw them as tools to reach his own goal.
Someone like this wanted to save humanity?
"Well?" The white-eyed man suddenly turned toward him again.
"Well what?"
"Your answer! Are you ready?" Ezrak’s eyes were almost shining with excitement and he pointed toward the huge egg.
"Are you ready to stand beside me and become part of the greatest thing a Volkari has ever done?"
His voice became louder.
"The final piece of my greatest monster?"
His smile became so wide that it almost looked painful.
"Together, we will make a Calamity."
He paused and then said in a tone as if he were offering the greatest deal in the world.
"And we will save the worlds."
Lian stayed silent for a few seconds, then laughed and a short laugh came from his throat, not because he was happy, but because of how meaningless what he had heard was.
Ezrak’s smile shook slightly and Vorhelm slowly shook his head.
"Save the worlds?" His eyes stayed directly on the white-eyed man.
"You really still believe that?"
"Why shouldn’t I believe it?" Ezrak kept his smile.
"Because you killed hundreds of thousands of people, cut human bodies apart, created creatures, turned cities into laboratories, and then called all those people you killed materials?
His tone was still calm and that calmness made the words heavier.
"No, you don’t want to save humanity." And he added with sarcasm.
"Be careful—" Ezrak’s face became cold for the first time, it was clear that this was his line.
Lian cut him off.
"You want to prove that you can make a Calamity."
Silence.
This time the white-eyed man gave no answer and Vorhelm did not take his eyes off him.
"Saving humanity is just a story you made for yourself so that everything you do can become acceptable." He pointed at the creature inside the container.

"You don’t look at the people you killed and call them victims...you call them material, because if you accept that they were people, you have to accept that what you have built all these years is not the way to salvation."
"You have to accept that you are not a savior." His eyes became colder.
The air in the cave became heavy, Ezrak was no longer laughing and instead of madness, anger and coldness could be seen in his eyes.
And Lian continued.
"You don’t love humanity, you love the idea of creating something that even the Calamities are forced to fear."
The man’s jaw tightened slightly, and this small reaction was enough for him, so he delivered the final blow.
"If someone comes tomorrow and proves to you that all five Calamities can be killed without this creature... I bet you still won’t stop making it."
No answer came and that silence was the answer, until this moment, Ezrak had almost always had something on his face.
A smile.
Laughter.
Excitement.
Mockery.
Childish anger.
But now there was nothing, his head became straight and his smile completely disappeared, his white eyes stayed fixed on Vorhelm without blinking.
The madness he showed had disappeared from him and the strange thing was that without it, he looked more frightening.
"You talk too much." Ezrak said in a completely cold voice.
Lian did not answer and the man turned his eyes toward the creature inside the container.
"Salvation."
"Power."
"Pride."
Then he looked at him again and the corner of his mouth rose very slowly.
"Whatever you want to call it, the result will not change." The distance between them became smaller and there was no excitement in his voice anymore.
"Just like I said before...you have no choice." His white eyes slowly narrowed.

chapters.title: Chapter 467: The Living Cave I
paragraphs: Ding...
Gareth was still standing behind the multi-layered glass of the observation room when the sound of the bell did not pass through the surveillance speakers.
Even so, he heard it.
For a moment, the sound echoed directly inside the depths of his mind, and all the hairs on the back of his neck stood up.
Before he could react, the image inside the cell broke apart.
Lian’s hand split into several semi-transparent cubes for a fraction of a second.
The table, the chair, the white-eyed man, and even part of the cell wall turned into irregular pieces that seemed to be in different points of space.
The commander took one step forward.
"What—"
Everything disappeared, no explosion happened, no wave of mana shook the room, and none of the hundreds of security arrays gave a warning before it happened.
The cell was simply empty.
For almost one second, complete silence filled the observation room, and then all the systems started screaming at the same time.
[Warning.]
[Target Number One has left the area.]
[Target Number Two has left the area.]
[Exit Method: Unknown.]
[Teleportation Array not activated.]
[Spatial Rift not detected.]
[No identifiable mana trace found.]
Gareth’s face immediately became cold, the inner door was still completely closed, but he did not even wait for the normal process.
"Open it!"
One of the agents nervously touched the control screen, and the locks were released at the highest possible speed.
He entered the cell... but it was empty, and the white-eyed man’s chair was still there, the chains had not been broken either.
The mana suppression rings had not fallen onto the floor.
In fact, they had disappeared with him as well, as if someone had taken not only the prisoner, but also a part of the reality around him from this place.
The sound of fast footsteps came from behind.
Rina entered the cell, and the usual coldness on her face was slightly broken.
"How did they get past the arrays?" she asked with a deep frown.
Gareth said nothing for several seconds, his eyes remained on the empty space in front of the chair.
Then he calmly said
"They didn’t get past them.
"What?"
He raised his head slightly.
"If they had passed through the arrays, at least one of them should have recorded something.
Spatial fluctuation, mana, a rift, pressure... anything, but nothing was recorded."
Rina pressed her lips together, and Gareth suddenly turned around, his tone was no longer the tone of the man who had joked with Lian a few minutes ago, but the tone of a commander.
"Close down the entire facility.
Check all exit routes, transportation systems, and outside communications.
Connect every spatial sensor in the country to the network; I want every unusual fluctuation, every new rift, and every unknown transfer that was recorded in the last ten minutes."
"Yes, Commander." Rina nodded.
"Contact the Federation Center as well.
Send them the first report and inform Overlord Orion."
"Do you think he will need to act himself?" This time, his deputy paused for a moment.
"I hope not." The commander looked at the empty chair.
"And Mr. Vorhelm?"
That question made Gareth frown even more, he had brought Lian here, he had personally asked him to enter that cell.
And now he did not even know where in the world he was.

"That madman took Lian with him, we have to find him, otherwise the Vorhelm family won’t leave us alone." He finally said calmly and his eyes stayed on the place where Lian had been sitting a few seconds ago.
At the same time, somewhere else
"You have no choice."
The cave fell silent for several seconds.
Lian stood in front of Ezrak and did not take his eyes away from those completely white eyes.
Then he slowly laughed.
"That sentence is usually said right before the other side makes a stupid choice."
Ezrak blinked several times, and then the corner of his lips rose.
"There you go again, your arrogant attitude still hasn’t changed."
"No, I’m just warning you, remember?
You were saying these things and making these threats in the border city too, what happened in the end?
In the end, you ran away like a dog."
The madman’s face became ugly, it was clear that some memories had been brought back to him that he was not happy about, even so, this was not enough to make him give up on his plan.
The Calamity Seed had to be completed today!
He had planned for years, made preparations, and was ready for this day.
"You want to fight?" Then Ezrak happily clapped his hands together.
"Great!
Great!
Let me see!
You’ve changed a lot since last time, so you have to show me how much better you’ve become, seeing the growth of my last piece!
Just thinking about it makes me excited."
"I thought you said I’m your last piece, so it’s better if you don’t break me."
Lian gave a short look at the huge chamber behind him.
"Exactly, that’s why I’m not going to kill you...just break you a little, enough to make you ready to be used."
Ezrak nodded very seriously and then smiled.
He paused for a moment.
And suddenly
Boom...!!!
The young Vorhelm immediately turned his head slightly.
A deep sound spread through the entire cave, it sounded more like a heartbeat.
Boom!!!
This time, the ground under his feet shook, and one of the biological tubes inside the wall contracted.
Then another.
He moved his eyes across the walls.
The thick veins that had seemed to be only part of the laboratory a few minutes ago now started to pulse one after another.
The dark liquid inside them moved several centimeters forward with every beat, and the temperature of the area changed slightly.
At the same time, Predator’s Instincts sensed something.
Life.
From the walls themselves...?
He could feel life and blood flowing through the floor, the ceiling, and the entire structure around him.
"This cave..." he whispered in surprise and
Ezrak proudly walked to the nearest wall and placed his palm against its semi-transparent tissue.
"You thought this was just a cave?
This has been my home and laboratory for twenty years, and more importantly...one of my children!"
The vein under his fingers contracted.
Boom.
"And I only taught it what shape to take."

Rina pressed her lips together, and Gareth suddenly turned around, his tone was no longer the tone of the man who had joked with Lian a few minutes ago, but the tone of a commander.
"Close down the entire facility.
Check all exit routes, transportation systems, and outside communications.
Connect every spatial sensor in the country to the network; I want every unusual fluctuation, every new rift, and every unknown transfer that was recorded in the last ten minutes."
"Yes, Commander." Rina nodded.
"Contact the Federation Center as well.
Send them the first report and inform Overlord Orion."
"Do you think he will need to act himself?" This time, his deputy paused for a moment.
"I hope not." The commander looked at the empty chair.
"And Mr.
Vorhelm?"
That question made Gareth frown even more, he had brought Lian here, he had personally asked him to enter that cell.
And now he did not even know where in the world he was.

"That madman took Lian with him, we have to find him, otherwise the Vorhelm family won’t leave us alone." He finally said calmly and his eyes stayed on the place where Lian had been sitting a few seconds ago.
At the same time, somewhere else
"You have no choice."
The cave fell silent for several seconds.
Lian stood in front of Ezrak and did not take his eyes away from those completely white eyes.
Then he slowly laughed.
"That sentence is usually said right before the other side makes a stupid choice."
Ezrak blinked several times, and then the corner of his lips rose.
"There you go again, your arrogant attitude still hasn’t changed."
"No, I’m just warning you, remember?
You were saying these things and making these threats in the border city too, what happened in the end?
In the end, you ran away like a dog."
The madman’s face became ugly, it was clear that some memories had been brought back to him that he was not happy about, even so, this was not enough to make him give up on his plan.
The Calamity Seed had to be completed today!
He had planned for years, made preparations, and was ready for this day.
"You want to fight?" Then Ezrak happily clapped his hands together.
"Great!
Great!
Let me see!
You’ve changed a lot since last time, so you have to show me how much better you’ve become, seeing the growth of my last piece!
Just thinking about it makes me excited."
"I thought you said I’m your last piece, so it’s better if you don’t break me."
Lian gave a short look at the huge chamber behind him.
"Exactly, that’s why I’m not going to kill you...just break you a little, enough to make you ready to be used."
Ezrak nodded very seriously and then smiled.
He paused for a moment.
And suddenly
Boom...!!!
The young Vorhelm immediately turned his head slightly.
A deep sound spread through the entire cave, it sounded more like a heartbeat.
Boom!!!
This time, the ground under his feet shook, and one of the biological tubes inside the wall contracted.
Then another.
He moved his eyes across the walls.
The thick veins that had seemed to be only part of the laboratory a few minutes ago now started to pulse one after another.
The dark liquid inside them moved several centimeters forward with every beat, and the temperature of the area changed slightly.
At the same time, Predator’s Instincts sensed something.
Life.
From the walls themselves...?
He could feel life and blood flowing through the floor, the ceiling, and the entire structure around him.
"This cave..." he whispered in surprise and
Ezrak proudly walked to the nearest wall and placed his palm against its semi-transparent tissue.
"You thought this was just a cave?
This has been my home and laboratory for twenty years, and more importantly...one of my children!"
The vein under his fingers contracted.
Boom.
"And I only taught it what shape to take."

chapters.title: Chapter 468: The Living Cave II
paragraphs: Lian’s eyes narrowed, now that he looked more carefully, it was not hard to understand the truth, part of the cave really was natural stone and ice.
But what he called a laboratory had grown on something alive.
The walls he thought were covered with unknown materials were actually thick layers of tissue.
The tubes were veins, some of the blue lights were sensory organs, and that weak smell of blood...was the blood of this place itself.
The first time he had seen this man, he thought that he had lived or hidden in that border city all this time, but now he understood how wrong he had been.
Many of the guesses about this man, not only his but also the Federation’s, had been wrong, and he had been hiding far more secrets than they expected.
According to Gareth, this man had been in their world for at least twenty years, God knew what he had done in this world during all those years.
"Every time I think you can’t get any stranger."
Lian slowly breathed out.
"Thank you."
Ezrak smiled with satisfaction.
"That wasn’t a compliment."
"It was for me."
At that moment, mana gathered in his legs.
[Thunder Step]
Boom!
The stone under his foot cracked, and his body jumped several meters forward in an explosion of blue-purple light.
Ezrak was nothing like Rodrick in physical strength, if Lian reached him, one hit would be enough.
The distance went from fifteen meters to less than five meters in a fraction of a second.
But at that exact moment, the floor of the cave opened...it really opened.
A large crack formed under the young Vorhelm, and two rows of white bones jumped out from both sides of it.
They were jaws!
Teeth as long as a human arm that could crush and tear anything apart.
Crack!
The two rows of bones slammed into each other with terrifying force.
If Lian had reacted half a second later, his body would have been crushed between them like a piece of meat, but before the jaws could close, his body turned into ash.
[Ash Step]
A mass of black ash scattered between the teeth and formed again several meters away.
"Ah!
You didn’t have this!
Is it new?
That’s so cool!"
Ezrak clapped excitedly.
"There are many things I didn’t have."
"You know, when you combine with a Calamity Seed and my child finally comes alive, it will also be able to use all the skills and little secrets you use, even thinking about it is great, isn’t it?"
Lian had not answered yet when the wall on his left split open and five thin arms jumped out.
They were tall, each one was more than four meters long, and each one had three joints, with thin fingers and curved bone claws at the ends.
The first one came toward his neck.
He lowered his body, and the claw passed over his hair and broke through the wall behind him.
The second attacked his stomach, and this time the young Vorhelm did not move back, blue-purple lightning covered his entire right arm.
[Thunder Calamity]
His fist hit the arm.
Boom!
The tissue exploded from the middle, and broken bone spun through the air before falling to the ground.
The third and fourth arms came at the same time, Lian turned half a step, his elbow was covered with lightning, and he broke one of them in half.
Another claw passed only a few centimeters from his face, but the fifth arm twisted up from below.
He grabbed it, and his fingers closed around the thin bones.
With one movement...crack!
He tore the arm out from its root, and black liquid splashed onto the ground, Ezrak placed his hands over his chest and watched with excitement.
"Did you see?
Did you see?
I modified this one three times, what do you think?
I made them very well, right?
This place isn’t only the best place to live, it can even protect me!"
"It’s ugly, and not only that, everything you make is ugly, you have no understanding of beauty, do you?
Or is the taste of your civilization naturally this terrible?"
Lian looked at the torn-off arm.
"Rude, what you said really hurt me, even if you’re the last piece I need, that doesn’t mean you can dare insult my child."
Ezrak’s smile immediately disappeared.
Behind Vorhelm, the sound of tearing flesh came.
He turned around to see what was happening, and the arms he had broken were growing again.
White bone first came out through the tissue, then flesh wrapped around it, and gray skin covered it.
All of this took less than ten seconds.
"Of course."
He whispered to himself, and this reminded him of the same creature that this madman had called his masterpiece in the border city.
That damn thing also had an amazing kind of self-healing, to the point that it seemed almost immortal, and now it seemed that Ezrak had applied the same ability to this cave as well.
This profession of making monsters really seemed terrifying, especially if someone could reach the same level of skill as this white-eyed man.
He could understand why the Federation was after him.
At that exact moment, the ground suddenly tilted, it was not that the cave had shaken, but the floor under his feet itself started to rise.
In less than two seconds, the flat surface became a slope of almost forty degrees.
Lian kept his balance, but the ceiling also came down at the same time, and from the right, a crack opened in the wall.
A new hallway appeared, and from the left, the path that had existed before was closed by two thick layers of flesh and bone.
The entire battlefield was changing.
"Do you like this place?"
Ezrak was standing somewhere higher and happily watching him.
Lian gave him a poker face, right now he really wanted to punch that bastard in the face.

chapters.title: Chapter 469: A Womb...?
paragraphs: At that moment, the sound of several biological sacs bursting came.
Pop!
Pop!
Three masses fell from the ceiling onto the ground, the first one was almost human-shaped, but it had no legs.
It placed its two very large arms on the ground and pulled its skinless body toward Lian, the second was only a large head with six thin arms sticking out from around its skull.
It was impossible to even understand what the third one was supposed to be.
A four-legged body with an exposed spine and two incomplete faces on its chest.
All three moved toward him before they had even completely come out of the liquid that had created them, and he gave them a short look.
"You don’t clean your workshop very much, what are these disgusting pieces of trash?"
"They are experiments, how many times are you going to insult my great experiments?"
Ezrak frowned.
"Since when is trash a type of experiment?"
Vorhelm looked at him in surprise.
"You really are annoying."
The white-eyed man decided to ignore him.
The first creature threw itself forward, and Lian stepped to the side, the creature’s fist broke the floor.
Before it could pull its hand out, lightning gathered in his palm and he struck the back of its head.
Boom!
The half-made skull exploded on the ground, and the second creature fell on him from above, its six arms wrapping around the young Vorhelm like a spider.
But his body disappeared for a moment.
[False Presence]
The claws closed around the false image, and Lian appeared two meters behind it.
Ezrak did not even look at the false image, and he immediately turned around, the wall behind him had opened and dozens of red threads like nerves were coming toward him at an incredible speed.
One of them hit his shoulder, his clothes were torn and his skin also received a thin cut, if it had hit his neck directly, it probably would have separated his head from his body.
Lian jumped backward and three more threads passed in front of his face, his eyes narrowed.
So False Presence had not worked on Ezrak, the man had noticed it and had informed this living cave as well and because of that his target had failed.
He knew this skill was not perfect, but he had not expected this white-eyed man to see through the skill.
"How?"
He whispered to himself, he had a few guesses but none of them were reliable.
"You are walking inside my body."
Ezrak happily pointed around him.
And suddenly...he became silent for a moment and frowned.
"No...that was a bad sentence."
"At least we agree on something."
Lian said while dodging another attack.
"You are walking inside my child’s body."
The white-eyed man corrected his sentence.
"Not much better, that sentence could get both of us arrested for a certain crime."
Ezrak shrugged, and in any case Lian had really understood what he meant and how he had noticed his [False Presence] skill.

The entire cave was full of sensory organs and it could see and notice the pressure of his steps, the heat of his body, the mana he released, the movement of the air when his body moved and maybe even his heartbeat.
That man did not need eyes to see him, as long as he was inside this huge creature, the entire battlefield was one eye.
The nerve threads attacked again, and this time the young Vorhelm did not move back, he placed his hand on the ground.
Mana left his body.
[Frost Dominion]
Crack...
Ice spread from under his palm, but this time it did not stop on the surface and he sent his control deeper...inside the tissue, inside the cracks and even inside the veins moving under the ground.
If he wanted to bring this living cave to its knees and defeat it, he needed to break it from the inside.
The black liquid inside one of the veins froze immediately, and the ice moved through the living network of the cave like a white disease.
One meter.
Five meters.
Ten meters.
The arms that had come out of the wall suddenly stopped in the middle of their movement, one of the nerve threads was only a few centimeters away from his eye when it froze.
Ice covered its entire surface.
"Oh."
Ezrak frowned even deeper, and it was clear that what he had done was enough to make the man feel threatened.
Crack!
One of the frozen veins inside the wall exploded, and black liquid and pieces of tissue fell onto the ground.
"You’re just ruining the floor of my home."
The white-eyed man looked at him unhappily.
"I’m just cleaning this place from the trash."
Lian stood up.
Ezrak opened his mouth to answer, but he did not let him, lightning appeared on his right arm, although this time he did not punch and placed his palm directly on the ice.
[Thunder Calamity]
Krrrrrrrr!
Lightning entered the ice...the ice was not actually just a surface and his goal was not only to freeze everything with ice, but now he had connected the entire frozen network inside the cave’s body.
In one moment, electricity passed through dozens of veins.
BOOOOOOM!
The entire part of the cave convulsed, the walls moved forward and backward, mouths inside the tissues opened without making a sound.
Eyes that Lian had not even noticed were there opened at the same time among the flesh, and a moment later they exploded from the strength of the current.
Several small chambers exploded, and the incomplete creatures inside them burned before they were born.
"Ah!"
Ezrak suddenly put both hands on his head, his body moved one step backward, his connection with the creature had received feedback for a moment.
And because of this, the connection between them shook and a strong nerve shock hit him.
Lian moved immediately, he was not going to waste such a great opportunity.
[Thunder Step]
Boom!
The distance closed in the blink of an eye, the white-eyed man raised his head, but it was already too late, for the first time the young Vorhelm had truly reached him.
A lightning-covered fist came toward his face, it seemed that this attack would definitely hit.
...but a wall of tissue grew between them and several meters of dense flesh and bone formed between the two of them in less than a second.
Lian’s fist went inside it, but he could not pass through all of its thickness and Ezrak’s laughter came from the other side.
"That was close!"
Lian pulled his fist out, the wall was quickly becoming thicker, a frown appeared on his face, the more time passed, the more he felt how annoying this living cave was.
No matter how much he tried, as soon as he got close to this bastard, the cave protected him in strange ways.
He had tried to freeze everything, he had tried to destroy it with lightning and he had even tried to tear them apart.
But in the end it was useless, everything he did was useless, so how was he supposed to kill this cave?
And while he was frowning, a familiar sentence echoed in his mind.
Aldric’s voice.
"When you first learn the skill, you’ll probably make a twenty-meter palm and get happy when you see it."
He looked at the huge wall, a small smile appeared on his face.
"I think he was right."
He raised his right hand, mana flowed toward his palm.
Instead of being compressed into a small space like Aldric’s version, the mana spread out from his palm.
A huge aura appeared in front of him, at first it was not in a clear shape and then it took form.
A huge palm, more than fifteen meters, and even he looked at it for a few seconds.
"Oh?!
Another new thing!!
...but why is it so big?"
Ezrak’s excited voice came from behind the wall.
"You like big?
Let’s see how different it is from a small one."
Lian pushed his palm forward and his eyes narrowed.
[Suppressing Palm]
BOOOOOOOOM!
The mana palm hit the wall.
Pressure was applied, the first meter of tissue was crushed immediately, then the second, and the bones inside the wall made a horrible sound.
Crack!
Crack!
Crack!
The entire mass that was several meters thick was pushed inward, and black liquid came out of the tissues like a fountain.
A moment later, the wall exploded from the middle and pieces of flesh and bone spread throughout the cave, and the force of the attack even pushed the white-eyed man several meters backward.
For a moment, there was silence.
The young Vorhelm looked at his own palm.
His control was terrible, a large amount of mana had been wasted, the size was much larger than what he needed.
But its power was not bad, in fact it was incredible, he had also used only a small amount of mana and this skill could make its attacks stronger or weaker depending on the amount of mana it needed.
On the other side of the ruined wall, Ezrak was lying on the ground, he had landed badly and it was clear that he was injured...it was expected that he would curse, get angry or something like that.
But a few seconds later, he started laughing, at first Lian thought it was because of anger.
But no.
The white-eyed man was genuinely happy and quickly stood up from the ground.
"Did you see?!"
Who was he talking to?
It was not clear, was he talking to him?
Or was he talking to someone else...?
"Did you see?
Did you see?
Did you see?!"
His eyes were shining with excitement.
"I was not wrong!
It became even better!
Much better!"
He started counting with his fingers in the air.
"Better bones.
Better muscles.
More mana.
More compatibility.
Stranger growth..."
He suddenly looked at Lian and his smile became wider.
"If you keep going like this, maybe I won’t even have to throw much of you away!
Everything about you is perfect!
I can combine everything about you with the Calamity Seed!
There is no useless part of your body!"
"Very kind of you."
The young Vorhelm stayed there for a moment and did not know how to answer.
"You’re welcome!"
Lian was not sure if the man had even understood the sarcasm, and the cave started moving again.
But this time he did not only defend himself, his eyes moved across the veins.
[True Sequence]
Information entered his mind.
Mana paths, nerve paths, contraction cycles, liquid distribution networks, and the points where Ezrak’s commands were turned into orders.
But there were too many of them, far too many, there were at least hundreds of paths and thousands of branches.
The structure of the cave was not like a skill that could be analyzed by looking at a few main paths.
This was a complete living creature.
Lian dodged several attacks and continued the analysis at the same time, the threads were different, but their sources of energy were connected and the different tissues worked independently.
But in the end, the energy returned to one path.
He jumped over a wall that was closing, a bone claw passed under his foot but he dodged it and landed on an icy platform.
His eyes followed the path of several huge veins, all of them went toward the center of the cave, toward the chamber and more exactly toward the Calamity Seed.
For several seconds, the entire picture came together in his mind.
Blood, nutrients, mana, fresh tissues and even the heat produced in different parts of the cave...all of them eventually reached that creature.
"I understand."
Lian looked at the huge egg.
"What?"
Ezrak, who was standing farther away, smiled.
"That when you said you built this cave for yourself, it was just a lie, wasn’t it?"
The white-eyed man’s smile stopped for a moment, but he continued.
"It isn’t even a laboratory, all of it is a womb, the real purpose of this place isn’t to protect you, this place is a womb for the Calamity Seed...like a mother’s womb for her child."
"The main purpose of this place is to protect the Seed and give it nutrients."
Ezrak said nothing, that was enough...Lian had guessed correctly.
"Now one question remains, why did you try to hide something like this?"
