Ezrak only looked at the scene for several seconds, his face had an expression that even Lian could not tell whether it was anger or confusion.
"You... brought an unknown creature into my unknown creature’s womb so it could steal its corpse from my unknown child?"
"When you say it like that, the plan sounds even better." Lian gave him a short look.
"That was not a compliment!"
"Anyway, if you don’t want to die, stay quiet, don’t forget that your dear child wants to kill you and for now, I am the one standing in its way." Of course, Vorhelm said it mostly in a mocking tone.
This white-eyed bastard could use that bell to leave this place whenever he wanted, at least that was his guess.
But it was interesting that he was still here, maybe he wanted to see the result?
Ezrak’s mouth stayed open for a moment, and he could not find an answer, in fact, he realized that his survival currently depended on this boy.
Unfortunately, he could not run away, otherwise he would have already done it.
But the Saint reacted differently, its black eye moved away from Lian for the first time and fixed itself on the Devouring Egg.
One of the halo’s branches came out of the womb’s corpse, the long bone bent like a spear and moved directly toward the egg.
"I’m not allowing that." Lian moved at the same moment.
[Thunder Step.]
Boom!
He appeared between the Calamity Seed and the egg, at the same moment the branch came down and he placed both feet firmly on the ground.
[Mountain Anchor]
The armor plates on his legs locked onto the surface, the force from his legs entered the ground and he raised both arms.
KAAAAANG!
The bone branch came down on his armored forearms and the ground under his feet sank several meters around him.
His knees bent and new cracks spread across the forearms of the World-Devourer Bastion, blood ran down from his nose.
But he did not move back even one step, and the egg behind him continued eating the womb.
And because of the damage he received, the flow of power in his body increased even more.
[Mental Corruption: 31%]
The Saint raised the branch and this time its entire body came forward, Lian prepared for the second attack, but before the attack landed, another part of the womb was absorbed by the halo.
[New growth stage recorded.]
The young Vorhelm’s expression changed.
Bad.
Very bad!
The branch came down again and Mountain Anchor was still active, he expected to be pushed back, this attack was from a Level 50 creature!.
He was wrong, it was not simply a matter of being pushed back...
BOOOOOOM!
The ground under his feet exploded and Mountain Anchor transferred the force into the ground for a fraction of a second, then the ground itself could no longer تحمل it.
The entire icy and tissue-covered floor under his feet broke.
Lian was separated from the ground and his body went into one of the icy tunnels like a stone thrown by a catapult.
Boom!
The first wall broke.
Boom!
The second.
BOOOOM!
The third.
More than one hundred meters away, he finally stopped inside a mass of ice, he did not move for several seconds and then the fingers of his right hand moved.
Pieces of ice moved aside and he sat up, took a deep breath and pain stabbed into his chest like a knife.
"H..." One of his ribs was not just cracked this time, it was probably broken, and his left hand also shook slightly for several seconds.
The flow of power in his body increased again because of the damage, but it was useless, he was facing an opponent whose power difference was too great, so great that no boost could make up for it.
[Mental Corruption: 47%]
Even so, he did not turn off the skill, the fact that he had still been able to survive this long was thanks to the boosts from Warrior’s Madness.
Lian took out the second bottle and drank it, warmth spread through his body again and the damaged rib was not completely healed, but at least the broken parts were stabilized.
Then he stood up and looked at the Level notification again.
"Level fifty... okay."
"Then I really can’t let you hit me anymore." From now on he could only dodge, if he was hit, staying alive would not be easy.
The sound of ice breaking came from the tunnel... the Saint was getting closer.
The young Vorhelm looked behind him, the exit of the cave could be seen.
The womb still had a lot of food for it, even with the Devouring Egg, the Saint could feed from another part.
So he had to separate that thing from its food, but what did the Saint want more than the womb’s food?
He placed his hand on the center of his chest for a moment, the Ruined Heart was still and unmoving, but the Calamity Seed wanted it.
Lian gave a calm smile, if a hunter wanted its prey, all he needed to do was make the prey go somewhere else.
A few seconds later, the Saint entered the tunnel and its black eye immediately fixed on him and instead of attacking, he turned around and started running.
[Thunder Step]
Boom!
"Where are you going?!" Ezrak, who had reached them from another part, shouted.
"Outside." The time for a strategic retreat had come.
Lian created an ice platform under his feet and crossed a huge gap.
The white-eyed man, seeing that his child was coming after them, no longer had time to ask for the reason and started running with him.
Behind them...
BOOOOOOM!
The Saint did not even use the tunnel anymore and directly broke through the wall, a huge amount of ice and stone scattered around.
The six-meter body passed through it and one branch of the halo entered the wall, suddenly, gravitational pressure appeared behind the young Vorhelm.
His body was pulled backward for a moment, but he grabbed the ceiling with his hand.
[Suppressing Palm]
This time the target was not the Saint.
Boom!
The ceiling several dozen meters ahead of the creature collapsed and hundreds of tons of ice and stone fell onto the path.
The creature disappeared under the rubble, it was not supposed to be hurt, but at least it could buy some time.
Lian did not even look back.
Three seconds.
That was all he wanted.
Three seconds of time.
[Ash Step]
He passed through a narrow section where the dead womb was collapsing.
[Thunder Step]
The distance became larger, but suddenly there was an explosion behind him and the Saint came out from the rubble.
But the three seconds had been spent and enough distance had been created.
Lian passed beside the main section of the laboratory, the Devouring Egg was still eating and huge masses of tissue were drying one after another.
Parts of the cave were collapsing because the biological structure was being destroyed.
"My laboratory!" Ezrak almost shouted when he saw the scene.
"Do you prefer your life or this cave?"
"Both!"
"If you don’t sacrifice something, you’ll lose both."
"I really hate you!"
Lian did not answer, the mouth of the cave could be seen ahead, the white land of Antarctica could be seen from there.
He activated the last Thunder Step he needed inside the cave, his body jumped out of the entrance and the icy wind immediately hit his armor.
As far as the eye could see, there was only white, huge amounts of snow, ice, and mountains that disappeared in the distance under the gray sky.
He landed on the ice and two seconds later...
BOOOOOOOOM!
Part of the mountain behind him exploded, pieces of ice as large as houses flew through the air and the Unborn Saint came directly out of the wall.
Its entire body could be seen under the cold light of Antarctica and the bone halo behind its head was open like a twisted crown.
Golden-black veins shone under its white skin and the strands behind its body moved in the wind like incomplete wings.
Ezrak also came out of the entrance a few moments later, he looked inside the cave and then at the Devouring Egg that was still there.
His face twisted, but he had no time to complain.
The Saint released the stored materials inside its body and the golden veins became brighter.
New pressure appeared in the area and this time even the snowy wind coming toward the Saint was pushed away before reaching its body.
Lian slowly breathed out, the battle was not over, it had only changed its form, and now he had to face a Level 55 bastard.
The Saint disappeared.
Predator’s Instincts suddenly screamed.
Left, the attack was coming from the left!
The young Vorhelm activated Ash Step without looking and those long white fingers passed directly through the place where his head had been a moment ago.
He appeared behind the Saint.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
Crack!
The claw hit the back of the creature’s knee, the tissue and tendon of part of the joint were cut.
[Cataclysm Pulse]
Boom!
The explosive wave did not even push the Saint back and it did not seem to feel anything from any of these attacks.
The young Vorhelm moved back at the same moment, just as he had thought, attacking was useless, this thing could no longer even feel his attacks.
The Saint turned around and its gaze fell on him again, on the thing it needed to complete itself.

chapters.title: Chapter 475: The Unborn Saint VI ( PS Bonus - )
paragraphs: "Okay, how about you stop attacking just this once?" Lian looked at the Unborn Saint and said with a smile.
But the creature ignored him, and its fingers moved toward him again, much faster than before.
[False Presence]
A similar presence moved in another direction, and the Saint could sense the real Lian, but for a few tenths of a second, its new senses also reacted to the other presence.
Those few tenths of a second were enough, and the young Vorhelm came down from above.
[Giant’s Momentum]
[Iron Fortress Charge]
The armored shoulder hit the Saint’s back.
Bــــــom!
Of course, the goal was not to hurt it, he had already understood that it was impossible with such a level difference between them, and his goal was to change its direction.
The Calamity Seed went straight into a valley of ice blades that he had created using Frost Dominion.
Seven blades broke along its path, and the young Vorhelm touched the ground with his palm.
[Thunder Calamity]
Krrrrr!
Lightning passed through the ice network, and this time the Saint’s body was not the main target, the ground under it exploded and its support was destroyed.
The creature fell into a deep crack, and Lian immediately moved away, while Ezrak, who was hiding behind a pillar, saw him for a moment.
His clothes and armor were full of cracks, and blood could be seen on part of his face, but his movements were still without hesitation.
"Amazing..." he quietly said.
A few seconds later, the crack exploded and the Saint came out, its growth was continuing.
At the same moment, Glacial Reaper Claw cut one of the white strands behind its body, and Thunder Calamity paralyzed another strand for a moment.
Cataclysm Pulse broke the distance, and Ash Step allowed Lian to escape from the deadly response.
Every skill he had was no longer an independent weapon, but had become part of a chain for survival.
But mana was not endless, and the Calamity Seed was still growing.
[Growth: 87.2%.]
[Growth: 89.1%.]
[Growth: 90%.]
The creature stopped for a moment, its body changed, its muscles became denser, the branches of its bone halo became thicker, and its white skin became less transparent.
But the strangest change was in its movements, it was no longer rushing, instead, it became calm.
Like a creature that had finally understood that it did not need to hurry.
The young Vorhelm activated Thunder Step, and the Saint only turned its head, its black eye followed his path.
Its hand came up.
Tap.
The white fingers closed around Lian’s throat, and his eyes opened slightly wider for a moment.
It had caught him.
In the middle of Thunder Step, without a gravity field and without any preparation, but only through its own reaction, he had not even noticed when or how it had done it!
The Saint lifted his body, its fingers tightened, and the bones of the armored neck began to make cracking sounds.
Because of the damage he received, the flow of power in his body increased again.
[Mental Corruption: 56%]
Lian placed his palm directly on the creature’s face, ready to use a large amount of his mana to get out of this situation.
[Cataclysm Pulse]
Booooom!
The Saint’s head moved backward, its grip loosened for a moment, and that moment was enough to give him a chance to use Ash Step.
His body turned into ash, but the creature reacted faster than before, and before his body could fully reform, its hands moved.
Kaaabooooom!
The attack hit the back of the World-Devourer Bastion directly, and he was thrown across the ice like a black meteor.
One hundred meters.
Two hundred meters.
Almost three hundred meters.
The ice behind him cracked, and he finally stopped on his side.
[Structural Memory activated.]
The cracks in the armor were slowly repairing themselves, and the two back plates were almost destroyed.
He coughed and blood fell onto the icy ground, and he drank another healing potion, and before he even finished, he took out a fourth bottle.
He drank the fourth potion as well.
Then he looked at his condition, it was very bad.
[Mental Corruption: 71%]
If he kept getting injured like this, sooner or later madness would take over his mind, and on the other hand, without that boost, he would have no power to continue.
His opponent had reached Level 60!
[Remaining Mana: 9%.]
Lian looked at the number for a few seconds, his breathing was no longer completely calm and every deep breath caused pain, several parts of his armor were still repairing themselves.
"You’re losing." Ezrak said.
"That was a very accurate observation, did you use your genius for this too?" The young Vorhelm looked at him.
"I’m serious! If you hadn’t killed the womb, we wouldn’t have this problem!"
"Me too, if you hadn’t created this thing, it wouldn’t have mattered whether the womb died or not, at least you could have put a destruction mechanism in it." He stood up again.
The Saint was slowly coming toward him through the storm, and every step broke the ice around its feet.
The young Vorhelm no longer planned to attack directly, he looked at the battlefield.
An idea formed, if he could not defeat this creature, he would force it to move through a place where every meter had already been prepared for him.
He could use Frost Dominion to fill the area with traps, but this idea also had a problem.
How long could he keep doing this? His mana was running out, and it was unlikely that he could keep going for long.
Maybe it was time to use his biggest trump card, the power of Black Silence?
Then he lowered both hands and sent the rest of his mana into the ground.
But this time, the ice did not grow on the surface, instead, a network was created deep underground.
One kilometer.
Two kilometers.
The ice branches connected to each other in the layers under Antarctica, and then [Thunder Calamity] activated.
Lightning entered the network and created hundreds of explosion points underground underground.
The Saint came closer and Lian moved backward, when the creature’s foot stepped on the first point, a second finger closed.
Booooom!
One hundred meters of ground under the creature exploded and it fell downward.
Lian used Thunder Step.
[Remaining Mana: 7%.]
The Saint came out of the crack and reached the second point.
Booooom!
The second explosion happened from the side and caused it to move several dozen meters away from its path.
The young Vorhelm moved behind a rock.
[Remaining Mana: 5%.]
The Saint no longer had a straight path, wherever it stepped, the ground changed shape, one part collapsed and another part rose.
An ice rock blocked its path and an explosion changed its direction.
The entire area had turned into Lian’s chessboard.
The creature was stronger, much stronger, but power was not enough to hit something that was not where it was expected to be.
[Remaining Mana: 3%.]
Three new pillars came out, created by him, and the Calamity Seed broke one of them.
Lian jumped around it from one place to another, pulling it in whatever direction he wanted so he could make it step into the traps.
[Remaining Mana: 2%.]
But the Saint was now almost complete, and the remaining biological resources in its body began to be used.
[Growth: 92.4%.]
[Growth: 94.8%.]
[Growth: 96%.]
[New growth stage recorded.]
The storm became silent for a moment, and the pressure of the creature’s existence spread like an invisible wave, and the snow around its body moved away without even touching it.
The ground under its feet sank, even the World-Devourer Bastion on Lian’s body made a quiet sound, and Predator’s Instincts activated.
But this time there was no direction for an attack, instead, only one simple thought appeared in his mind.
Death danger.
Death danger.
The Saint disappeared, even its first movement could not be seen.
[Ash Step]
The young Vorhelm’s body turned into ash at the last moment, and the white fingers of the monster passed through it.
Lian appeared a few meters away.
[Remaining Mana: 1%.]
He looked at the number.
"Great."
The Saint suddenly turned its head away from him, and its black eye landed on Ezrak, the white-eyed man immediately became silent.
"No."
One of the five complete branches of the halo turned toward him.
The madman took one step back, but a gravitational pressure fell on his body, as if something he himself had created had decided to kill him first.
Boom!
Both of his knees hit the ice.
"Damn it!" Even in this situation, he did not use the bell... because he could not anymore!
The Saint turned its gaze back to Lian.
Ezrak was the second target.
Lian was still the first priority.
But this time, the creature did not run toward him, the five complete branches of the halo behind it slowly opened and one after another separated from its body.
The young Vorhelm narrowed his eyes, each branch was like a huge spear that stabbed into a different point of the ice.
The first, one hundred meters to the east.
The second in the south.
The third in the west.
The fourth in the north.
The fifth appeared at a farther distance.
The ground shook and columns of black-gold light rose from the ice into the sky.
The wind stopped... then its direction changed and the snow began to fall upward.
Small pieces of ice separated from the ground, then larger pieces, rocks weighing several tons, and all of them remained floating in the air.
Lian raised his head, the sky above the area became dark, and a huge ring formed between the five pillars.
Then a second ring.
Third.
Fourth.
Fifth.
Huge circles made of white bones and black-gold mana rotated inside each other.
Like a heavenly crown.
What the hell was this thing doing now?

chapters.title: Chapter 476: The Unborn Saint ( Final )
paragraphs: The thing that was supposed to come down to carry out the final judgment was the incomplete sixth branch behind the Unborn Saint.
But unlike the others, it did not separate and instead pointed directly at Lian’s chest.
Predator’s Instincts gave only one command.
Run.
This was a warning of certain death, if he did not run, his only possible fate would definitely be death.
He looked around, one question remained, where? Where was he supposed to run?
The gravitational pressure had sealed off several kilometers around him, Ash Step could only move him a few meters, and he had only one percent of his mana left.
Thunder Step might work one more time, and after that all his mana would be gone.
The sky above him filled with hundreds of bone spears, and the tips of all of them pointed downward.
At the same time, the ice under Lian’s feet began to rise, and a huge part of the ground was pushed toward the sky like an upside-down mountain.
He was surrounded from both above and below, and both results meant death.
The Saint planned to crush him between the sky and the ground.
He raised his head, and hundreds of spears began to shake, and at the same moment, the creature’s hand came down and the entire sky fell.
And ...Boom!

Lian waited for the explosion, he was not worried about death, the Extra Life he had could bring him back to life once, and after returning to life, all his mana would return to its peak and his condition would also return to normal.
It was a shame to waste an Extra Life again so soon, but that thing was exactly for events like this.
But the explosion ...did not come.
His eyes narrowed slightly, the spears had stopped, and hundreds of thousands of pieces of bone were floating motionless dozens of meters above his head.
The floating pieces of ice did not move, and the five huge rings had stopped moving.
Even the snow particles seemed to be frozen in the air for a moment.
At first, Lian thought time had stopped, but no, he could feel himself breathing and Ezrak was also moving, so time had not stopped.
"What the hell is this?" Then a voice came from above, the voice was calm.
The young Vorhelm raised his head, and a man was standing on one of the huge floating pieces of ice, his face was calm and both hands were inside the pockets of his clothes.
His dark hair moved around his face in the weak wind.

There was no huge aura around his body, and there was no great display of mana coming from him, but this very man was standing in the center of an attack that only a few moments ago had been described by Lian’s Predator’s Instincts with one word.
Death.
His eyes opened slightly wider for a moment, he knew this face, in fact, almost every man in the world and everyone who had access to the internet knew him.
Overlord Orion, known as Mountainbreaker.
Orion did not even look at Lian at first, his eyes stayed on the Unborn Saint, and his right eyebrow rose slightly.
"A Calamity Seed?" He examined it for a few seconds, then his frown became slightly deeper.
His eyes moved over the bone halo and the creature’s body structure.
"It’s artificial?"
Even his voice contained a small amount of surprise.
Ezrak, who was still on one knee under the pressure, slowly lowered his head, hoping he would not be noticed, but ...he was wrong.
"You." Orion’s gaze fell on him.
"Hello?" The white-eyed man gave an awkward smile.
But the Overlord ignored him for now.
The Unborn Saint still did not know what it was facing, and the heavenly rings began to shake again.
Its pressure increased, and all the spears tried to come down.
Orion let out a short sigh, took his right hand out of his pocket, did nothing special, and simply raised his palm.
Then he closed his fist.
The space became heavy for a moment.
Krrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrack!

chapters.title: Chapter 477: This Is an Overlord
paragraphs: The Unborn Saint did not move anymore.
Its six-meter body was buried inside a deep crater, and Orion’s foot was placed right in the center of its chest.
The five complete branches of the bone-like halo were buried in the ice, the huge black eye on its mouthless face was still open, but even it no longer dared to move.
Lian stood a few dozen meters away..what caught his attention the most was the way this Overlord acted, he had heard that he had one of the most chill personalities among all the Overlords.
But now he understood that even the news and rumors had greatly underestimated how chill he was.
Mountainbreaker looked at the creature under his foot for a few seconds without saying anything, then he slightly reduced the pressure of his foot.
At that moment...crack...the sound of moving bones came.
Young Vorhelm narrowed his eyes slightly and the Saint’s chest, which had been completely crushed under Orion’s pressure, started to change.
It was not only healing, the bones slowly separated from each other and their angles changed.
Some became thicker, while others created a new layer around themselves, and even now its body was still finding a way to adapt.
Orion raised an eyebrow.
"Interesting." He said as he increased the weight of his foot on the Saint’s chest again.
"The more I crush it, the more its body looks for a new way to avoid being crushed next time."
Crack!
The bones that were changing broke again.
"That’s exactly why I stopped trying to kill it with force after a certain point." Lian said calmly.
Orion gave him a short look, there was no exaggerated praise or surprise in his eyes, only a calm sense of approval.
"You made the right choice." He looked at the creature under his foot again.
"Killing something that learns from every time you kill it is a very good way to create an even bigger problem."
He studied the creature for a few more moments, then reached into his storage space and when he pulled his hand out, a small object was between his fingers.
A black hexagonal prism, almost the size of his palm.
There were no clear marks on its surface, but even Lian could feel the strange amount of space compressed around it just by looking at it.
Orion dropped the prism onto the ice.
Tap.
The object landed right beside the Saint...then it opened, six thin black plates separated from the main body and floated into six different directions around the Saint.
One above.
One below.
The other four around it.
The space between the plates suddenly became dark, and the Saint’s black eye changed slightly, as if it had noticed something, and the bone-like halo behind its head moved.
Gravity pressure burst out from its body and the ground around the crater started to crack.
It was as if it had finally understood what fear was, and its instincts were telling it that it should not let itself get trapped inside that hexagonal prism.
"I said calm down." But the Overlord only pressed his foot harder against its chest.
Boom!
The entire body of the Calamity Seed sank a few more centimeters into the ice, the gravity pressure collapsed at the same moment and the six black plates lit up at the same time.
Then something strange happened, the space between them seemed to fold.
Lian could not fully follow it with his eyes, the Unborn Saint was still the same size but at the same time the distance between it and him was becoming larger.
One meter.
Ten meters.
One hundred meters.
One thousand meters.
Without actually becoming smaller, it was as if an endless distance was forming between it and this world.
The black eye could still be seen, the halo was still struggling, but it was getting farther away every second and then everything disappeared.
The six black plates returned toward the center, came together and in less than two seconds became the same small prism that Orion had taken out of his clothes.
The man bent down and picked it up.
His eyes stayed on the prism in Orion’s hand, it was not hard to guess that it was probably some kind of dimensional prison.
It was not a bad idea either.
At least until they found a way to truly destroy the Saint, keeping it somewhere where it could not grow made more sense than trying to kill it.
Of course, he knew that Mountainbreaker and the Federation’s main goal was to research that thing.
But now there was one more person left.
Lian slowly turned his head toward Ezrak, the white-eyed man understood at the same moment and calmly took two steps back.
Orion put his other hand inside his clothes, and another black prism came out.
"I don’t think you’ll need that for me." Ezrak gave a small smile.
But Mountainbreaker did not even answer him and only turned the prism between two fingers.
Lian was looking at the man, but his mind was focused on that bell, this crazy man had been in danger all this time and still had not used it.
The same bell that had brought them directly from the base under the mountain to Antarctica.
And that was exactly what made something click in his mind, from the moment they arrived in Antarctica, Ezrak had many chances to escape.
When he was killing the womb, when the Saint woke up earlier than expected, when the creature attacked him and when the Overlord arrived.
Even a few moments ago, when Mountainbreaker had put all his attention on the Saint.
But he had only used the bell once, the very first time.
So that thing was not unlimited, maybe it had a recovery time, maybe using it required certain conditions.
Maybe each use consumed part of his soul or his own power.
Whatever the reason was, Ezrak could not simply disappear whenever he wanted.
Orion seemed to be prepared for that as well.
"I saw the recording of your escape from the base, so I’m not going to make the same mistake they did this time."
The prism slipped from his hand.
Tap.
The six plates opened.
The white-eyed man did not wait this time.
Two small objects came out from under his clothes, one looked like a piece of dried meat. The other was a thin bone covered with green mana lines.
But before he could activate either of them, Orion looked at him.
Just a look.
A huge pressure like an invisible mountain fell on Ezrak’s body.
Boom!
Both his knees hit the ice, the objects fell from his hands and his white eyes opened wider for a moment.
"That’s really unfair."
"Life isn’t fair."
"That was such a cliché answer."
"Shut up, or instead of sending you to prison, I’ll send you directly to the rest of your destroyed civilization."
"I understand..."
The black plates lit up, the space folded again and this time Ezrak did not resist much.
But before the distance between himself and the world became larger, he looked at Lian, a very small smile appeared on his face.
A calm and strange smile, as if it was saying something without words ...we’ll meet again.
Young Vorhelm showed no reaction, but strangely, deep inside, he agreed with it.
A few seconds later, the crazy scientist also disappeared, the prism closed and Orion picked it up and put it inside his clothes.
For a moment, silence covered the icy plain.
Two major problems had been contained, at least for now, and then he turned his eyes toward the mountain.
Lian also looked in the same direction without thinking, a large part of the cave entrance had collapsed and the dead flesh of the womb was stuck to the walls like dried skin.
But something was strange, parts of the cave were simply missing, as if they had been eaten.
The Overlord looked at it for a few seconds, as if he was thinking how it was possible for part of a cave to have been eaten..?
Lian remembered at the same moment, the Devourer Egg.
He naturally had not forgotten it during the entire fight with the Saint, he simply did not have the chance to deal with it.
The last time, he had left it inside the cave to consume the huge body of the womb, now that everything was over, he had to take it back.
Vorhelm focused for a moment, but there was no sign of the egg, and he did not know if that was a good thing or not, because if Mountainbreaker saw the egg, he would definitely take it as well.
And just as he expected, Orion entered the destroyed cave to investigate and he also followed him.
A few minutes later, they returned to the center of the former laboratory, or what was left of it.
A large part of the womb had completely dried up, the empty biological tubes and the huge masses of flesh that the Devourer Egg had reached had almost become dry shells.
But the egg itself was gone and there was still no sign of it.
The Overlord stopped at the exact place where Lian had left it and bent down, touching some of the dried flesh with two fingers.
"Something was here."
He only nodded.
"Looks like it."
"Whatever it was, it looks like it ate quite a lot too." Orion looked around.

Young Vorhelm showed no reaction, but strangely, deep inside, he agreed with it.
A few seconds later, the crazy scientist also disappeared, the prism closed and Orion picked it up and put it inside his clothes.
For a moment, silence covered the icy plain.
Two major problems had been contained, at least for now, and then he turned his eyes toward the mountain.
Lian also looked in the same direction without thinking, a large part of the cave entrance had collapsed and the dead flesh of the womb was stuck to the walls like dried skin.
But something was strange, parts of the cave were simply missing, as if they had been eaten.
The Overlord looked at it for a few seconds, as if he was thinking how it was possible for part of a cave to have been eaten..?
Lian remembered at the same moment, the Devourer Egg.
He naturally had not forgotten it during the entire fight with the Saint, he simply did not have the chance to deal with it.
The last time, he had left it inside the cave to consume the huge body of the womb, now that everything was over, he had to take it back.
Vorhelm focused for a moment, but there was no sign of the egg, and he did not know if that was a good thing or not, because if Mountainbreaker saw the egg, he would definitely take it as well.
And just as he expected, Orion entered the destroyed cave to investigate and he also followed him.
A few minutes later, they returned to the center of the former laboratory, or what was left of it.
A large part of the womb had completely dried up, the empty biological tubes and the huge masses of flesh that the Devourer Egg had reached had almost become dry shells.
But the egg itself was gone and there was still no sign of it.
The Overlord stopped at the exact place where Lian had left it and bent down, touching some of the dried flesh with two fingers.
"Something was here."
He only nodded.
"Looks like it."
"Whatever it was, it looks like it ate quite a lot too." Orion looked around.

chapters.title: Chapter 478: The Egg That Disappeared
paragraphs: Lian stayed silent, that part was obvious, with the appetite that egg had, it was clear that it would eat anything in its path.
What was not clear was the egg’s current location.
There was no shell left and no sign of it breaking, not even a trail on the ground and not even a hole that could show that something had taken it from below.
Ed only stared at the empty spot for a few seconds.
Had it escaped? The thought was so ridiculous that he raised an eyebrow for a moment.
How could an egg escape? Did it roll away? Grow legs? Or maybe it was no longer an egg?
That last thought was not as funny, that egg unfortunately had nothing in common with a normal egg, what kind of egg was even aware?
His expression became a little more serious, but before he could investigate more, Orion’s voice came.
"Anyway, whatever was here is no longer here, and I can’t feel any trace of it either."
Lian nodded again, it was also good news that this man had not been able to find the egg, and it was also clear that he currently had more important things to deal with.
He was also sure that the Federation would soon send an elite team here to search both this womb and almost the entire area, just in case Ezrak had hidden something else here.
Still, he did not like the idea of an unknown creature that belonged to him being lost in Antarctica.
"Gareth is waiting for you." The Overlord then raised his hand and moved it without saying anything else.
Before Lian could say anything, white light covered his entire vision.
One moment he was in Antarctica, and the next moment his feet were on a metal floor.
He blinked and looked around, black walls, cold lights on the ceiling, and it was not hard to know where he was, the same facility under the mountain.
And right in front of him stood Gareth, the commander was standing beside a large table with several people.

He stopped in the middle of his sentence and his eyes immediately locked onto him, and when he saw that he was safe, the pressure that had been sitting on his face for several hours disappeared in an instant.
"Damn..." He let out a deep breath and rubbed his face for a moment.
"Good. You’re alive."
"I’m glad to see you too." Vorhelm’s young man said calmly.
The commander spent a few more seconds making sure there was no immediate problem, then gave a short look behind Lian.
"Mountainbreaker found you?" Of course, it did not sound like a question, he seemed almost certain.
"Yeah."
"Then it’s over."
Lian thought for a moment about the two black prisms that were now with Orion.
"I guess, for now."
Gareth raised his eyebrows slightly, but decided not to ask for now and put his hand on one of his people’s shoulders.
"Call a healer, I want his condition checked."
"I’m not that badly hurt."
"I need to make sure you’re okay, otherwise both your uncle and your teacher Aldric won’t let me off easily."
Lian did not answer, he was not surprised that the commander knew his uncle, after all, his uncle was a very well-known person.
And about his concern regarding Teacher Aldric’s reaction, considering that he was his favorite student...or at least that was how it seemed, it was normal too.
A little later, the World Devouring Fortress had been removed from Lian’s body.
The first examination showed that his injuries were serious, but there was nothing that could not be stabilized with rest, the right potion and a few hours of time.
The armor itself was also repairing thanks to Structural Memory and it should not take too long for it to fully recover.
Gareth waited until the examination was finished, and when the doctor left, he sat in front of him.
"So, why exactly did that madman take you?"
Lian thought for a few seconds, not to make a lie but to decide how much of the truth he should tell.
In the end, he chose the simplest version.

"He had seen some kind of potential in me before, apparently he decided from the first time that he wanted to use my body as part of his next monster, he also said some things about the Calamity Seed and making a much stronger creature. That the creature he was making could become something even stronger."
He shrugged.
"Honestly, I’m not sure which parts of what he said were true and which parts were just the nonsense of a madman."
That sentence was not completely a lie, he had only left out a very large part of the truth.

Besides, he could not change everything either, first, Overlord Orion knew about the Calamity Seed and had taken that madman for interrogation, and he personally doubted that Ezrak would be able to stay silent anymore.
"You said he wanted to make another monster, the Overlord was able to capture that creature?" Gareth slowly nodded.
"Yeah."

"Good, losing it could have destroyed a lot of information. Especially if it really was artificially created, as for the white-eyed man himself, he will probably go directly under Strategic Supervision."
"So they won’t bring him back here anymore?" Lian kept his eyes on him.

"Unlikely, after what we saw today, no sane person would put him in the same kind of prison again. The man escaped from one of the safest facilities in the country and even the arrays did not understand how."
Then he added.
"Most likely, from now on he will be kept directly under the watch of the Overlords and the higher parts of the Federation."
"Does that mean I can’t see him anymore?" The young Vorhelm paused for a moment.
Gareth became silent.
One second.
Two seconds.
Then he started laughing, and the young Vorhelm looked at him without changing his expression.
"What?"
"Are you serious?"
"Yeah."
"Lian, that man kidnapped you."
Lian stayed silent, and the commander raised another eyebrow.
"He took you to the middle of nowhere and wanted to use your body to make his monster." And in the end he stared at him for a few seconds.
"Why do you want to see him again? Do you miss him?"
"I became interested in his work." Lian answered with complete seriousness.
"You have some problems too." Gareth’s laugh stopped, and he stared at him for a few seconds before saying very calmly.
"Maybe." He shrugged in response.
But the real reason was completely different, Ezrak had information, information that could be very useful to him.
That man knew about the Five Calamities, the Calamity Seeds, and the Sixth Position, and it was clearly possible that he even knew more.
And there was something that was more important to Lian than all of those.
The Anchor and Vessel of their world, with Ezrak’s information, it might be possible to identify them.
And if that madman really had information about the Calamities, worlds, and how to destroy them, he might know something that could help Lian later.
"Forget about him for now." Gareth gave the table a short tap with his hand.
Lian looked at him.

"It’s unlikely that the Federation will allow anyone to even get close to him without direct permission, but don’t worry about his work. If the knowledge of the Valkaris is really useful, sooner or later we’ll get something out of him." He gave a faint smile.
"I hope so." The young Vorhelm nodded, as if he had to let it go for now.
But his inner feeling said something else.
Dimensional prison, Overlord, Strategic Security, or whatever name they wanted to give it.
He did not feel that Ezrak’s story had ended inside that prism.

A man who had managed to cross from his own world, hide on Earth for years, and escape from one of the Federation’s safest prisons without activating a single warning would not stay inside a box forever that easily.
He did not know when, but he was sure he would see Ezrak again.
After a few more checks and changing his damaged clothes, a military vehicle took Lian out of the facility.
When he returned to the academy, the sun was still in the sky.
Students were moving around the grounds.
Two people beside the path were talking about the exam results, while another group was laughing.
Someone was talking about the organizations that had come to recruit the top students.
Life continued completely normally.

None of them knew that a few hours earlier, thousands of kilometers away, a creature had been born earlier than it should have, and the System considered the result of its completion to be "A Calamity Released into the World."
Lian also had no intention of telling anyone, he entered the dormitory building, went up the stairs and opened the door to his room.
He expected it to be empty, Kain should have already returned to the Ruined Realm by now, considering how much he wanted to go there.
But he was still there.
His best friend was sitting on a chair and checking something on a small screen, and when the door opened, he raised his head.
"Where were you?" And he stared at him for a few seconds.
"An interrogation." Lian entered and closed the door behind him.
"An interrogation?"
His eyes moved from head to toe, his clothes had been changed, he had changed clothes in the middle of an interrogation.
Kain raised an eyebrow.
"Why do you look like someone who just came back from a war?"
"The interrogation took a long time."
The Child of Light looked at him without saying anything, Lian also looked at him and they stared at each other in silence for a few seconds.
"Never mind..."

chapters.title: Chapter 479: Time To Hunt
paragraphs: "So, what’s your plan now?" Kain looked at him for a few more moments.
"I’m going back to the Ruined Realm." Lian already knew the answer and had made his decision.
"For hunting?"
"Yeah. My level has been stuck at twenty-three for a while. For now, I want to focus on raising it."
His next goal was clear.
The second evolution.
And the difference in power he had seen against Orion today had only reminded him more of how much further he still had to go, of course, he also planned to collect as many Fragments as possible.
He still had not had the time or chance to use any of the abilities from his first evolution, simply because he could not afford their cost.
"Base #3?"
"No. #9." The young Vorhelm shook his head.
"Really there? I thought you would go back to our country’s base." Kain raised an eyebrow.
"Yeah, did you find anything new around Base #3?"
"Honestly, no, after the path opened and we were able to move forward, we went quite far, but I can’t say we reached anything special, there were a few dungeons, but they were cleared."
Lian nodded, that was what he expected.
"There are some good hunting areas around Base #9. At least that’s what the reports say." That was what he had heard about it.
Besides, that base was one of the biggest ones and there were several uncleared dungeons and very good hunting areas around it.
"So you want to level up there?"
"For now."
"Then I’m coming too." Kain said almost immediately.
"Are you sure?"
He shrugged.
"I don’t have anything special to do here. I also want to get closer to my second evolution sooner, and I haven’t had a chance to go to Base #9 until now, I think it’s not a bad idea to do it now."
"Alright." Lian nodded and then suddenly remembered something and tilted his head slightly.
"By the way..."
"What?"
"What did you do with my old mount? I’m sure I gave it to you before I left."
"I sold it." This time Kain looked away for a second.
"You sold it?" The young Vorhelm stayed still for a few moments, even though he no longer needed it, he had not expected it to be sold.
"You were gone for nine months!" His friend immediately became defensive and opened his hands.
"Did you expect me to keep that poor thing somewhere until it rotted? It needed food, it needed a place, it needed care. Besides, we didn’t even know if you would come back."
Lian looked at him for a few seconds, Kain had clearly been preparing for this conversation for a long time, and in the end he nodded.
"No. You did the right thing."
"That’s it?"
"What?"
"Weren’t you going to yell at me?"
"You wanted me to yell at you?" The young Vorhelm raised an eyebrow.
"No, but I was prepared for an argument." He had expected to hear at least a few complaints, but even that did not happen.
But he really had not made the wrong decision, and even if he had not sold it, Lian probably would not have had any use for his old mount anymore.
With One, it was unlikely that he would even have the chance to pay attention to it.
A while later, Kain stood up from the chair and put the few things he had left into his storage space.
"I have to go to Base #3 first, I have a few things and some unfinished work there. I’ll take care of them and get to #9 tomorrow."
"No problem." Lian nodded.
"Just don’t go find another problem before then, at least wait until I come too and we can find one together."
"I won’t promise, but I’ll try, you know, it’s not my fault either, problems come looking for me themselves."
"Sometimes I really can’t tell if you’re joking or not." Kain stared at him for a moment and sighed, then left the room and closed the door behind him.
The room became silent again and Lian sat there for a few seconds.
He was about to open the System panel when he felt something, as if a part of his existence had suddenly become lighter for a moment.
His eyebrows came together and at that moment small black particles separated from around his body.
One.
Ten.
Hundreds of particles.
He quickly stood up from the bed and the particles gathered in front of him, first taking the shape of an unclear mass, then a circle and finally the shape of an egg.
The young Vorhelm’s eyes became slightly wider for a moment.
The Devouring Egg.
The same egg that had disappeared in Antarctica a few hours ago was now sitting very quietly on the floor of the room.
He stared at it without saying anything for a few seconds.
"So you can do this kind of thing too?" he asked quietly.
The egg moved very clearly and the top of its shell bent forward once, as if it had nodded.
Lian stayed silent for a moment and then a short laugh came from his throat.
"Good."
Now at least he knew how it had disappeared from Antarctica.
Apparently, after finishing its feeding, the egg had somehow connected itself to him again and returned with him.
Not bad, this way even Overlord Orion had not noticed it.
He bent down and placed his palm on the shell, as if he wanted to pat it, and at the same time a quiet notification appeared.
[Devouring Egg.]
[Embryo Formation Progress: 31%.]
Lian’s eyes became slightly wider, thirty-one percent, before eating the womb, the amount had been much lower.

So that cave had helped it a lot, which also made sense, it had eaten at least hundreds of tons of biomass, artificial samples, growth materials and womb tissue that had been made to feed a Calamity Seed.
It was no surprise that the egg had been able to make such a big jump.
"Good, good." He gently moved his hand over the shell several times.
The egg moved a little, as if it was happy with the praise, and a small smile appeared on Lian’s face.
"Don’t worry."
His eyes moved toward his storage space, he still had many corpses inside.
"I have more meals for you too."
The egg moved again, as if its appetite had awakened again.
"When we reach the Ruined Realm, I’ll let you eat all of them."
He touched the egg again, this time black particles separated from its surface and within a few seconds, its entire body turned into light and dark particles and disappeared back into his body.
Lian looked at the empty spot for a few moments, so Ezrak was not the only one who had strange things related to movement.
He would have to investigate this later too, but for now it was time to leave.
He opened the System panel.
Kain had to use a gate to enter the Ruined Realm, almost everyone did the same.
But not him, after surviving as one of the twenty-five thousand victims of the first transfer, the System had given him a special reward.
A reward that he had not been able to use for a long time because he had not had the chance, but now the time to use it had finally come.
[Return to the Ruined Realm.]
[This ability was given as a survival reward from the first transfer of the victims.]
[Conditions for use:]
[Can only be used from the original world.]
[Only previously registered return points can be selected.]
[The transfer of other people is not possible.]
[Do you want to enter the Ruined Realm?]
[Yes / No]
Lian looked at the panel for a few seconds and a very small smile appeared on his face.
[Yes.]
The panel changed.
[Select your return point.]
Three options appeared.
[Dreadmaw Mountains.]
[Base #3.]
[Base #9.]
His eyes stopped on the first option, the Dreadmaw Mountains, and for a moment, memories returned to his mind.
The village that he had found with Seris for the first time and where he had almost been killed, and the creature that he had thought was impossible to fight at that time.
An Unholy.
At that time, his only choice had been to run when facing such a creature, what could he have done? Even being able to escape had been a miracle by itself.
But now? He was level twenty-three, he had completed his first evolution, he had an Ancient-rank armor along with several Divine skills and experience that he had not even had one year ago.
Lian’s eyes narrowed for a moment, if he returned to that mountain now, would he still have to run?
It was an interesting question, very interesting.
His finger moved toward the first option for a moment, but then stopped.
No.
Not yet.
He had seen enough creatures today whose power was greater than he had expected.
He was not going to enter another deadly battle just because of his curiosity.
"Later." He could hunt that Unholy later too.
His eyes moved down.
Base #3 and then #9.
His current goal was simple, raise his level, hunt, obtain Fragments and move toward his second evolution.
[Base #9 selected.]
[Transfer beginning.]
Light appeared under his feet, but he did not feel any strange pressure on his soul.
The System’s transfer was calm, and his feet first turned into particles of light, then his body, his hands, his head, and a few seconds later the dorm room was empty.
Lian appeared again, and when he opened his eyes, he was standing in the middle of the transfer platform of Base #9.
Two guards near the platform looked at him in surprise for a moment.
It was clear that seeing someone enter directly without activating the gate was not something they saw every day.
He ignored them and a notification appeared in front of him.
[Welcome to the Ruined Realm.]
[Current Location: Base #9.]
He looked past the buildings around him, then at the tall walls of the base and beyond them at the huge and unknown lands that continued to the horizon.
It was time to hunt.

Besides, we didn’t even know if you would come back."
Lian looked at him for a few seconds, Kain had clearly been preparing for this conversation for a long time, and in the end he nodded.
"No.
You did the right thing."
"That’s it?"
"What?"
"Weren’t you going to yell at me?"
"You wanted me to yell at you?" The young Vorhelm raised an eyebrow.
"No, but I was prepared for an argument." He had expected to hear at least a few complaints, but even that did not happen.
But he really had not made the wrong decision, and even if he had not sold it, Lian probably would not have had any use for his old mount anymore.
With One, it was unlikely that he would even have the chance to pay attention to it.
A while later, Kain stood up from the chair and put the few things he had left into his storage space.
"I have to go to Base #3 first, I have a few things and some unfinished work there.
I’ll take care of them and get to #9 tomorrow."
"No problem." Lian nodded.
"Just don’t go find another problem before then, at least wait until I come too and we can find one together."
"I won’t promise, but I’ll try, you know, it’s not my fault either, problems come looking for me themselves."
"Sometimes I really can’t tell if you’re joking or not." Kain stared at him for a moment and sighed, then left the room and closed the door behind him.
The room became silent again and Lian sat there for a few seconds.
He was about to open the System panel when he felt something, as if a part of his existence had suddenly become lighter for a moment.
His eyebrows came together and at that moment small black particles separated from around his body.
One.
Ten.
Hundreds of particles.
He quickly stood up from the bed and the particles gathered in front of him, first taking the shape of an unclear mass, then a circle and finally the shape of an egg.
The young Vorhelm’s eyes became slightly wider for a moment.
The Devouring Egg.
The same egg that had disappeared in Antarctica a few hours ago was now sitting very quietly on the floor of the room.
He stared at it without saying anything for a few seconds.
"So you can do this kind of thing too?" he asked quietly.
The egg moved very clearly and the top of its shell bent forward once, as if it had nodded.
Lian stayed silent for a moment and then a short laugh came from his throat.
"Good."
Now at least he knew how it had disappeared from Antarctica.
Apparently, after finishing its feeding, the egg had somehow connected itself to him again and returned with him.
Not bad, this way even Overlord Orion had not noticed it.
He bent down and placed his palm on the shell, as if he wanted to pat it, and at the same time a quiet notification appeared.
[Devouring Egg.]
[Embryo Formation Progress: 31%.]
Lian’s eyes became slightly wider, thirty-one percent, before eating the womb, the amount had been much lower.

So that cave had helped it a lot, which also made sense, it had eaten at least hundreds of tons of biomass, artificial samples, growth materials and womb tissue that had been made to feed a Calamity Seed.
It was no surprise that the egg had been able to make such a big jump.
"Good, good." He gently moved his hand over the shell several times.
The egg moved a little, as if it was happy with the praise, and a small smile appeared on Lian’s face.
"Don’t worry."
His eyes moved toward his storage space, he still had many corpses inside.
"I have more meals for you too."
The egg moved again, as if its appetite had awakened again.
"When we reach the Ruined Realm, I’ll let you eat all of them."
He touched the egg again, this time black particles separated from its surface and within a few seconds, its entire body turned into light and dark particles and disappeared back into his body.
Lian looked at the empty spot for a few moments, so Ezrak was not the only one who had strange things related to movement.
He would have to investigate this later too, but for now it was time to leave.
He opened the System panel.
Kain had to use a gate to enter the Ruined Realm, almost everyone did the same.
But not him, after surviving as one of the twenty-five thousand victims of the first transfer, the System had given him a special reward.
A reward that he had not been able to use for a long time because he had not had the chance, but now the time to use it had finally come.
[Return to the Ruined Realm.]
[This ability was given as a survival reward from the first transfer of the victims.]
[Conditions for use:]
[Can only be used from the original world.]
[Only previously registered return points can be selected.]
[The transfer of other people is not possible.]
[Do you want to enter the Ruined Realm?]
[Yes / No]
Lian looked at the panel for a few seconds and a very small smile appeared on his face.
[Yes.]
The panel changed.
[Select your return point.]
Three options appeared.
[Dreadmaw Mountains.]
[Base #3.]
[Base #9.]
His eyes stopped on the first option, the Dreadmaw Mountains, and for a moment, memories returned to his mind.
The village that he had found with Seris for the first time and where he had almost been killed, and the creature that he had thought was impossible to fight at that time.
An Unholy.
At that time, his only choice had been to run when facing such a creature, what could he have done?
Even being able to escape had been a miracle by itself.
But now?
He was level twenty-three, he had completed his first evolution, he had an Ancient-rank armor along with several Divine skills and experience that he had not even had one year ago.
Lian’s eyes narrowed for a moment, if he returned to that mountain now, would he still have to run?
It was an interesting question, very interesting.
His finger moved toward the first option for a moment, but then stopped.
No.
Not yet.
He had seen enough creatures today whose power was greater than he had expected.
He was not going to enter another deadly battle just because of his curiosity.
"Later." He could hunt that Unholy later too.
His eyes moved down.
Base #3 and then #9.
His current goal was simple, raise his level, hunt, obtain Fragments and move toward his second evolution.
[Base #9 selected.]
[Transfer beginning.]
Light appeared under his feet, but he did not feel any strange pressure on his soul.
The System’s transfer was calm, and his feet first turned into particles of light, then his body, his hands, his head, and a few seconds later the dorm room was empty.
Lian appeared again, and when he opened his eyes, he was standing in the middle of the transfer platform of Base #9.
Two guards near the platform looked at him in surprise for a moment.
It was clear that seeing someone enter directly without activating the gate was not something they saw every day.
He ignored them and a notification appeared in front of him.
[Welcome to the Ruined Realm.]
[Current Location: Base #9.]
He looked past the buildings around him, then at the tall walls of the base and beyond them at the huge and unknown lands that continued to the horizon.
It was time to hunt.

chapters.title: Chapter 480: A Hungry Egg
paragraphs: Lian looked at the buildings around him for a few seconds.

If there were no monsters, awakened weapons, and the constant smell of blood in the air, this place would look more like a city from a few centuries ago than a base in a world where a large part of its civilization had been destroyed.
But he had not come here to look around, first he needed to find out what there was to hunt around the base.
The Hunters’ Information Center was only a few streets away from the transfer platform.
After asking around for a while, he entered a two-story building whose stone walls were covered with dozens of maps, hunting notices, and pictures of monsters.
Several Awakened were standing in front of the mission boards.
Some had taken missions to collect materials, some were looking for specific monsters, and several groups were discussing their travel routes.
Lian walked directly to the information counter.
A middle-aged man was sitting behind it and writing something in a large notebook.
"I want a map of the discovered areas around the base." Then he said.
Without looking at him much, the man opened a drawer under the desk and took out a thin sheet of treated leather.
"This is the newest version. Safe areas, caravan routes, and confirmed hunting areas are marked. Don’t enter the red areas without a group unless you know what you’re doing."
The young Vorhelm put the money on the table and took the map.
When he opened it, a large part of the area around the base appeared in front of him.
Base #9 was almost in the center of the discovered area.
To the east, the Broken Plains were marked, a little lower was the Leafless Forest, the Bone Marsh was to the southwest, and in the north there was a large area with many warning marks.
[Wolfgrave Frontier.]
He kept his eyes on it for a few seconds.
A large part of the area was still empty and the lines on the map suddenly stopped at a certain distance from the base.
The information was not bad, but it was not complete either, however, it caught his attention the most because it was related to wolf-type monsters.
Lian closed the map.
There was no reason to try anything here, he left the information center and after finding a quiet corner in one of the side streets, he reached into his storage space.
Something small and old came out.
World Memory.
The artifact did not look very special, but as soon as he placed the map in front of it, its surface began to shine.
System notifications appeared.
[External map detected.]
[Synchronization with World Memory has begun.]
[Registered information is being matched.]
[Time differences detected.]
A white line came out of the artifact and moved across the map.
He silently watched as the first changes appeared, and they were roads.
Several narrow paths appeared in areas that were completely empty on the base’s map.
Then ruins, small towers, bridges that had collapsed a long time ago, and even an old river path appeared on the map, though its riverbed was now dry.
Parts of the forest also changed.
The base map showed the current locations, while World Memory added information from the past and even older information about these areas.
Two types of information were connected into one image, but not everything was recovered, and in several areas, only unclear lines could be seen.
[Damaged information.]
[Structure identified.]
[Current condition unknown.]
Lian gave a faint smile.
"This is much better."
But he had another tool, and this time he took a magnificent book out of his storage space.
Celestial Book of Treasure.
The book was still closed when it suddenly reacted, thin golden lines on its cover lit up, and then the pages began turning without his help.
One page.
Ten pages.
Several dozen pages.
Finally, the book stopped on an empty page, and light came out from between the paper and moved across the completed map like thin threads.
A few seconds later, the first mark appeared.
A weak white point not too far from the base.
Then two blue marks.
One was near the Leafless Forest and the other was beside the Bell Ruins, then a purple mark appeared deep inside the Wolfgrave Frontier.
Lian raised an eyebrow slightly, but the book was not finished yet, and much farther away, almost near the edge of the incomplete information on the map, a golden point lit up for a moment.
Only once, and then its light became weaker.
Lian kept his eyes on the golden mark for a few seconds, he realized that the book was showing treasures beyond its ten-kilometer limit.
This made him wonder if it was because he himself had become stronger? In other words, would the book’s limits become weaker as he became stronger?
But just like before, it did not give any information about the treasures, it seemed he needed to get close to them and touch them to find out what they were.
Interesting, there were many places to explore, but not for now and then his eyes returned to the purple mark.
The Wolfgrave Frontier.

Higher-level monsters that were also wolf-type monsters, which meant he could get Fragments by killing them, and more importantly, according to the Celestial Book of Treasure, there was also a treasure there.
Those were enough reasons.
He put the book and World Memory back into his storage space and left the alley.
His target was decided.
Lian left the base through the northern gate.
At first, he followed the main road, but after about one kilometer, he changed his path and entered an area where scattered ruins could be seen among the gray grass.
It was still not enough, several hunting groups could be seen in the distance.
He continued for about three more kilometers and then activated Predator’s Instincts.
There were no humans nearby, and he did not sense any suspicious presence either.
This place was enough.
He opened his storage space and then the first corpse fell onto the ground.
Boom.
A four-meter-tall monster.
Then the second.
The third.
The fifth.
The tenth.
But the stream of corpses did not stop, dozens of corpses appeared one after another among the ruins.
Small monsters, larger creatures, and a very large number of Cindari corpses that he had killed.
A few minutes later, what was in front of him looked more like a huge hill of flesh and bones.
Hundreds of corpses and the heavy smell of blood and dead flesh spread through the area.
"It was much more than I thought." Lian looked at the result for a few seconds, he knew he had many corpses in his storage space.
But he was not exactly sure how many there were, almost everything he had hunted in the Special Area was now here.
Then he called another presence from inside himself, dark particles formed in front of his body, slowly gathered together, and a few seconds later the Devourer Egg appeared on the ground.
As soon as it appeared, the surface of its shell shook slightly.
"You said you wanted food, here you go." The young Vorhelm pointed at the hill of corpses with his finger.
The Egg reacted quickly and several thin, dark threads came out from its lower part.
Plop!
They entered the nearest corpse, and the monster’s body tissue immediately began to change.

The color of its skin disappeared, the flesh slowly dried up, and several dark veins stretched from the corpse toward the Egg, while the biological matter left the monster’s body like an invisible liquid.
More threads grew.
To the second corpse.
The third.
The fifth.
The tenth.
[Large food source detected.]
[Feeding process started.]

Lian watched for a few moments, this thing really had no end to its appetite, and even after eating the living Womb, the Egg’s embryo formation process had only reached thirty-one percent, yet it looked even hungrier.
In any case, that Womb alone had caused a huge increase, and now there were hundreds of more corpses in front of it.
He did not know what the result would be, but he was really curious to know what this Egg would become when it was born.
"For now, eat."
Then he turned his attention to another matter, the Colony Link was activated.
[Special Colony member selected.]
[One.]
[Level: 19.]
[Condition: Healthy.]
[Summon special member?]
[Yes.]
The space in front of him twisted slightly and a huge creature came out through the Colony connection.
One landed on the ground.
Now it was time to deal with his only Colony member.

chapters.title: Chapter 481: The First Hunt After Evolution
paragraphs: The six legs of One immediately took the weight of his large body, and his long antennae began to move.
He checked the area for a few seconds, then his eyes stopped on the hill of corpses and finally on the egg.
The giant ant stayed completely still for a few moments.
"That is not your food." Lian gave a short laugh.
One turned his head toward him, and through the link, a very clear feeling of dissatisfaction was sent to him.
The young Vorhelm put a hand on the upper part of his armored head.
"Don’t worry. We have work for you too."
He opened his panel again, his level was nineteen, but his exp was almost full.
The limited hunts One had done in the Special Area had brought him close to level twenty.
There was not much left before he reached level 20 and then completed his first evolution, as expected, monsters also had evolutions just like Awakened.
But their evolution was different from the evolutions of Awakened, the first one mostly had to perform an action that was partly natural to them to evolve.
But the second one did not, Awakened had to complete the evolution Quest given to them by the System.
Through the link, Lian directly sent him the meaning of the goal, level 20.
One raised his antennae.
"Anything we find below level twenty, as long as it does not have unnecessary danger, is yours."
This time, something like excitement came back through the link.
"Good."
He gave the egg one last look, it was still busy eating the corpses at a fast speed.
He could call it again later and did not need to worry about it anymore, the egg had already shown that it had strange abilities and could even hide and escape from an Overlord.
So they moved together with One without worry.
The hunt had begun.
The first monster was found less than twenty minutes later, Lian felt its presence even before seeing it.
Something was hiding between the old broken stones.
One noticed it too, he lowered his head and a lizard almost two meters long crawled out from the gap between two stones.
The skin of its entire body was made of thick gray plates that almost looked the same as the stones around it.
[Stone-Skin Lizard.]
[Level: 15.]
When the lizard saw them, and more exactly when it saw Lian, it turned around as if it wanted to run ... as if some kind of instinct was telling it to run!
"Yours."
The giant ant attacked at that moment, and his huge body moved forward with a speed greater than what could be expected from his size.
His heavy front leg landed directly on the lizard’s back.
Boom!
The stone floor cracked, but the monster did not die, the plates on its back spread the force, and the lizard turned with a rough sound and hit One’s side with its heavy tail.
Crack!
One moved half a step.
Lian did not interfere.
The lizard gathered its body behind its stone plates again, and One raised his claw once more, but this time he stopped.
His antennae moved, and instead of attacking directly, he attacked from the side, one of his front legs went under the lizard’s body.
He lifted its body, and the monster struggled as the giant ant turned it with more force.
Boom!
The lizard fell on its back, its soft and unarmored stomach was exposed and One’s jaws came down.
Crack!
The entire soft part of its stomach was torn open, and a few seconds later the monster became still.
[Special Colony Member, One, received Exp.]
"Great." Lian nodded, and One sent a clear feeling of pride through the link.
But their work had only just started, and they continued along their path based on the World Memory.
The second hunt was a little harder.
The Broken-Tusk Boar appeared in a small field almost an hour later, its height was close to 3 meters.
Two broken and curved bone tusks came out from both sides of its jaw, and the muscles on its shoulders were so large that the front half of its body looked unnaturally heavy.
[Broken-Tusk Boar.]
[Level: 18.]
As soon as the boar saw them, it dug the ground with its foot and then attacked.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Every step sent dirt into the air, One did not run this time and his six legs firmly stood on the ground.
His head lowered and the collision happened ...BOOOOM!
A wave of dirt spread around them, and the giant ant was pushed almost two meters back while the other monster was thrown one meter back.
Both of them stood again.
The boar attacked for the second time without stopping, and this time One did not repeat the same mistake, just one moment before the collision, he moved the weight of his body to the right.
One of his front legs hit the boar’s shoulder, changing the direction of its attack, and the boar passed beside One.
Before it could turn its heavy body back, the giant ant fell on it.
Two front legs held the boar’s legs against the ground, and the giant jaws closed.
Crack!
Its neck broke.
Lian watched from a few meters away, One was no longer just a creature that crushed everything with raw power.
He was slowly learning, and what he learned remained in his mind, which was normal, this ant had very good intelligence.
Several more hunts continued.
Two level sixteen lizards and a group of carrion crows that kept attacking from above.
In that fight, One was bothered more than ever, the monsters came down each time, attacked, and then went back up.
He could not easily reach them.
Lian only created a few ice blades in the air, but not to kill them, only to block their escape paths, and this forced one of the crows to fly lower.
One was waiting for it, and with a heavy jump, his jaws closed around the monster’s wing and slammed it directly onto the ground.
The others were also caught one after another, and after the last crow, a faint light came out of One’s body and the giant creature stopped for a moment.
The young Vorhelm opened his panel.
[One has reached level 20.]
[Maximum level before the first evolution has been reached.]
[Level condition completed.]
[Checking evolution conditions...]
He waited for a few seconds, and then a new notification appeared.
[First evolution condition is incomplete.]
[To begin evolution, the special member must absorb more monster cores.]
[Required amount: Variable.]
[The quality, level, rank, and compatibility of the core affect the amount of absorption.]
[Final condition: Reach complete saturation.]
Monsters had to eat the cores of other monsters to evolve, at least this was true for Normal monsters and, to some extent, Mutated monsters.
Of course, absorbing the cores of other monsters was one of their two paths, and it was considered the harder path for monsters.
The second path, which most normal monsters chose, was eating humans, the energy they received from eating each human was equal to three cores from monsters of the same level.
And if those humans were Awakened, even better.
For Fallen Monsters and especially higher ones such as Unholy, who had intelligence at the level of humans, their evolution conditions could be much more complicated.
In any case, the condition for One was clear too, he had to absorb the cores of other monsters, and there was no specific number.
So ten cores might be enough, or fifty.
He looked at One, and the creature moved his antennae, no special feeling of disappointment came through the link because he could not evolve directly.
He mostly seemed eager, as if he could not wait to have his first evolution.
"It’s fine, we were going to hunt anyway." He looked toward the path ahead.
From this moment on, every monster was not only Exp, and its possible core could also bring One one step closer to his first evolution.
But well, it was time for him to join the hunt too.
Hours passed, and the farther he and One moved from the base, the more the environment around them slowly changed.
There were more dead trees, gray grass replaced the open areas, and a light fog could be seen between the dry tree trunks.
And the Celestial Book of Treasure inside his storage space sent a weak pulse from time to time.
At first, Lian did not pay much attention to it, but the farther they went, the stronger the pulse became, and he stopped for a moment.
He took out the map combined with the World Memory, the purple mark was still in the same direction.
The Wolfgrave Frontier.
Almost directly ahead.
"Good, we are going the right way." He closed the map, his goal had been clear from the beginning, unfortunately, this area was still unknown on the map.
And it was considered one of the areas that had little information about it, most Awakened also stayed away from it because they did not see much benefit there unless a group went there.
One turned his head slightly and they moved again.
About half an hour later, the first howl was heard.
Awoooooooo—
The sound was far away but clear, and the giant ant immediately changed his stance, his legs bent slightly and his antennae moved forward.
Lian also stopped, the presences entered his senses one after another.
One.
Two.
Five.
There were five of them, and they were approaching from several directions.
"These ones are mine." He raised his hand.
One sent a weak protest through the link.
"Their levels are above twenty."
The protest became weaker, and a few seconds later, the first wolf came out of the fog, its body was much larger than a normal wolf.

sentences.text: The six legs of One immediately took the weight of his large body, and his long antennae began to move.
He checked the area for a few seconds, then his eyes stopped on the hill of corpses and finally on the egg.
The giant ant stayed completely still for a few moments.
"That is not your food." Lian gave a short laugh.
One turned his head toward him, and through the link, a very clear feeling of dissatisfaction was sent to him.
The young Vorhelm put a hand on the upper part of his armored head.
"Don’t worry.
We have work for you too."
He opened his panel again, his level was nineteen, but his exp was almost full.
The limited hunts One had done in the Special Area had brought him close to level twenty.
There was not much left before he reached level 20 and then completed his first evolution, as expected, monsters also had evolutions just like Awakened.
But their evolution was different from the evolutions of Awakened, the first one mostly had to perform an action that was partly natural to them to evolve.
But the second one did not, Awakened had to complete the evolution Quest given to them by the System.
Through the link, Lian directly sent him the meaning of the goal, level 20.
One raised his antennae.
"Anything we find below level twenty, as long as it does not have unnecessary danger, is yours."
This time, something like excitement came back through the link.
"Good."
He gave the egg one last look, it was still busy eating the corpses at a fast speed.
He could call it again later and did not need to worry about it anymore, the egg had already shown that it had strange abilities and could even hide and escape from an Overlord.
So they moved together with One without worry.
The hunt had begun.
The first monster was found less than twenty minutes later, Lian felt its presence even before seeing it.
Something was hiding between the old broken stones.
One noticed it too, he lowered his head and a lizard almost two meters long crawled out from the gap between two stones.
The skin of its entire body was made of thick gray plates that almost looked the same as the stones around it.
[Stone-Skin Lizard.]
[Level: 15.]
When the lizard saw them, and more exactly when it saw Lian, it turned around as if it wanted to run ... as if some kind of instinct was telling it to run!
