chapters.title: Chapter 495: Skill Fusion For The First Time
paragraphs: The lights of Base #9 became clearer through the fog as they got closer.
They passed through the northern gate of the base.
Some of the guards placed their hands on their weapons when they saw the giant ant coming directly toward the gate, but Lian’s presence on its back made no one react any further.
When they saw an Awakened enter the base with it without the slightest concern, they quickly understood that they were not dealing with a wild monster.
After passing through the gate, he jumped down.
"Go back and rest." He said while placing his palm on the upper part of One’s head.
One’s antennae moved slightly.
A moment later, its huge body turned into particles of light and disappeared in front of several nearby Awakeneds.
[Special Colony Member — One.]
[Location: Colony House.]
The young Vorhelm changed his path toward the center of the base.

The streets had not changed much since he left. Hunters were moving around, carts full of monster parts were passing through the market, and the continuous sound of metal being hit could be heard from the blacksmith workshops.
But when he reached the transfer gate area, his eyes stopped for a moment on the large board beside the square.
Lian looked at it without moving for a few seconds and then calculated again.
"One day?"
Almost a full day had passed since he returned to Base #9.
In his own mind, this time had been divided into several hunts, finding the Wolfgrave Fortresses, fighting Two, checking the temples, and walking around for a while.
When he put all of it together, a full day had really passed.
He let out a short breath.
"I achieved too much for a short hunt."
Kain had said that he would come here after finishing his work in Base #3.
And he had said that he would probably arrive the next day.
So if everything had gone according to plan, he would not need to wait much longer.
He stood beside one of the stone pillars around the square.
The gate area was crowded.
A group of Awakeneds came out of one of the gates with broken armor.
Two carriers placed a large box that smelled of blood onto a cart, and several students were arguing about the prices near a potion shop.
In the middle of all this crowd, he opened a panel that only he could see.
[Current Fragments: 2161.]
His eyes stayed on the number for a few seconds.
Only a short time ago, this amount of Fragments would have been a very large number for him.
But this time, he did not plan to immediately go to his innate traits tree.
His recent battles had made another problem clear.
He did not lack skills, on the contrary, perhaps he had too many skills.
Some of his abilities had very similar roles, and in difficult battles, he had to activate several skills one after another just to perform a single move.
Thunder Step to get closer.
Ash Step to change his position.
Warrior’s Madness and Predator’s Frenzy to increase his combat ability, and several separate defensive skills to protect his body.
It was not a big problem in a normal battle, but against enemies like Two, even a fraction of a second was important.
He opened another part of the panel.
[Skill Fusion.]
[The ability to combine two or more compatible skill structures.]
[The required Fragments are calculated based on the number, Rank, and complexity of the structures.]
He checked the options for a few moments, and the first choice was almost obvious.
[Thunder Step selected.]
[Ash Step selected.]
[Structural compatibility detected.]
[Common path: Thunder Acceleration / Ashen Movement / Fallen Wolf Speed.]
[Fusion cost: 500 Fragments.]
[Warning: After fusion, the original skills can no longer be used independently.]
Lian paused at the last line, the fusion was not going to add a third skill to his already long list.
The two previous abilities would really disappear and a new structure would replace them, but he had used both of them together so many times that the decision was not difficult.

In most battles, he used Thunder Step for explosive movement, and exactly when the enemy read his path, he used Ash Step to break the angle, and Fallen Wolf Speed, which only increased his speed and had not been used for a long time,
Anyway, the main point was using Thunder Step and Ash Step, which required two commands to activate and consumed Mana separately twice.
[Fusion has begun.]
The three structures overlapped in his mind for a moment, the fast and direct pattern of Thunder Step collided with the scattered structure of Ash Step and the speed increase of Fallen Wolf Speed.
At first, they seemed opposite.
One moved the body with real acceleration, while the other turned the body’s structure into ash for a few meters.
But then the paths connected.
[Fusion successful.]
[Ashen Thunder Step received.]
[Explosive movement with the power of thunder.]
[The user can turn their body into ash for a short part of the movement and change the exit point within the allowed range.]
[Changing the direction increases the Mana cost.]
[The ashen part is still limited to a short distance.]
[Rank: Common (+).]
He checked the structure of the new skill for a few seconds.
It was strange.
Before, he had to decide when Thunder Step would end and when Ash Step would begin.
Now that point was practically part of the skill itself.
He could move directly forward with thunder, disappear for a moment at the end of the movement, and appear a few meters away at a different angle.
[500 Fragments used.]
[Remaining Fragments: 1661.]
He moved to the second option.
[Warrior’s Madness selected.]
[Predator’s Frenzy selected.]
[Very high structural compatibility.]
[Fusion cost: 550 Fragments.]
He read the descriptions of both again.
In practice, both had the same purpose, forcing his body and mind to fight beyond their normal state.
But activating both at the same time always caused some interference, and not to mention that he had not made much use of Predator’s Frenzy until now.
But if a single structure could do the same thing with better coordination, there was little reason to keep both.
[Coordinated enhancement of physical ability, offensive pressure, and hunting focus.]
[Reduced interference between physical and instinctive enhancements.]
[The more damage the user takes, all stats increase by 30% every minute for 15 minutes.]
[The mental weakness of Madness has been removed.]
[300 Mana is consumed every minute.]

Lian gave a very small smile, in other words, after only ten minutes, all of his stats would become three times higher, and he could fight for another five minutes with his stats increased to more than three times their normal amount.
This was a very large boost.
Of course, its cost was also very high, 300 Mana every minute, which meant 3000 Mana in ten minutes, and this was only at Common Rank.
God knows how much the cost would increase when it ranked up.
[Confirmed.]
[Fusion has begun.]
For a few seconds, warmth formed in his chest.
His heartbeat did not become faster, but simply imagining activating the new structure was enough to make him feel that his muscles and instincts knew they had to work in the same direction.
[Fusion successful.]
[Predator’s Madness received.]
[Rank: Common (+).]
[550 Fragments used.]
[Remaining Fragments: 1111.]
Lian looked at the new number for a few seconds.
One more fusion could be done, and this time, his decision took a little longer.
Three defensive skills.
[Diamond Skin selected.]
[Ossuary Armor selected.]
[Solar Forge Aegis selected.]
[Three compatible defensive structures detected.]
[Fusion cost: 650 Fragments.]
The panel displayed a preview of the possible result.
[Result Preview.]
[Multi-layered defensive structure.]
[Inner Layer: Enhances the body’s natural defense by creating a diamond layer that increases defensive power by up to 50%.]
[Middle Layer: A compressed bone structure created to distribute pressure and increase defensive power by up to 50%.]
[Outer Layer: A molten coating with the ability to control the amount of heat, increasing defensive power by up to 50%.]
[200 Mana will be consumed per minute.]
[Can be used together with external defensive equipment.]
The World-Devourer Bastion was not supposed to be part of the fusion.
That armor was an Ancient-Rank equipment.
The new defensive structure would work under it or alongside it and could reduce the pressure entering his body and the armor itself.
At first glance, this skill seemed useless and stupid, but was it really like that? Was a single Ancient-Rank armor really enough?
He thought about his battle with the Unborn Saint, and considering that he might face much stronger enemies in the future, defense would be very important.
Until now, all the fusions he had done had been made with the future in mind.
When he might face other Calamities, or when an enemy was more than twenty Levels above him,
A single Ancient-Rank armor would not be enough there, and this skill could boost his defensive power by up to 150%.

[Common path: Thunder Acceleration / Ashen Movement / Fallen Wolf Speed.]
[Fusion cost: 500 Fragments.]
[Warning: After fusion, the original skills can no longer be used independently.]
Lian paused at the last line, the fusion was not going to add a third skill to his already long list.
The two previous abilities would really disappear and a new structure would replace them, but he had used both of them together so many times that the decision was not difficult.

In most battles, he used Thunder Step for explosive movement, and exactly when the enemy read his path, he used Ash Step to break the angle, and Fallen Wolf Speed, which only increased his speed and had not been used for a long time,
Anyway, the main point was using Thunder Step and Ash Step, which required two commands to activate and consumed Mana separately twice.
[Fusion has begun.]
The three structures overlapped in his mind for a moment, the fast and direct pattern of Thunder Step collided with the scattered structure of Ash Step and the speed increase of Fallen Wolf Speed.
At first, they seemed opposite.
One moved the body with real acceleration, while the other turned the body’s structure into ash for a few meters.
But then the paths connected.
[Fusion successful.]
[Ashen Thunder Step received.]
[Explosive movement with the power of thunder.]
[The user can turn their body into ash for a short part of the movement and change the exit point within the allowed range.]
[Changing the direction increases the Mana cost.]
[The ashen part is still limited to a short distance.]
[Rank: Common (+).]
He checked the structure of the new skill for a few seconds.
It was strange.
Before, he had to decide when Thunder Step would end and when Ash Step would begin.
Now that point was practically part of the skill itself.
He could move directly forward with thunder, disappear for a moment at the end of the movement, and appear a few meters away at a different angle.
[500 Fragments used.]
[Remaining Fragments: 1661.]
He moved to the second option.
[Warrior’s Madness selected.]
[Predator’s Frenzy selected.]
[Very high structural compatibility.]
[Fusion cost: 550 Fragments.]
He read the descriptions of both again.
In practice, both had the same purpose, forcing his body and mind to fight beyond their normal state.
But activating both at the same time always caused some interference, and not to mention that he had not made much use of Predator’s Frenzy until now.
But if a single structure could do the same thing with better coordination, there was little reason to keep both.
[Coordinated enhancement of physical ability, offensive pressure, and hunting focus.]
[Reduced interference between physical and instinctive enhancements.]
[The more damage the user takes, all stats increase by 30% every minute for 15 minutes.]
[The mental weakness of Madness has been removed.]
[300 Mana is consumed every minute.]

Lian gave a very small smile, in other words, after only ten minutes, all of his stats would become three times higher, and he could fight for another five minutes with his stats increased to more than three times their normal amount.
This was a very large boost.
Of course, its cost was also very high, 300 Mana every minute, which meant 3000 Mana in ten minutes, and this was only at Common Rank.
God knows how much the cost would increase when it ranked up.
[Confirmed.]
[Fusion has begun.]
For a few seconds, warmth formed in his chest.
His heartbeat did not become faster, but simply imagining activating the new structure was enough to make him feel that his muscles and instincts knew they had to work in the same direction.
[Fusion successful.]
[Predator’s Madness received.]
[Rank: Common (+).]
[550 Fragments used.]
[Remaining Fragments: 1111.]
Lian looked at the new number for a few seconds.
One more fusion could be done, and this time, his decision took a little longer.
Three defensive skills.
[Diamond Skin selected.]
[Ossuary Armor selected.]
[Solar Forge Aegis selected.]
[Three compatible defensive structures detected.]
[Fusion cost: 650 Fragments.]
The panel displayed a preview of the possible result.
[Result Preview.]
[Multi-layered defensive structure.]
[Inner Layer: Enhances the body’s natural defense by creating a diamond layer that increases defensive power by up to 50%.]
[Middle Layer: A compressed bone structure created to distribute pressure and increase defensive power by up to 50%.]
[Outer Layer: A molten coating with the ability to control the amount of heat, increasing defensive power by up to 50%.]
[200 Mana will be consumed per minute.]
[Can be used together with external defensive equipment.]
The World-Devourer Bastion was not supposed to be part of the fusion.
That armor was an Ancient-Rank equipment.
The new defensive structure would work under it or alongside it and could reduce the pressure entering his body and the armor itself.
At first glance, this skill seemed useless and stupid, but was it really like that?
Was a single Ancient-Rank armor really enough?
He thought about his battle with the Unborn Saint, and considering that he might face much stronger enemies in the future, defense would be very important.
Until now, all the fusions he had done had been made with the future in mind.
When he might face other Calamities, or when an enemy was more than twenty Levels above him,
A single Ancient-Rank armor would not be enough there, and this skill could boost his defensive power by up to 150%.

chapters.title: Chapter 496: The Name Is One
paragraphs: [Confirmed.]
The three structures merged together.
[Fusion successful.]
[Molten Bastion Body received.]
[Rank: Common (+).]
[650 Fragments used.]
[Total Fusion cost: 1700 Fragments.]
[Remaining Fragments: 461.]
He closed the skill panel, the number of his skills had become lower, but what remained was cleaner.
Three new structures instead of seven separate structures, and this satisfied him more than simply adding several new skills.
But there were still a considerable number of Fragments left.
He opened another section.
[Traits.]
Five options appeared.
[Skill Overdrive.]
[First Level Effect: Skill power increases by 10% for 10 seconds.]
[Each additional Level: 10% more power and 10 more seconds.]
[Quick Mana.]
[Each Level: Mana recovery speed increases by 10%.]
[Lifesteal.]
[First Level: 1% chance to activate with each successful hit.]
[When activated, 2% of the damage dealt is recovered.]
[Each additional Level: 1% more chance and 2% more recovery.]
[Force Spike.]
[First Level: 1% chance to increase attack power by 10%.]
[Each additional Level: 1% more chance and 10% more power.]
[Natural Armor.]
[Each Level: Natural defense power of the body increases by 50%.]
His eyes stayed on Natural Armor for a while, fifty percent per level was not a small number.
But this effect was applied to his body’s natural defense, not making the power of World-Devourer Bastion or his other equipment fifty percent stronger.
And only a few minutes ago, he had created a new defensive skill as well.
For now, the other choices were more interesting to him, first was Skill Overdrive.
In the battle with Two, there had been many times when the difference between breaking through a defense and failing to break it was only a little more power at that exact moment.
The ten percent was not permanent and only lasted for ten seconds.
But those ten seconds, if used on something like Suppressing Palm, Thunder Calamity, or Glacial Reaper Claw, could make a huge difference.
[Skill Overdrive upgraded to Level 1.]
[Cost: 100 Fragments.]
"Accept."
[Skill Overdrive.]
[Skill Power: +10%.]
[Duration: 10 seconds.]
[Remaining Fragments: 361.]
Lian moved his eyes to the next option.
Lifesteal.
Its first Level was really nothing special, a one percent chance and two percent recovery, and in a short battle, it might not even activate once.
But it was not going to stay at Level one forever.
If he reached higher Levels one day, long battles could become completely different.
[Lifesteal upgraded to Level 1.]
[Cost: 200 Fragments.]
[Lifesteal.]
[Activation chance with each successful hit: 1%.]
[Recovery amount when activated: 2% of the damage dealt.]
[Remaining Fragments: 161.]

He looked at the final number for a few seconds, he had spent two thousand Fragments this easily, even though obtaining them had taken him one day, for other Awakeneds, it could take months or even years.
But it had only taken him a few minutes to spend them.
"The difficulty of obtaining Fragments really isn’t fair." He sighed, and this was said by someone who could obtain Fragments a thousand times more easily than others.
"Are you talking to yourself or waiting for the gate to answer?"
Lian raised his head.
Kain was standing a few meters away.
"You arrived at the right time."
"Have you been waiting for long?" His friend came closer and looked around.
"Long enough to become poor again." Lian answered in a completely serious tone.
Kain moved his eyes from his face downward.
"What did you buy?"
"Some things."
"My work in Base Three is finished. What about you? What did you do yesterday?"
Lian thought about the events of the past day for a moment.
Hundreds of wolves, hidden fortresses, a Level forty monster, and an S-Rank treasure.
"I found an interesting area."
"That’s all?" Kain waited for a few seconds for more explanation, but nothing came.
"For now, yes."
"Why have you become so lazy when talking? You weren’t like this before, but recently it seems like you don’t feel like explaining things."
The young Vorhelm said nothing, he had not noticed this himself, but if it was really like that, the only reason could be Seris.
Before leaving, they checked the amount of water, food, and potions they had. Kain bought a few extra bottles, and Lian also bought several potions to replace the ones he had used.
Less than half an hour later, they left Base #9.
They walked for the first few kilometers.
The road was still busy, and different hunting groups could be seen along the way.
When the number of Awakeneds around them finally became lower, Lian stopped.
Kain walked a few steps ahead and turned back.
"What happened?"
Without explaining anything, he activated Colony Link.
[Special Colony Member selected.]
[One.]
[Summoning.]

Particles of light gathered beside the road, at first only a vague shadow appeared, then six huge legs, black natural armor, jaws, and a few seconds later, One appeared on the ground at its full huge size.
Boom!
The dirt around its feet rose slightly.
Kain stopped in the middle of the movement he was about to make, he said nothing for several seconds. His eyes moved up from the legs of the giant ant.
They stopped on its large jaws, then on its thick natural armor, and finally returned to his best friend.
"Since when can you summon monsters?" He asked in disbelief and took one step closer.
"Wait... is this your mount, or did you really summon it?"
Lian walked beside One and placed a hand on the upper part of its head.
"I can summon it. And yes, for now, it can also act as a mount."
Kain carefully walked around One, and the giant ant also moved its antennae slightly toward him.
The young Vorhelm saw no reason to hide this part of his abilities from his friend.
Other people had seen One, and some of his friends also knew about its existence.
Hiding the fact that he had such a companion from his best friend, while other people already knew about it, was more stupid than careful.
"My god... how? Where did you even get it from? What’s its name?"
Lian thought for a moment about how much of the story he should explain, and in the end, he simply gave up on explaining.
"It’s a little hard to explain, but its name is One."
"One?" Kain became silent.
"Yeah."
"You mean... one?"
"Exactly."
The Child of Light turned his head toward the giant ant again, looked at the giant ant for a few seconds, and then looked at Lian.
"You’re joking."
"No."
"Lian, look at this." He pointed at the huge creature with both hands.

"A giant armored ant that can probably cut a person in half with one move. You could have given it a name that would scare people when they heard it. An old name, a war name, anything... and you named it One?"
"It’s a good name, it’s short, it’s easy to remember, and it didn’t complain either, besides, are you questioning my naming skills?"
Kain stared at him.
"Because it can’t talk, bastard! Don’t take silence as agreement!"
One’s antennae moved again.
Through the Colony Link, Lian received something like boredom, One apparently had little interest in discussing its own name.
It mostly wanted to move.
For a moment, the young Vorhelm thought about another member who was resting inside the Colony House.
One and a huge, imposing, and terrifying wolf whose name was Two.
Maybe it was better not to tell Kain anything about this for now.
If he was this unhappy about One’s name, hearing the name of the second member would probably not be a good experience for him.
"Let’s go." Lian ended the discussion.
"I still have something to say about this name." Kain shook his head.
"Later."
They got onto One’s back, and a few seconds later, the giant ant started moving.
One’s speed was unusual for a creature of that size.
The stone roads passed under its feet one after another, and soon the walls of Base #9 became small in the distance.
"Where do you want to go?" The young Vorhelm asked.
"Do we have a map?"
He took out World Memory, he had the completed map of the area around the base with him.
He activated the effect, and a few seconds later, old paths, ruins, and areas whose information was incomplete appeared on the map.
He held it toward Kain, and at first he said nothing, then his eyes moved across the details and he realized that it was not a simple map.
"This isn’t a simple map, is it?"
His friend did not give much explanation either.
"That’s right, it also adds the old information of this world to the map. Not all of it is reliable, some places have changed, but it’s better than a normal map."
Kain checked it for several minutes.
The borders of known areas, hunting routes, areas that had already been recorded, and finally the farthest point that the new information from Base #9 reached.
His finger stopped there.
"What do you think about going to find something that isn’t on this map yet?" After all, this map showed the discovered areas! Not the entire Ruined Realm...

chapters.title: Chapter 497: The Twelve Ancient Guilds
paragraphs: Lian checked the distance.
Even with One’s speed, it was not a short journey, and some parts of the road were so rough that they could not move at full speed the entire time.
"It’ll take two, maybe three days just to reach the last area that the people from the base have recorded."
"So?" Kain raised his head.
He looked at him, but before he could say anything, Kain continued.

"We’re not going to have a boring journey with this creature. Besides, discovering a new area is much more interesting than going somewhere that a hundred people have already mapped before us and even know where the monsters sleep."
Lian thought for a few seconds, a new area meant a chance for the title of Pioneer of Forgotten Realms to activate again.
Maybe a treasure, maybe new ruins, or creatures that no one had any information about yet.
In any case, he had no special reason to refuse, it was not like he had anything else to do, he had a full month of free time.
Only after that did he have to go to the Pendragon Family.
"It’s fine."
"Finally."
The young Vorhelm marked the route on World Memory and One changed its direction.
And they moved toward the last known point on the map.
The first hour passed mostly in silence.
After the base and most of the hunting groups disappeared behind them, Lian finally asked about something he had wanted to know since Kain returned.
"How is Base #3? Did anything special happen during this time?"
Kain thought for a moment.

"It depends on what you mean by special. New rankings were released, both for students and other Awakeneds. Groups have moved further forward, several new routes have become safe, and some hunting grounds have almost been completely emptied."
He shrugged.
"But if you’re looking for another disaster or strange attack, like during the siege, then no."
"Are Kael and his group still there?" The question of why the President had paid for his armor was still in his mind.
And no matter how he thought about it, he felt that it was connected to Kael.
"His group, yes." Kain gave him a short look.
"His group?" Lian noticed the pause.
"They are still active in Base #3. Actually, they are now one of the most well-known groups there, but Kael is no longer there."
"Where did he go?"
"From what I heard, he joined one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds."
This time, the young Vorhelm said nothing for a few seconds.
The Twelve Ancient Guilds.
It was not a name that Awakeneds were unaware of, they were not simply twelve large and wealthy Guilds.
Some normal Guilds had more members, and some companies even had more financial resources.
But the Twelve Ancient Guilds were different, each of them had a legacy that had been preserved for generations.
Their own training methods, resources that could not easily be found in the market, and information that was not always even available to governments.
They had existed since the first Ruined Realm, and it could be said that they were the first Guilds to be established.
Their position, influence, and power were almost higher than those of all modern Guilds, organizations, and governments.
And most importantly, joining them was not just signing a work contract.
Someone who truly entered the main level of one of those Guilds was basically entering a structure that had its own methods, rules, and legacy for raising its Awakeneds.
That was also why their member selection was very limited, talent was necessary, but it was not always enough.
Lian had once encountered someone from that environment directly.
When he had returned to the Vorhelm Family for his sister’s birthday, he had met one of the geniuses connected to one of those Twelve Guilds.
He did not expect Kael to eventually enter one of them as well.
"How did he get in? Is there any information about it?" He asked after some time.
Kain shrugged.
"I don’t know, I only heard that he left. No one explained the details to me."
Lian became silent again.
Kael was talented, that part was not strange, from the short time he had worked with his group, he had understood that Kael was not a thoughtless leader and his power was not low either.
But another question remained, why had he left his own group?
Or maybe he had not left it at all, it was possible that joining the new Guild had only caused him to stay away from Base #3 for some time.
And that old guess still existed.
That Kael might really be the President’s son, although he was quite sure about it, it was still unclear.
Lian had no definite proof, but if it was true, joining one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds could have a greater meaning.
Or maybe it had nothing to do with it, for now, he had too little information and he let the matter go.
Some time later, the old road entered a large plain.
One continued forward over the cracked stones without slowing down.
"One more thing, I heard that encounters with the natives of the Realm have increased during these months." Lian looked at the horizon.
Kain became a little more serious.
"They have. But most of what I know is just what I heard. I didn’t see them much around the routes where I hunted."
"What did you hear?"
He thought for a few moments to organize the information.

"There have been conflicts several times around routes and territories, sometimes they only saw each other and pulled back, sometimes it turned into a fight, and it is said that several Awakeneds have also gone missing."
"Gone missing?" Lian slightly turned his head.

"Yeah. It’s not clear if they died or not. One rumor says that some of them were captured alive, some people say they may have been taken to one of the Seven Regions for questioning, but it has not been confirmed. For now, it’s more hunter talk than an official report."
The Seven Regions.
The remaining civilizations of this world were not something the Federation could ignore forever.
Just as they could not ignore the presence of thousands of new humans from another world.
Both sides had reacted to each other’s presence, and it was not clear how long they could tolerate each other, and unfortunately, the relationship between the two sides was not good at all.
Both sides were strongly hostile toward each other, and it did not seem like either side had any interest in talking or becoming friends.
"Is it clear how the Federation wants to deal with this?"
Kain slightly pressed his lips together.

"No. At least, it isn’t clear from the news. It’s obvious that they are looking for information and probably don’t want to start a large war for no reason, but it’s also unclear what the other side thinks about us."
He was silent for a moment and then continued.

"It’s not like the Federation has little pressure either, right? They have this place. The rifts in the earth have also increased. And according to what is being shown in the news, it seems that the situation in the Heavenly Realm isn’t good either."
This time, Lian said nothing, the Heavenly Realm was still a very distant goal for him, he would only have the chance to enter it after reaching Level sixty.
He was only Level twenty-six himself.
Because of that, he did not have much reason or opportunity to follow all the news about that Realm.
But if things were also getting worse there, it was different.
Gareth’s words returned to his mind, the increasing number of rifts and the greater pressure on different areas of the earth.
Events that once seemed unrelated were now slowly coming together.
The Ruined Realm.
The Heavenly Realm.
The rifts.
The Calamities.
If the pressure on all these fronts increased at the same time, even a world with many powerful Awakeneds could not divide its resources endlessly.
He looked at the sky above them for a moment, he did not know why but he felt as if the pressure on their world was quickly reaching the highest known level.
"Anyway, how do we know? Maybe we’ll also run into the natives." Kain said after several minutes of silence.
"With our luck?" Lian gave him a short look.
"Then it’s confirmed." Kain laughed.
The first day of the journey passed without any major event.
The farther they moved from the base, the more signs of the old civilization appeared and the fewer Awakeneds they saw.
In the afternoon, they passed under a huge aqueduct whose stone arches stretched for hundreds of meters along the valley.
It had probably once carried water from the mountains to a distant city, now the upper channel was completely dry.
Black roots had come out of cracks in the stones and hung down from under the arches.
On one of the smaller bridges, a rotten carriage was still left in its place.
Beside it lay the bones of a large animal that had four legs, but its long skull and curved horns looked nothing like the horses of Earth.
Kain went down for a few minutes to examine it, but he found nothing valuable.
That night, they stopped in the upper part of the aqueduct.
During that first stop, he tested Ashen Thunder Step for the first time.
The movement began.
Boom!
His body moved forward several dozen meters with thunder, and at the end of the path, instead of stopping, his body turned into ash for a moment.
The flow of the movement broke and he formed again three meters to the right.
Lian immediately had to take one extra step to keep his balance.
He looked at the place where he intended to appear and the place where he had actually appeared for a few seconds.
The distance was less than half a meter, but the structure worked, his body simply had to get used to changing direction during the same movement.
On the second day, the land completely changed.
They entered an area of terraced gardens.

sentences.text: Lian checked the distance.
Even with One’s speed, it was not a short journey, and some parts of the road were so rough that they could not move at full speed the entire time.
"It’ll take two, maybe three days just to reach the last area that the people from the base have recorded."
"So?" Kain raised his head.
He looked at him, but before he could say anything, Kain continued.
"We’re not going to have a boring journey with this creature.
Besides, discovering a new area is much more interesting than going somewhere that a hundred people have already mapped before us and even know where the monsters sleep."
Lian thought for a few seconds, a new area meant a chance for the title of Pioneer of Forgotten Realms to activate again.
Maybe a treasure, maybe new ruins, or creatures that no one had any information about yet.
In any case, he had no special reason to refuse, it was not like he had anything else to do, he had a full month of free time.
Only after that did he have to go to the Pendragon Family.
"It’s fine."
"Finally."
The young Vorhelm marked the route on World Memory and One changed its direction.
And they moved toward the last known point on the map.
The first hour passed mostly in silence.
After the base and most of the hunting groups disappeared behind them, Lian finally asked about something he had wanted to know since Kain returned.
"How is Base #3?
Did anything special happen during this time?"
Kain thought for a moment.
"It depends on what you mean by special.
New rankings were released, both for students and other Awakeneds.
Groups have moved further forward, several new routes have become safe, and some hunting grounds have almost been completely emptied."
He shrugged.
"But if you’re looking for another disaster or strange attack, like during the siege, then no."
"Are Kael and his group still there?" The question of why the President had paid for his armor was still in his mind.
And no matter how he thought about it, he felt that it was connected to Kael.
"His group, yes." Kain gave him a short look.
"His group?" Lian noticed the pause.
"They are still active in Base #3.
Actually, they are now one of the most well-known groups there, but Kael is no longer there."
"Where did he go?"
"From what I heard, he joined one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds."
This time, the young Vorhelm said nothing for a few seconds.
The Twelve Ancient Guilds.
It was not a name that Awakeneds were unaware of, they were not simply twelve large and wealthy Guilds.
Some normal Guilds had more members, and some companies even had more financial resources.
But the Twelve Ancient Guilds were different, each of them had a legacy that had been preserved for generations.
Their own training methods, resources that could not easily be found in the market, and information that was not always even available to governments.
They had existed since the first Ruined Realm, and it could be said that they were the first Guilds to be established.
Their position, influence, and power were almost higher than those of all modern Guilds, organizations, and governments.
And most importantly, joining them was not just signing a work contract.
Someone who truly entered the main level of one of those Guilds was basically entering a structure that had its own methods, rules, and legacy for raising its Awakeneds.
That was also why their member selection was very limited, talent was necessary, but it was not always enough.
Lian had once encountered someone from that environment directly.
When he had returned to the Vorhelm Family for his sister’s birthday, he had met one of the geniuses connected to one of those Twelve Guilds.
He did not expect Kael to eventually enter one of them as well.
"How did he get in?
Is there any information about it?" He asked after some time.
Kain shrugged.
"I don’t know, I only heard that he left.
No one explained the details to me."
Lian became silent again.
Kael was talented, that part was not strange, from the short time he had worked with his group, he had understood that Kael was not a thoughtless leader and his power was not low either.
But another question remained, why had he left his own group?
Or maybe he had not left it at all, it was possible that joining the new Guild had only caused him to stay away from Base #3 for some time.
And that old guess still existed.
That Kael might really be the President’s son, although he was quite sure about it, it was still unclear.
Lian had no definite proof, but if it was true, joining one of the Twelve Ancient Guilds could have a greater meaning.
Or maybe it had nothing to do with it, for now, he had too little information and he let the matter go.
Some time later, the old road entered a large plain.
One continued forward over the cracked stones without slowing down.
"One more thing, I heard that encounters with the natives of the Realm have increased during these months." Lian looked at the horizon.
Kain became a little more serious.
"They have.
But most of what I know is just what I heard.
I didn’t see them much around the routes where I hunted."
"What did you hear?"
He thought for a few moments to organize the information.

"There have been conflicts several times around routes and territories, sometimes they only saw each other and pulled back, sometimes it turned into a fight, and it is said that several Awakeneds have also gone missing."
"Gone missing?" Lian slightly turned his head.
"Yeah.
It’s not clear if they died or not.
One rumor says that some of them were captured alive, some people say they may have been taken to one of the Seven Regions for questioning, but it has not been confirmed.
For now, it’s more hunter talk than an official report."
The Seven Regions.
The remaining civilizations of this world were not something the Federation could ignore forever.
Just as they could not ignore the presence of thousands of new humans from another world.
Both sides had reacted to each other’s presence, and it was not clear how long they could tolerate each other, and unfortunately, the relationship between the two sides was not good at all.
Both sides were strongly hostile toward each other, and it did not seem like either side had any interest in talking or becoming friends.
"Is it clear how the Federation wants to deal with this?"
Kain slightly pressed his lips together.
"No.
At least, it isn’t clear from the news.
It’s obvious that they are looking for information and probably don’t want to start a large war for no reason, but it’s also unclear what the other side thinks about us."
He was silent for a moment and then continued.
"It’s not like the Federation has little pressure either, right?
They have this place.
The rifts in the earth have also increased.
And according to what is being shown in the news, it seems that the situation in the Heavenly Realm isn’t good either."
This time, Lian said nothing, the Heavenly Realm was still a very distant goal for him, he would only have the chance to enter it after reaching Level sixty.
He was only Level twenty-six himself.
Because of that, he did not have much reason or opportunity to follow all the news about that Realm.
But if things were also getting worse there, it was different.
Gareth’s words returned to his mind, the increasing number of rifts and the greater pressure on different areas of the earth.
Events that once seemed unrelated were now slowly coming together.
The Ruined Realm.
The Heavenly Realm.
The rifts.
The Calamities.
If the pressure on all these fronts increased at the same time, even a world with many powerful Awakeneds could not divide its resources endlessly.
He looked at the sky above them for a moment, he did not know why but he felt as if the pressure on their world was quickly reaching the highest known level.
"Anyway, how do we know?
Maybe we’ll also run into the natives." Kain said after several minutes of silence.
"With our luck?" Lian gave him a short look.
"Then it’s confirmed." Kain laughed.
The first day of the journey passed without any major event.
The farther they moved from the base, the more signs of the old civilization appeared and the fewer Awakeneds they saw.
In the afternoon, they passed under a huge aqueduct whose stone arches stretched for hundreds of meters along the valley.
It had probably once carried water from the mountains to a distant city, now the upper channel was completely dry.
Black roots had come out of cracks in the stones and hung down from under the arches.
On one of the smaller bridges, a rotten carriage was still left in its place.
Beside it lay the bones of a large animal that had four legs, but its long skull and curved horns looked nothing like the horses of Earth.
Kain went down for a few minutes to examine it, but he found nothing valuable.

During that first stop, he tested Ashen Thunder Step for the first time.
The movement began.
Boom!
His body moved forward several dozen meters with thunder, and at the end of the path, instead of stopping, his body turned into ash for a moment.
The flow of the movement broke and he formed again three meters to the right.
Lian immediately had to take one extra step to keep his balance.

The distance was less than half a meter, but the structure worked, his body simply had to get used to changing direction during the same movement.
On the second day, the land completely changed.
They entered an area of terraced gardens.

chapters.title: Chapter 498: Our Luck Is Really Something ( PS Bonus - )
paragraphs: Hundreds of stone terraces had been built along the mountain slope, and thousands of fruit trees had probably once grown on them.
Now, most of the trees were dead.
Hollow trunks rose toward the sky like black hands.
But not everything was dead, small ponds between the terraces had been filled with rainwater, and plants with pale blue leaves had grown inside them.
As One passed by, the light of the plants shook on the surface of the water, it was beautiful despite being abandoned, and perhaps that was what made its beauty sad.
It was clear that people had truly lived here once, built gardens, shared the water between the terraces, and walked along the narrow paths between the trees.
And now, the only thing left from that life was the stones between which monsters wandered.
They encountered three groups of monsters that same day.
Lian did not interfere much.
Kain handled the first group, golden light gathered around his hands, and by using the narrow space between two walls, he did not let the monsters reach him at the same time.
One took the second group.
A heavy monster with thick skin struck its Natural Armor several times, but in the end, it fell under its jaws.
The young Vorhelm only blocked the path with ice when one of the creatures tried to escape.
The cores were also left for the giant ant.
[Monster core absorbed.]

It was still not enough, it seemed that absorbing cores had no end, even Lian’s guess of fifty had turned out to be wrong, and although it had absorbed hundreds of cores, it was still not enough to complete One’s evolution condition.
One’s dissatisfaction was completely clear through the Colony Link, and its master placed a hand on one of its antennae.
"I don’t know how many more you want either. Don’t look at me." This made a thought come to his mind.
Maybe this was why normal monsters preferred to eat humans and Awakeneds instead of absorbing the cores of their own kind.
Maybe eating humans was actually a shortcut that allowed them to complete their evolution condition faster.
"Are you talking to it?" Kain passed by them.
"It understands."
"Great. Now I dislike its name even more."
Lian did not answer.
A large part of the third day passed without any fights, the World Memory showed several old roads that practically no longer existed.
One had been buried under a mountain slide, and another passed through a forest that had completely swallowed the path over the centuries.
In the end, they had to take a longer route along the mountain slope.
And near the afternoon, they saw the first lantern.
"What is that?"
The young Vorhelm looked ahead, a stone statue was standing at the edge of the path.
It was taller than a human, and both hands of the statue were holding something like a huge lantern.
The lantern was unlit, and several hundred meters ahead stood a second statue, then a third, and a line of statues continued along the road.
Some were still intact, while some had no heads.
One was broken and had fallen to the ground, but its hands were still locked around the stone lantern.
Lian opened the map, and the last record from the base was located around this area.
[Pass of the Extinguished Lanterns.]
They moved for a few more minutes, and then the main view appeared.
Two huge mountain walls rose on both sides of a very deep valley.
A stone bridge stretched between them, the bridge was wide enough for several carts to pass beside each other at the same time.
Both sides of the path were covered with statues holding lanterns.
Nothing could be seen under the bridge except fog, thick gray fog that had completely swallowed everything hundreds of meters below the edges.
On the other side of the bridge, the remains of a huge gate stood, and one of its towers had collapsed while the other half was still standing on the cliff.
And behind it, a wide plain disappeared into the fog.
He looked at the map, the line of new information from the base ended exactly there, while the World Memory still showed several old roads on the other side of the pass.
From this point onward, their map came to an end and lost all its usefulness, and unfortunately, the World Memory was also useless without a usable map.
And this was not good news at all because they had to continue the rest of the path without a map.
"I think we made it." Kain smiled.
"Almost." Lian was still looking at the map.
Near the entrance of the bridge, a camp could be seen, several tents, carts, and marked hunter flags with a small defensive array around them.
It was clear that groups of Awakeneds were using this place as a stopping point before advancing farther.
But a few seconds later, the young Vorhelm noticed something.
Smoke.
The problem was that there was too much of it, and it looked darker than the smoke from a cooking fire.
His eyes narrowed slightly.
"Kain."
"I saw it."
One slowed down without needing an order, and it was not long before the sound of the first explosion came.
BOOOOOOM!
A light passed beside the bridge and hit the outer layer of the camp’s defensive array.
The defensive layer shook and one part of it went out for a moment, at the same time, a scream was heard.
Lian leaned slightly forward from One’s back, and as they got closer, the scene became clearer, several Awakeneds had taken positions behind an overturned cart.
One of them had fallen to the ground and blood was coming from his thigh, while two others were trying to pull him back.
On another part of the bridge, three Awakeneds were fighting a group of attackers.
But they were not monsters ...they were humans!
They were wearing armor with different designs.
Dark metal, long pieces of cloth, engraved shoulder guards, and weapons that had nothing in common with the usual equipment of Earth’s Awakeneds.
One of them also held a long spear with Mana lines running along its body, their movements were not disorganized, they had a formation.
Two people in front and archers or something similar behind them, while another person was giving orders from a distance.
They looked nothing like the people from their world, so there could only be one meaning ...the natives of the Ruined Realm.
Lian checked the entire battlefield for a moment, there was no way to know who had started the fight.
It was possible that the Awakeneds had entered a forbidden area, or it was possible that the other group had attacked them.
There could be another reason between them.
But for now, several Awakeneds were injured, the camp’s defensive array was close to breaking, and the battle was still continuing.
One stopped at the top of the slope, and Kain slowly got down from its back, took a battle stance, and pale light formed between his fingers.
Just a short while ago, he had said that they might encounter the natives of this world themselves, and now it had happened ...
Lian did not jump down and first moved his eyes from the camp to the native warriors, then to the escape routes, the injured, the enemy formation, and finally to his friend.
The corner of his lips rose slightly.
"There you go, I told you, with our luck, meeting them was only a matter of time."

chapters.title: Chapter 499: The Thief They Were Looking For
paragraphs: Kain stared at the scene in front of them for a few seconds.
The sound of metal hitting metal, Mana explosions, and the screams of the injured reached the top of the slope.
The temporary defensive array around the camp had cracks in several places, and its light became weaker for a moment every time an attack hit it.
"I didn’t mean that we would find them right in the middle of a battle." He said with a slight frown.
Down in the pass, around fourteen native humans were fighting the Awakeneds.
Their movements also did not look like those of a random group of hunters, they were organized.
Three people were pushing the front line, several others were moving from both sides, and the archers were creating opportunities for the others to get closer to the camp from behind.
Since it was impossible to see their Level just because they were humans, but from their aura and presence, it was unlikely that they were above Level 30.
Although there were also two stronger presences, along with a man who seemed to be the leader of the group and might be Level 30.
For the groups of Awakeneds that worked in this area, they were not a small force.
The result of the battle also showed this.
One of the Awakeneds had fallen onto his knee and was pressing a hand against his bloody side.
Another man was trying to pull him behind an overturned cart, while two natives were approaching from the side with spears.
A little farther away, the wall of the array shook again.
BOOM!
A crack of light appeared on its surface.
One of the native warriors passed through the crack and brought his sword down toward an Awakened who was standing behind it.
There was no attempt to negotiate, and neither side seemed to have any intention of retreating.
The young Vorhelm watched for only a few more seconds.
"Let’s go."
One moved almost at the same moment.
The ant’s six huge legs struck the ground, and every step lifted a mass of dirt and small stones behind them.
Several Earth Awakeneds quickly noticed the huge creature coming down the slope.
Their first reaction was fear, one of them even pointed his weapon at One, but when he saw Lian and Kain on its back, he lowered his hand.
After seeing which direction they had come from and Kain’s equipment, it was clear that they were not enemies.
The natives also noticed their presence.
Two of them turned their heads for a moment, but the battle did not allow them to focus for any longer.
The Child Of Light jumped off its back before One completely reached the camp.
Golden-white light gathered around his right palm.
At the same moment, one of the native warriors threw his spear toward an injured Awakened who no longer had a chance to dodge.
He moved his hand, and a line of light passed between his fingers.
Clang!
The light attack hit the body of the spear directly, knocking the weapon off course in the air, and it fell into the ground several meters away.
The injured Awakened looked at Kain with wide eyes.
"Move!" He shouted loudly, and without waiting for an answer, he gathered the light around both of his hands again.
The native attacker who had thrown the spear ran directly toward him.
Kain held out his palm.
BOOM!
A compressed wave of light hit the man’s chest and sent him several meters backward.
The armor on the front of his chest cracked, but at that exact moment, one of the natives standing a little farther behind became completely still.
It was as if he had seen something impossible!
His eyes were not on Kain, but on the light around his hands, and for several seconds, the man even forgot about the battle around him.
His pupils narrowed.
"That light..."
Another warrior who was wearing longer clothes under his armor heard him.
He turned his head and looked at Kain for a moment, then his expression changed.
"Wait!"
His voice passed through the screams of the battlefield, and several members of the group instinctively looked at him.
The man took one step forward and stared more carefully at the light around Kain’s hands.
"Don’t kill him!"
"What did you see?" The leader of the group, who seemed to be the strongest native present, immediately turned toward him.
"The light of that foreign barbarian... it has the mark of the Divine of Light!" The man still seemed unable to believe what he was seeing.
The commander frowned, as if he could not understand how a foreigner could use light power that contained a mark of their goddess.
How could something like this even be possible?

But suddenly he thought of something, and his eyes widened slightly ...that’s right, there had been a report from an abandoned temple a few months ago that foreign barbarians had managed to steal their goddess’s tear.
"Could this barbarian... be the same thief?" He whispered.
Lian, who had just gotten down from One’s back, calmly fixed his eyes on the man’s face.
Thief?
He was also a little surprised, what exactly was different about the light Kain was using compared to a normal user of the Light element?
Was this something that only worshippers of the Divine of Light could notice?
And it was not difficult to understand what they meant by the thief.
His mind quickly went back to several months ago, in the same ruin where he had saved Kain, there had been two natives as well.
He had captured one, but the other had escaped, and it was normal for him to report to the other people of his race that the Divine of Light’s tear had been absorbed by a foreigner.
The news that a foreigner had entered a ruined temple belonging to the Divine of Light and taken the tear would naturally not remain hidden.
The native commander’s eyes remained fixed on Kain for a moment, and then his decision was made.
"We want him alive! The others don’t matter!"
"This is the thief we’ve been looking for for a long time!"
The entire formation of the battlefield changed.
Three of the natives who had been fighting the other Awakeneds immediately pulled back and turned toward Kain, while two others moved from the side.
A man also took something out from his belt.
Black rings with thin chains hanging between them, and Mana marks moved across their surfaces.
At first glance, they seemed to be some kind of restraint tool.
Kain condensed the light around both of his hands and gave Lian a quick look.
"I think they want me."
"Obviously, they seem to have realized that you’re the one who stole their god’s tear."
"Hey! I didn’t steal anything, their own god chose me, how is that my fault?"
The young Vorhelm ignored him, it was better to end this situation as soon as possible.
The first native attacked, and his speed was not bad for his Level, he closed the distance in only a few steps, and the hand holding the restraint ring went directly toward Kain.
But Lian appeared between them, without using any skill and only using his raw speed.
The attacker did not even understand when he had moved from several meters away to directly in front of him.
The young Vorhelm’s hand closed around his wrist, and the man tried to pull his hand back ... but it did not move.
He twisted his wrist, and the attacker’s body was forced to twist with the movement, his foot left the ground and ...BOOM!
His face hit the stone.
Lian immediately touched the back of his neck with his other hand, one short and controlled pressure, and the man’s body went limp and fell unconscious on the ground.
The natives looked at each other when they saw this scene and swallowed.
One of them had been knocked out this easily ...?
At the same time, a second one came from the left and swung his sword in a precise path toward Lian’s neck... but he only moved his head a few centimeters to the side.
The edge of the blade passed beside his skin, the attacker’s eyes widened for a moment, and before he had a chance to react, the young Vorhelm’s fist hit his stomach.
Of course, he did not use all of his raw strength, if he really hit with all his power, there would be no one left to interrogate.
THUD!
The air left the man’s lungs, his mouth opened, his feet lifted from the ground, and when he came down again ...he was no longer conscious.
The third attacker immediately attacked, but he kept his distance and threw a short spear toward Lian.
It had good speed.
But he raised his hand.
Clang.
The spear stopped in his hand.
The Awakeneds around them forgot about their own fights for a moment.
Lian looked at the weapon in his hand, then held it from the opposite end and threw it.
The native man instinctively pulled his body backward, but the spear did not hit him.
BOOM!
It struck the stone right beside his foot.
More than half of the shaft disappeared into the ground, and the man stared at it for a moment.

sentences.text: Kain stared at the scene in front of them for a few seconds.
The sound of metal hitting metal, Mana explosions, and the screams of the injured reached the top of the slope.
The temporary defensive array around the camp had cracks in several places, and its light became weaker for a moment every time an attack hit it.
"I didn’t mean that we would find them right in the middle of a battle." He said with a slight frown.
Down in the pass, around fourteen native humans were fighting the Awakeneds.
Their movements also did not look like those of a random group of hunters, they were organized.
Three people were pushing the front line, several others were moving from both sides, and the archers were creating opportunities for the others to get closer to the camp from behind.
Since it was impossible to see their Level just because they were humans, but from their aura and presence, it was unlikely that they were above Level 30.
Although there were also two stronger presences, along with a man who seemed to be the leader of the group and might be Level 30.
For the groups of Awakeneds that worked in this area, they were not a small force.
The result of the battle also showed this.
One of the Awakeneds had fallen onto his knee and was pressing a hand against his bloody side.
Another man was trying to pull him behind an overturned cart, while two natives were approaching from the side with spears.
A little farther away, the wall of the array shook again.
BOOM!
A crack of light appeared on its surface.
One of the native warriors passed through the crack and brought his sword down toward an Awakened who was standing behind it.
There was no attempt to negotiate, and neither side seemed to have any intention of retreating.
The young Vorhelm watched for only a few more seconds.
"Let’s go."
One moved almost at the same moment.
The ant’s six huge legs struck the ground, and every step lifted a mass of dirt and small stones behind them.
Several Earth Awakeneds quickly noticed the huge creature coming down the slope.
Their first reaction was fear, one of them even pointed his weapon at One, but when he saw Lian and Kain on its back, he lowered his hand.
After seeing which direction they had come from and Kain’s equipment, it was clear that they were not enemies.
The natives also noticed their presence.
Two of them turned their heads for a moment, but the battle did not allow them to focus for any longer.
The Child Of Light jumped off its back before One completely reached the camp.
Golden-white light gathered around his right palm.
At the same moment, one of the native warriors threw his spear toward an injured Awakened who no longer had a chance to dodge.
He moved his hand, and a line of light passed between his fingers.
Clang!
The light attack hit the body of the spear directly, knocking the weapon off course in the air, and it fell into the ground several meters away.
The injured Awakened looked at Kain with wide eyes.
"Move!" He shouted loudly, and without waiting for an answer, he gathered the light around both of his hands again.
The native attacker who had thrown the spear ran directly toward him.
Kain held out his palm.
BOOM!
A compressed wave of light hit the man’s chest and sent him several meters backward.
The armor on the front of his chest cracked, but at that exact moment, one of the natives standing a little farther behind became completely still.
It was as if he had seen something impossible!
His eyes were not on Kain, but on the light around his hands, and for several seconds, the man even forgot about the battle around him.
His pupils narrowed.
"That light..."
Another warrior who was wearing longer clothes under his armor heard him.
He turned his head and looked at Kain for a moment, then his expression changed.
"Wait!"
His voice passed through the screams of the battlefield, and several members of the group instinctively looked at him.
The man took one step forward and stared more carefully at the light around Kain’s hands.
"Don’t kill him!"
"What did you see?" The leader of the group, who seemed to be the strongest native present, immediately turned toward him.
"The light of that foreign barbarian... it has the mark of the Divine of Light!" The man still seemed unable to believe what he was seeing.
The commander frowned, as if he could not understand how a foreigner could use light power that contained a mark of their goddess.
How could something like this even be possible?

But suddenly he thought of something, and his eyes widened slightly ...that’s right, there had been a report from an abandoned temple a few months ago that foreign barbarians had managed to steal their goddess’s tear.
"Could this barbarian... be the same thief?" He whispered.
Lian, who had just gotten down from One’s back, calmly fixed his eyes on the man’s face.
Thief?
He was also a little surprised, what exactly was different about the light Kain was using compared to a normal user of the Light element?
Was this something that only worshippers of the Divine of Light could notice?
And it was not difficult to understand what they meant by the thief.
His mind quickly went back to several months ago, in the same ruin where he had saved Kain, there had been two natives as well.
He had captured one, but the other had escaped, and it was normal for him to report to the other people of his race that the Divine of Light’s tear had been absorbed by a foreigner.
The news that a foreigner had entered a ruined temple belonging to the Divine of Light and taken the tear would naturally not remain hidden.
The native commander’s eyes remained fixed on Kain for a moment, and then his decision was made.
"We want him alive!
The others don’t matter!"
"This is the thief we’ve been looking for for a long time!"
The entire formation of the battlefield changed.
Three of the natives who had been fighting the other Awakeneds immediately pulled back and turned toward Kain, while two others moved from the side.
A man also took something out from his belt.
Black rings with thin chains hanging between them, and Mana marks moved across their surfaces.
At first glance, they seemed to be some kind of restraint tool.
Kain condensed the light around both of his hands and gave Lian a quick look.
"I think they want me."
"Obviously, they seem to have realized that you’re the one who stole their god’s tear."
"Hey!
I didn’t steal anything, their own god chose me, how is that my fault?"
The young Vorhelm ignored him, it was better to end this situation as soon as possible.
The first native attacked, and his speed was not bad for his Level, he closed the distance in only a few steps, and the hand holding the restraint ring went directly toward Kain.
But Lian appeared between them, without using any skill and only using his raw speed.
The attacker did not even understand when he had moved from several meters away to directly in front of him.
The young Vorhelm’s hand closed around his wrist, and the man tried to pull his hand back ... but it did not move.
He twisted his wrist, and the attacker’s body was forced to twist with the movement, his foot left the ground and ...BOOM!
His face hit the stone.
Lian immediately touched the back of his neck with his other hand, one short and controlled pressure, and the man’s body went limp and fell unconscious on the ground.
The natives looked at each other when they saw this scene and swallowed.
One of them had been knocked out this easily ...?
At the same time, a second one came from the left and swung his sword in a precise path toward Lian’s neck... but he only moved his head a few centimeters to the side.

chapters.title: Chapter 500: Third Region... Again
paragraphs: Lian’s attention, however, fell on the strongest native present.
The native commander had finally understood what had happened.
Eight of his people were on the ground, while two others had been injured by the Awakeneds from the camp.
And the human who had taken most of them out of the battle had not even changed his breathing.
The commander was not stupid, his eyes moved to Lian once, then to Kain, the possible carrier of the Divine of Light’s tear.
If they stayed here, not only would they be unable to capture him, but there was also a high chance that no one would return to deliver the news.
He made his decision.
"Retreat!"
The remaining people immediately moved.
"Send the news! He’s here!" The commander shouted in a louder voice.
Two people ran toward the eastern side of the bridge, one went down the path toward the pass, and the commander chose another path as well.
He did not even look at his unconscious people.
Delivering the news was more important, for greater goals, small sacrifices were not a problem.

"Looks like leaving your friends behind is some kind of tradition." Lian tilted his head slightly and laughed, back in the ruined temple of the Divine of Light, one of the natives had also abandoned his friend and escaped.
And now the other natives had done the same thing, and by leaving their friends behind, they wanted to escape, of course, their decision was not completely wrong either.
They had understood that they had to deliver the news to the rest of their people no matter what.
But unfortunately for them, this time they were not going to escape, the young Vorhelm’s foot stayed firmly on the stone and the air around him became cold for a moment.
[Frost Dominion.]
KRRRRRRRRRK!
Ice came out from the cracks in the stone pavement.
First, it moved toward the right side of the bridge and a thick wall grew within a few seconds, blocking the path of the two escaping people.
One of them tried to jump over the wall, but the ice grew right under his hand and locked his palm in place, then the ice wrapped around his wrist.
His legs.
His knees.
The man was trapped in the same position.
The second escapee turned and moved toward the side, although ice came out from under his feet like teeth and covered both of his lower legs.
"Damn it!"
On the other side, the commander had almost reached the gate, but the stone surface in front of him turned white, a line of ice moved ahead of his steps.
Then several pillars rose and completely blocked the path, the man stopped and looked behind him.
"You’re not going anywhere." Lian calmly walked between the unconscious people.
For several seconds, no one moved, the natives had now realized ...this battle was over.
The young Vorhelm did not let the Earth Awakeneds kill the unconscious people, not because he was worried about them, but because dead people could not answer questions.
Ice caught the hands and feet of the conscious people, and the remaining natives faced the same situation after they woke up.

One slowly came forward from behind the camp, several of the prisoners’ expressions changed when they saw it, even in a world where seeing monsters was normal, a giant ant of that size, with those jaws and Natural Armor, was not a calming sight.
Lian sent a simple command through the Colony Link.
Be scary.
One sent something like confusion for a moment, then it seemed to understand the meaning and lowered its huge body.
Its head moved close to one of the prisoners, its jaws slowly opened.
The distance between those hard teeth was large enough for a human head to easily fit between them.
The native man did not take his eyes off One.
CLACK!
The jaws closed right beside his face, the air created by them moved the man’s hair.
The giant ant then placed one of its front legs on a large stone.
CRACK!
The stone cracked under its foot, the pressure increased and the stone was completely crushed.
Lian stood beside One.
"Don’t worry, as long as you don’t force me to guess the answers to my questions myself, you won’t be its next meal."
One of the natives spat at his foot with hatred.
"Barbarian thieves!... You think you can scare us with a monster!?"
Lian looked at the spit on the ground, then raised his head...although there was no anger on his face.
Before he could ask another question, a voice came from behind.
"You two came from Base #9?"
He turned around.
A man around thirty years old was approaching with cracked armor. There was a deep cut on his forehead, and his left hand was wrapped in cloth.
He was probably the person currently leading the camp, his eyes kept moving between Lian, Kain, and One.
He still could not fully believe what he had seen.
"Is this the first time they have attacked you?" Lian asked instead of introducing himself.
"No, it has been going on for a while now." The man paused for a moment.
"Oh? How long?"
"Three days. Maybe almost four days."
"Were you here from the beginning?" Lian looked toward the pass.

"Yeah. This is the last forward camp. Several groups passed through here before and went a few kilometers farther, but for the last three or four days, these natives have not let us advance because of their attacks."
Kain came closer, and the man continued.
"Every time we send a group, these bastards appear. One time there were eight of them, another time there were almost twenty, and today there were these guys."
"Always the same number?" The young Vorhelm asked after thinking for a moment.
"No, but there isn’t much difference."
"Did they follow you back to the base or the camps farther behind?"
"Never." The man shook his head.
"Did they try to take this place?"
"No."
"Take your supplies or equipment?"
"No."
"When they had the advantage, did they kill everyone?"
This time the man did not answer immediately, as if he had never thought about this himself before.
"Now that I think about it ...no."
His frown became deeper, as if he was only now putting together the behavior of the last few days.

"Sometimes they could have pushed harder. Especially on the first day, several of us were injured and the front line had completely collapsed, but after they destroyed the equipment we used to check the path, they pulled back."
"How many died?" Lian asked.
"Two people over these few days, we had more injured."
Two people.
No number of deaths could be ignored and called small, lives were valuable, but considering the strength of these groups and the chances they seemed to have, it could have been much more.
The man continued.
"They do the same thing every time. They hurt a few people, destroy the equipment, stop the group from moving forward, and then disappear."
Lian asked nothing else, his eyes moved toward the other side of the pass, he had some guesses.
The way the natives attacked made it clear that their goal was not only to kill, they only wanted to stop the outsiders from moving forward.
The first explanation was simple.
One of the seven Regions of the natives might be located nearby.
If the Earth Awakeneds continued moving forward more every day, it was logical that the people living in that area would not want to let groups of outsiders get too close.
But something did not make sense.
He had limited information about the seven Regions, but he knew one thing.
They had survived in this world for centuries, a world where most of its civilizations had been destroyed under attacks from monsters and demons.
The defensive structures of those regions were so powerful that even demons had not been able to enter them.
So what threat could a few Level twenty and thirty Awakeneds be?
If one of the Regions was really nearby, it was unlikely that they would worry about a few hunters from Earth suddenly entering their city.
Entering such a place was probably almost impossible without permission.
There was another problem as well, if this pass was truly an important border, the behavior of the natives made no sense.
They should have stationed forces, built a fortress, completely blocked the road, or at worst destroyed the forward camp and pushed the Earth Awakeneds dozens of kilometers back.
But they had done none of those things.
They came, caused casualties, destroyed the equipment used for advancing, and then pulled back.
Why?
Lian looked at the burned tents for a few seconds.
The answer slowly took shape, if these natives killed fifty Awakeneds, what would happen?
Base #9 would send a larger group, if that group was also destroyed, the situation would no longer be a small border conflict.
The Federation would get involved.
And eventually, much more powerful Awakeneds would be sent, people who, like him, could kill all fourteen of these natives with one move.
So the natives did not want to make the war bigger, but at the same time, they did not want anyone to move farther forward.
That meant their goal was not to permanently protect the pass, they were buying time, for a few days and maybe a week, until something on the other side of the pass was finished.
"So they’re just keeping us here..." He frowned slightly.
"What do you mean? Why would they need to keep us here?" Kain, who was standing beside him, looked at him.
Lian looked at the broken gate on the other side of the bridge, behind it was the fog and the place where the map’s information ended.
"That is what I want to find out." Then his eyes returned to the prisoners, in fact, there was no reason to spend a long time guessing, they were still alive and he could simply ask them.
He turned toward the prisoners, but before asking the question, something else came together in his mind.
Their reaction to Kain.
An ordinary person could not understand from seeing the light for a few seconds that there was something different about its source.

Even if Lian did not know Kain’s story, he would probably only see it as a Light-based talent, and even then, he himself could not notice any difference in the Light power his friend was using right now.
But these people immediately understood that difference and connected it to the report about the ruin and the stolen Divine’s tear.
So either they had special training about all the Divines, or they came from a place where such knowledge was a normal part of the knowledge of its important forces.
Among the seven Regions, one option made more sense than the others.
The Third Region, which worshipped the Divine of Light, so if his guess was correct, these people were from the Third Region.
’Now that I think about it, I seem to be running into the Third Region too often.’ He thought to himself and laughed, it could not be a coincidence, right?
Lian stopped in front of the prisoners and his eyes passed over all of their faces once.
"You’re from the Third Region, right?"
No one answered, but one of the younger men looked at the commander for only a moment, it was very short, but the young Vorhelm saw it.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"Thank you, so you really are from the Third Region."

So the natives did not want to make the war bigger, but at the same time, they did not want anyone to move farther forward.
That meant their goal was not to permanently protect the pass, they were buying time, for a few days and maybe a week, until something on the other side of the pass was finished.
"So they’re just keeping us here..." He frowned slightly.
"What do you mean?
Why would they need to keep us here?" Kain, who was standing beside him, looked at him.
Lian looked at the broken gate on the other side of the bridge, behind it was the fog and the place where the map’s information ended.
"That is what I want to find out." Then his eyes returned to the prisoners, in fact, there was no reason to spend a long time guessing, they were still alive and he could simply ask them.
He turned toward the prisoners, but before asking the question, something else came together in his mind.
Their reaction to Kain.
An ordinary person could not understand from seeing the light for a few seconds that there was something different about its source.

Even if Lian did not know Kain’s story, he would probably only see it as a Light-based talent, and even then, he himself could not notice any difference in the Light power his friend was using right now.
But these people immediately understood that difference and connected it to the report about the ruin and the stolen Divine’s tear.
So either they had special training about all the Divines, or they came from a place where such knowledge was a normal part of the knowledge of its important forces.
Among the seven Regions, one option made more sense than the others.
The Third Region, which worshipped the Divine of Light, so if his guess was correct, these people were from the Third Region.
’Now that I think about it, I seem to be running into the Third Region too often.’ He thought to himself and laughed, it could not be a coincidence, right?
Lian stopped in front of the prisoners and his eyes passed over all of their faces once.
"You’re from the Third Region, right?"
No one answered, but one of the younger men looked at the commander for only a moment, it was very short, but the young Vorhelm saw it.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"Thank you, so you really are from the Third Region."
